case_summary.text: GST : Where applicant is awarded a contract with Railways for construction of new building of railway station, new constructions involved in contract are taxable at 12 per cent GST as per Entry No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017
12% GST leviable on contract for construction of new building of railway station

GST : Construction of railway station, buildings, parking area, roads, pavement and other civil constructions within station boundary on land owned by city development authority under a tripartite agreement with it and Smart City Corporation, is an original work as defined under Para 2(zs) of Notification No. 12/2017- CT(R) and hence, covered under SAC 9954 21; however, same being done purely on commercial basis and not being directly related to railways; cannot be treated as pertaining to Railways; activity would be taxable at rate of 18 per cent GST instead of 12 per cent

GST : Supply of goods and services for construction of railway infrastructure facilities for feeder line of Rail Corridor owned by South Eastern Coalfield Limited for evacuation of coal, under contract awarded by RITES, a PSU, is specifically covered under SAC 9954 21 and same is considered to be an original work pertaining to Railways and a composite supply in terms of section 2(30); therefore, such supply would attract 12 per cent GST subject to condition that it satisfies definition of works contract under section 2(119), otherwise it would be taxable at rate of 18 per cent GST

GST : Where petitioner, a joint venture formed for executing railway projects, was assigned a works contract by RVNL for various railway infrastructure developments and it paid GST at 12% under Serial No.3(v)(a) of Notification No.11/2017, but was later issued a demand for an 18% tax rate by revenue, expression "pertaining to" in said notification has a wide import,

GST : Composite supply of works contract services provided by respondent company by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works pertaining to railways as sub-contractor to main contractor would be covered under item (v) of Sr. 3, describing construction services, under Notification No. 11/2017 dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018 dated 25-1-2018, which provides for concessional rate of 12 per cent GST on composite supply of works contract

GST : Supply of works contract services of construction for Indian Railways either as a main contractor or in capacity of a sub-contractor through main contractor, is covered under entry at Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) and GST is payable at 18 per cent

GST : Supply of works contract services of construction for Indian Railways either as a main contractor or incapacity of a sub-contractor through main contractor, is covered under entry at S. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT(R) and GST is payable at 18%

GST : Construction of new railway siding is 'works contract' and also qualifies to be 'original works' pertaining to railways; same is taxable at rate of 12 per cent under Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 till its omission

GST : Where applicant is awarded a contract with Railways for repair work, addition and alteration of existing structure, other repair works of old construction involved in contract are liable to tax at 18 per cent as per Entry No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017
18% GST is leviable on supply of works contract services of construction to Indian Railways: AAR
18% GST leviable on construction of CBD railway station, commercial buildings, foot over bridge, parking area etc.: AAR
Original works contract pertaining to railways whether provided by main-contractor or sub-contractor attracts 12% GST

GST : Where works were undertaken for Indian government enterprise for railways namely, RITES qualifies as original work pertaining to railways, GST at 12 per cent will be available if said work qualifies as composite supply of works contract

GST : Construction of new railway siding is 'works contract' and also qualifies to be 'original works' pertaining to railways; taxable at rate of 12 per cent under Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 till omission of said entry vide Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022

GST : Works Contract Services by way of repairing/renovation and other improvements for railway track would be leviable to GST at rate of 18 percent, as stipulated by Serial number 3 [S.No. (xii)] of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

GST : Sub-contractor providing works contract services by way of construction, erection, commissioning, or installation to main contractor in respect of original contract works pertaining to railways would be covered for concessional rate of GST at rate of 12 per cent
GST : Works contract service by way of repairing/renovation and other improvements for railway track would be leviable to GST at rate of 18 per cent
Construction of pavement, track work, warehouse, etc., for an undertaking owned by Railways is taxable at 18%
Construction of new railway siding is ‘works contract' and taxable at 12% under GST: AAR

GST : Where assessee, a joint venture formed for executing railway projects, was assigned a works contract by RVNL for various railway infrastructure developments and assessee had paid 12 per cent GST on execution under Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No.11/2017, but later on a demand notice was issued for levying 18 per cent GST, since assessee’s contract was clearly related to railway development, and infrastructure projects so executed were aiding railway operations, even if carried out by a subsidiary like RVNL, same would still constitute original work pertaining to railway for purpose of subject notification and, thus, be covered under Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of said notification; assessee’s activity would be eligible for concessional rate of GST

GST : Where applicant, a Government Entity, is supplying works contract services to South Central Railways under General Construction service for long-distance underground/overland/submarine pipe lines, communication and electric power lines (cables) and it engaged a private turnkey contractor on a back to back arrangement to execute contract for South Central Railways, supply of services by applicant to South Central Railways is taxable at rate of 18 per cent as per Entry at Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

GST : Where applicant sub-contractor was executing works contract like supply of goods or services or both pertaining to Railways based on an order received from main contractor who got work order directly from Railways, such contract work of applicant to main contractor was covered under entry 3(v) of Notification no. 11/207-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28.6.2017 as amended by notification no. 20/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 22.8.2017 and was liable to tax at rate at 12 per cent (6 per cent under
Works contract pertaining to railways provided by sub-contractor to main-contractor attracts 12% GST
Supply of works contract services to South Central Railway shall be taxable at 18% under GST: AAAR
GST : Sub-contractor undertaking works contract relating to construction of pavement, track work, etc., pertaining to High Speed Rail Project is entitled to concessional GST rate of 12 per cent

GST: Construction of a private railway siding for carriage of coal and oil fuel to thermal power station by applicant project management consultant in terms of agreement with Region Development Corporation is a composite supply of works contract taxable at rate of 12 percent under Serial No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017
CGST: Works contract service of maintaining existing railway tracks is a composite supply of labour and goods and is taxable at rate of 18 per cent

GST/WBGST : Construction of a private railway siding for carriage of coal and oil fuel to a thermal power station by applicant, a project management consultant in terms of agreement with region development corporation is a composite supply of works contract taxable @ 12% under Serial No 3(v)(a) of Notification no 11/2017-CT(Rate) dated 28.06.2017

GST : For supply of works contract awarded by Government, tax rate applicable is 12 per cent GST and sub contracts, if any, awarded will also attract 12 per cent GST but supply of work contract awarded by a company for construction of Biotech lab and administrative block at Life Science Park attracts 18 per cent GST

GST: Sub-contractor providing services of composite supply of works contract in respect of original works pertaining to railways would be covered for concessional rate of GST at rate of 12 per cent as given under Serial No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 as amended

GST : Where applicant is awarded a contract with Railways for repair work, addition and alteration of existing structure, services of repair, maintenance, renovation of residential complex meant for use of railway employees are covered under Entry No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and are taxable at 12 per cent GST

GST: Works contract service provided by applicant to National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS) for construction of hostel building on campus is taxable at 18 per cent GST under residual item no. (xii) of Serial No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017

CGST : Works contract service, as defined under section 2(119) of GST Act, of maintaining existing railway tracks, is taxable at rate of 18 per cent – It is, a 'Composite Supply' of labour and goods in nature of Works Contract, as defined under section 2(119) of GST Act, and is, therefore, classifiable under (ii) of column 3 [Description of Service] of Heading 9954 (Construction services)

GST : Concessional GST rate of 12 per cent is not applicable on works contract service of construction of IT towers for government entity as it is meant for commerce/industry; GST is payable at 18 per cent

GST : GST at 12 percent is not available on supply of repair and maintenance service in relation to railway tracks for Indian Railways as said supply is not in relation to immovable property and does not amount to original work, therfore GST is payable at 18percenton said composite supply
Works contract service pertaining to railways provided by sub-contractor to main contractor taxable at 12% GST

GST : Works contract services provided by applicant-assessee to KSTP by way of construction of roads and bridges is for use of general public, therefore, rate of tax for works contract services provided by applicant-assessee to Kerala State Transport Project (KSTP) by way of construction of roads and bridges for public use will be taxable at 128 per cent and thereafter, it is 18 per cent w.e.f 18-7-2022

GST : Supply of repair and maintenance service in relation to railway tracks for Indian Railways is not in relation to immovable property and hence, does not amount to original work; therefore, GST at 12 per cent is not available and GST is payable at 18 per cent on said composite supply

GST : Activity of applicant company for electrical cable supply and laying work of new underground cable for metro rail project was in nature of composite supply of works contract and same would be covered under Sr. No. 3, item no. (ii) of Notification No. 11/2017 dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018 dated 25-1-2018 and attract 18 per cent GST (9 per cent each of CGST and SGST)

GST : Where rate of GST on work contract awarded to assessee for redevelopment of carriageway, foothpath, vending zone covering ROW within ABD area of Aligarh Smart City, was enhanced from 12 per cent to 18 per cent vide Notification No. 03/2022-Central Tax (Rate) with effect from 18-7-2022, in view section 14, in cases where advance was received or invoices were raised before 18-7-2022, GST rate applicable would be 12 per cent and in cases where advance was received or invoices were raised after 18-7-2022, GST rate applicable would be 18 per cent

GST : Where applicant is responsible for providing services of commissioning and erection of rail tracks and goods necessary for said service is provided by client, service provided by applicant cannot be considered as a composite supply of works contract; said services would be classified under residuary category of Construction Services falling under Heading 9954 chargeable to GST at rate of 18 per cent

GST : Installation and erection of electric equipment/transmission lines by State transmission corporation for Railway with resultant civil structure used predominantly for business purpose are classifiable as 'Works Contract Service' under Heading No. 99542 and is taxable at 18 per cent

GST : Works contract services performed by assessee as per contracts awarded by M/s Kerela State film development corporation Ltd, a government authority to construct a cultural complex is in nature of construction of structure meant for predominantly use as a cultural establishment and is liable to GST at 12 percent as per Sl 3(vi)(b)of Notification 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate)

GST : Works contract services performed by assessee as per contracts awarded by Kerela State film development corporation Ltd, a government authority to construct a cultural complex is in nature of construction of structure meant predominantly for use as a cultural establishment and is liable to GST at 12 per cent as per Sl 3(vi)(b) of Notification 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate)
18% GST to be levied on supply of construction, civil works etc. including service of transportation, freight & insurance: AAR

GST : Applicant engaged in construction of commercial complex for Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation will be liable to pay GST at 18 per cent in light of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended ultimately by Notification No. 03/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022

GST : Where assessee was engaged in construction work for a public enterprise and from 1-1-2022, rate of GST was enhanced from 12 per cent to 18 per cent, enterprise was to be directed to pay difference of GST amount to assessee at 6 per cent

GST (MISC) : Where when petitioner works contractor had executed construction work, GST was charged at rate of 12 per cent on total value of work order, however, GST authority had fixed GST to be payable at rate of 18 per cent of total value of work order, since said issue of additional 6 per cent was still pending before National Rural Infrastructure Development Agency (NRIDA), authority was directed to hear petitioner-contractor and department and decide issue

GST : Works rendered by applicant-assessee to awarders will be taxable at 18% (CGST at 9% and SGST @ 9%), if time of supply of services falls between 1-7-2017 to 21-8-2017, however, if supply is made between 22-8-2017 to 17-7-2022, it will be taxable @ 12%

FACT: The applicant is contractor with railways and it has been awarded a contract with KSR Bengaluru City Railway Station and service buildings at Bangalore.

The contract includes new works, repair works, addition and alteration to existing structures.

The applicant states that the Railway is considering all service buildings as business/commerce establishments and rate charged is 18 per cent (even for original works) and works related to all welfare buildings (i.e., only colonies) are charged at 12 per cent.

The applicant is seeking advance ruling as regards applicability of GST rate for works contract services doing original works with Railways.

HELD: The applicant is executing two types of works wherein, in one set of work the applicant is executing works contract for construction of new buildings and in the second set of work, it is executing works contracts not involving new construction. The correspondence of the applicant with the Railways revealed that in Zonal Works, majority of the works, it is executing are like provision of compound wall to Railway properties, laying of tiles for buildings, plumbing with new pipelines, provisions of new GLR and OHT, Staff recreation like parks, new rain water harvesting structures, painting, renovation of old structures etc. The applicant has claimed before the Railway Authorities that these are all original works as they involve new asset creation or bringing life to unused structures of Railways and these come under the works contract services as per CGST Act. [Para 9]

The issue is basically divided into two categories. One that results in the new buildings and the other repair and reconstruction of the old structures. [Para 10]

To summarize, the entry at 3(v) do not specify the class of service provider to whom it applies. The entry is specific to the composite supply of works contract pertaining to railways including monorail and metro. This view is fortified by the justification of the recommendation of the Fitment Committee to the 25th GST Council meeting (available in Volume-2 of the Agenda) after which the downward revision of the rate was effected. In the case at hand, the applicant is entrusted with certain works of design, manufacture, installation and commissioning of the Telecommunication systems including signalling system by Siemens who has been awarded the entire work relating to signalling and Telecommunication under CMRL project Phase-1 and the works are composite supply of original work pertaining to railways and the only leg of the entry No. 3(v) of the Notification which has not been established is whether the works satisfies the definition of 'Works Contract' under section 2(119) for which sufficient documentary proof is not furnished. The applicant has expressed his inability to furnish the necessary documentation and have opined that the documents furnished is sufficient for pronouncing the ruling. Therefore, considering all the submissions and that the application is pending before this Authority for long, it would be appropriate to hold that the benefit of the entry at Sl. No. 3(v) will be applicable to the applicant subject to the works undertaken by them being 'Works Contract' as per section 2(119) of the Act and the applicable GST is at the rate of 12 per cent effective from 25-1-2018.

The rate of tax of 6 per cent CGST as per entry No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017 amended vide Notification No. 1/2018 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 effective from 25-1-2018 may be applicable to the applicant provided the works contracted and undertaken by them satisfies the definition of 'Works Contract' as defined in clause (119) of section 2. [Para 12]

Since the works related to railways network, the contract can be said to be pertaining to Railways. The term pertaining to Railways is more expansive and includes other establishments other than Indian Railways. Hence the contract is pertaining to Railways. [Para 4.8] There is no stipulation in Entry No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 that the contract must be executed to the Railways, but it is sufficient that it must be pertaining to Railways and the supplier and the recipient in each of the contract is immaterial. [Para 4.9]

Hence the subcontract work is covered under Entry No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended by Notification No. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017) and is liable to tax at 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST or 12 per cent IGST) with effect from 22-8-2017. [Para 4.10]

Ruling

The contract work of the applicant to the main contractor, who is executing the works contract to DFFCCIL, is liable to tax at 6 per cent under CGST Act and at 6 per cent under Karnataka GST Act or 12 per cent under IGST Act, 2017. The relevant entry is Entry No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended by Notification No. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017).

The date of application of the rate of tax of 12 per cent is from 22-8-2017. [Para 5]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Services provided by sub-contractor to main contractor pertaining to railways - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Applicant is providing works contract service as sub-contractor to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways - It executes and undertakes composite supply of works contract - Whether tax rate to be charged by applicant to main contractor would be at rate of 6 per cent of CGST and 6 per cent of SGST - Held, yes [Para 11] [In favour of assessee]GST: Where applicant is providing works contract service as sub-contractor to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways and it executes and undertakes composite supply of works contract, tax rate to be charged by applicant to main contractor would be at rate of 6 per cent of CGST and 6 per cent of SGST

FACT: The applicant is providing works contract service as sub-contractor to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways. It executes and undertakes composite supply of works contract.

It sought advance ruling on the following questions:

1.

What tax rate to be charged by the applicant to main contractor on works contract services pertaining to railways original works contract.

2.

Whether to charge tax rate of 12 per cent GST or 18 per cent GST.

The Authority for Advance Rulings ruled that

-

The tax rate to be charged by the applicant to the main contractor would be at the rate of 6 per cent of CGST and 6 per cent of SGST.

-

The tax rate to be charged would be 12 per cent.

On appeal to Appellate Authority for Advance Ruling by revenue:

HELD: There is no dispute that the services provided by the sub-contractor to its main contractor are composite supply of works contract. The main issue to decide is that the works contract services provided by the applicant are covered under item (v) of Sr. No. 3, describing the construction services, under the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by the Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 or otherwise. [Para 7]

The Authority for Advance Ruling has decided that the works contract services provided by the applicant as sub-contractor to its main contractor are squarely covered under item (v) of Sr. No. 3, describing the construction services, under the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by the Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018, which provides for the concessional rate of 12 per cent GST on the composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning, or installation of original works pertaining to railways, including monorail and metro. The Authority had agreed to the applicant's contention that the works contract services provided by it or part of the works contract entered between the main contractor and railways is same, because the services performed by it as well as property in goods, i.e., material used by it in the execution of the works contract are directly getting transferred to the railways in its entirety without any change, modification or alteration therein. Thus the composite supply of any works contract undertaken by the sub-contractor as per the agreement entered between the main contractor is pertaining exclusively to railways. Therefore, by virtue of this clause 'pertaining to the railways' of item (v) of Sr. No. 3, describing the construction services, under the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by the Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018, the composite supply of the sub-contractor, i.e., the applicant to its main contractor is squarely covered under this item which provides for concessional rate of 12 per cent GST to such services. [Para 8]

) dated 28-6-2017, has specified the rate of central tax to be levied on Intra State supply of services of description specified in column 3 of the table in the said Notification, falling under scheme of classification of services mentioned therein. The relevant clauses (v) as mentioned by the applicant in their favour, of the said Notification, as amended by Notfn No. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 22-10-2017. A plain reading of Sr. No. 3, clause (v) reveals that 'composite supply of WCS supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning, or installation of original works pertaining to, railways attracts a tax rate of 6 per cent each of CGST and SGST. The applicant has submitted that they have been sub-contracted by the main contractor to supply WCS and in turn the main contractor is supplying WCS to the railways. From the submissions made by the applicant it appears that the WCS provided by them is the same or a part of the main contract entered into between the main contractor and the railways. It also appears that works contract service is civil works performed by the sub-contractor for the railways and the property in goods (materials used in the supply of Works Contract Service) also gets transferred to the railways directly. In such a case as per the abovementioned clause (v) of Notification No. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 22-10-2017, the works contract service provided by the sub-contractor to the main contractor would be supply of works contract pertaining to railways and, therefore, chargeable to tax at the rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent of CGST and SGST each). However, the benefit of 12 per cent tax rate would be available to the applicant only if the Works Contract services provided by them are Composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning, or installation of original works pertaining to railways. Thus, in respect of Sr. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 dated 28-6-2017 as amended up till today, even the sub-contractor providing services of composite supply of works contract in respect of original works pertaining to railways would be covered for concessional rate of GST at the rate of 12 per cent as given under Sr. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 as amended referred above. [Para 5]

The tax rate to be charged by the sub-contractor to the main contractor would be at the rate of 6 per cent of CGST and SGST each, in the present case. The tax rate to be charged would be 12 per cent in the present case. [Para 6]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Execution of works of laying of track, pavement along track, construction of Admin building, Warehouse, Electrical Works and Fire-fighting works - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant has been awarded a contract by one R, which is a public sector undertaking, for execution of works of laying of track as per layout plan, pavement along track, construction of Admin building, Warehouse, Electrical works and Fire-fighting works, etc. - Contract is involving both supply of goods and services - Whether said work contract is covered under clause 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, - Held, no [Para 15] [In favour of revenue]GST : Where applicant has been awarded a contract by one R, which is a public sector undertaking, for execution of works of laying of track, pavement along track, construction of Admin building, Warehouse, Electrical works and Fire-fighting works, etc. and contract is involving both supply of goods and services, said contract is not covered under clause 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

FACT: The applicant has been awarded a contract by one Rites Limited, which is a Public Sector Undertaking. Said contract is awarded for execution of works of laying of track as per layout plan, pavement along the track, construction of Admin building, Warehouse, Electrical works and Fire-fighting works, etc. at Khodiyar Gandhinagar, Gujarat. Further contract is involving both supply of goods and services and is a composite supply in the nature of works contract supply.

The applicant sought advance ruling in respect of the following question:

Whether the said work can be covered under clause 3(v)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, i.e., works contract by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works pertaining to railways so as the entitle it for charging rate of GST at the rate of 12 per cent instead of 18 per cent.

HELD: Entry No. 3(v)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended by Notification No. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017, reads as :

Composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 by ways of construction, erection, commissioning or installation by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works pertaining to, -

(a)

Railways, including monorail and metro-----; [Para 13]

The contract of the applicant should satisfy the following conditions to get covered under the aforesaid Entry No. 3(v)(a):

(i)

The contract must be a composite supply of works contract;

(ii)

The works must be a construction, erection, commissioning or installation by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works;

(iii)

It must pertain to railway. [Para 14]

The work awarded to the applicant comprises of laying of track as per layout plan, pavement along the track, construction of Admin building, Warehouse, Electrical works and Fire-fighting works, etc. at Khodiyar, Gandhinagar, Gujarat. These works are in the nature of new works to be executed. These also involve construction of original works. As such same are covered under the definition of original work as defined in clause (zs) of the Notification No. 12/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. [Para 14.1]

As the work awarded to the applicant is relating to an immovable property; wherein transfer of property in goods is involved, the entire contract is covered under the definition of works contract as defined under section 2(119). Hence the first condition is satisfied. [Para 14.2]

The main issue is whether the work awarded to the applicant is contract pertaining to railways. In the instant case, the work relating to construction has been awarded by an entity viz. Rites Ltd. However, the applicant has submitted no evidence in support of the claim that work awarded to it pertains to railways. [Para 14.3]

'Railways' has not been defined under the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. Section 2(31) of the Railways Act, 1989 defines railways as :

(31) 'railway' means a railway, or any portion of a railway, for the public carriage of passengers or goods, and includes -

(a)

supply of right to use the equipment along with manpower service, maintenance service, etc. As multiple taxable supplies of services are involved, this is a composite supply of service. However, this is not a works contract as there is no immovable property nor transfer of title of goods is involved. As per Explanatory Notes to classification of services for SAC 9973, the agreement of wet leasing of machinery falls under classification of SAC 997319 for leasing of machinery with or without operator, etc. The agreement for Comprehensive Annual Maintenance Contract (CAMC) of Mechanical & Electrical under Schedule VI(a) and Schedule VI(b) will involve supply of goods, spares, etc. and services and hence is a composite supply. This maintenance is in relation to the factory being erected, commissioned involving transfer of goods and hence is a composite supply of works contract which is a supply of service as per Schedule II of the CGST Act. [Para 5.2]

From a reading of Serial No. 3(ii) and Serial No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, it is apparent that the rate of tax applicable for Composite supply of works contract, supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of 'original works' pertaining to 'railways' is 6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent SGST.

The Tender Document and Letter of Acceptance indicate that the contract in question is for erection, commissioning, installation, maintenance of a factory for manufacturing stainless steel coaches at ICF, Chennai which is a 'Production Unit' under the Ministry of Railway. Therefore, all the works under this contract is pertaining to railways as defined in section 2(31) of the Railways Act, 1989.

The 'Original works' is defined under Para 2(zs) of Notification No. 12/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as all new constructions;

(i)

all types of additions and alterations to abandoned or damaged structures on land that are required to make them workable;

(ii)

erection, commissioning or installation of plant, machinery or equipment or structures, whether pre-fabricated or otherwise;

Applying the said definition, to the case at hand, the work executed by the applicant is an 'Original work' as it is for erection, commissioning, installation of plant and machinery and structures.

The agreement for erection, commissioning, installation of plant and machinery for a factory to manufacture stainless steel coaches covering Schedule I, II, III is taxable at 6 per cent CGST as per Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and 6 per cent SGST as per Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. II(2)/CTR/532(d-14)/2017 vide G.O. (Ms) No. 72, dated 29-6-2017 as amended with effect from 22-8-2017. Prior to that, it is taxable at 9 per cent CGST as per Sl. No. 3(ii) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and 9 per cent SGST as per Sl. No. 3(ii) of Notification No. II(2)/CTR/532(d-14)/2017 vide G.O. (Ms) No. 72 dated 29-6-2017 as amended.

The agreement for wet leasing of Robotic spot welding machine and Laser cutting and welding machine as per Schedule V(a) and Schedule V(b) is not a works contract though it is a composite supply and hence is not eligible for benefit of Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

The agreement for Comprehensive Annual Maintenance Contract (CAMC) of Mechanical & Electrical under Schedule VI(a) and Schedule VI(b) is composite supply of works contract maintenance pertaining to railways. However, Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of the above Notification dated 28-6-2017 does not cover maintenance. Hence it is not eligible for benefit of Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of this Notification.

The applicant in its written submissions has stated that it is also eligible for benefit of Sl. No. 3(vi)(a) of the Notification dated 28-6-2017 which is for composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, provided to the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of -

(a)

A civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession;

, Staff recreation like parks, new rain water harvesting structures, painting, renovation of old structures etc. The applicant has claimed before the Railway Authorities that these are all original works as they involve new asset creation or bringing life to unused structures of Railways and these come under the works contract services as per CGST Act. [Para 9]

The issue is basically divided into two categories. One that results in the new buildings and the other repair and reconstruction of the old structures. [Para 10] The rate of tax applicable in terms of Entry No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is 6 per cent under CGST. [Para 10.1]

Entry 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is related to works contract services supplied to Railways, which is construction or erection or commissioning or installation of original works. The entire dispute is regarding what are 'original works'. [para 10.2]

The term 'original works' has been defined in clause (zs) of para 2 of Notification No. 12/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. [Para 10.3]

On examination of definition of 'original work', it is seen that only 'additions or alterations made to abandoned or damaged structures on land that are made to make them workable' are treated as original works and not all repairs and maintenance services. [Para 10.4]

The works carried out by the applicant are analyzed and it is found that they involve two types of works - one being new construction and other being repairs of old structures. In as far as construction of new structures are concerned which are constructed where nothing existed before would definitely fall under the realm of 'original works'. [Para 10.5]

But in case of constructions which are made where the structures already existed, the same can be classified as (a) where the additions and alternations are made to the abandoned structures on land or damages structures on land to make them workable; (b) repairs of already existing structures which are in working condition and (c) construction services on structures not on land.

It is pertinent to note that only those works contract services covered under (a) are to be treated as 'original works' and not those covered under related to (b) and (c). The meaning of the words 'structures on land' needs to be analysed as only these qualify for the reduced rate of tax. [Para 10.6]

Both the contextual meaning in relation to railways is that the structure should be something which is built from parts, i.e., a building, or other constructed ones. Secondly, these constructed structures should be on land to be covered under the scope of the entry. All these point to the scope of the entry that the structures which are directly on the land are included. Further, these structures must be damaged to the extent that the same cannot be used and the activity of works contract services, if executed to make these unusable structures reusable, would cover under this entry for reduced rate of tax. [Para 11]

All repairs made to buildings do not constitute 'original works'. It is only those services executed to make an unusable building usable again is covered under 'original works'. [Para 13]

The Railways Department is a Central government Department and, hence, it is clear that the services provided to them if it is for a purpose other than for business, then the same would be covered under entry 3(vi)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. However, the services of repairs, maintenance, renovation and alterations of residential complex meant for use of the Railway employees are covered under entry 3(vi) of the Notification and, hence, eligible for tax at 6 per cent CGST. [Para 14]

As regards the question of rate of tax, it is submitted by the applicant that the contract is a single contract and it consists of multiple works. On the question whether this contract amounts to a composite supply or mixed supply or a bunch of separate supplies, it is seen that the same cannot be a composite supply of works contracts as there is no principal supply and the works are not naturally bundled. It cannot be a mixed supply also because the valuations of each of the supply of works are valued separately and they would amount to separate contracts. Hence, there is no common price for all the contracts. Hence, it can be decided that each of the works mentioned in a schedule is a separate contract in itself and this is bolstered by the fact that the works are not in the same place and also are different in nature. [Para 15]

is clear from the above that structure or machinery that cannot be located/moved or shifted elsewhere at frequent intervals will be considered as immovable property. Therefore, it is found that the contract given to the applicant by LMRC for designing and installation of the Automatic Fare Collection System which cannot be shifted or moved to other places/buildings at frequent intervals and is meant for permanent beneficial of the building i.e. Stations under LMRC; will fall under the 'Works Contract'.[Para 9.3] Coming to the next question for which Advance Ruling is required, the Authority noticed that the Notification No. 1/2018- Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 has been issued by the Central Government making amendments in the Notification No. 8/2017-Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

Previously, under the Notification dated 28-6-2017, composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 was attracting duty at the rate of 18 per cent under Heading 9954 (Construction Services) at Sl. No. 3.

Vide Notification No. 20/2017-Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017, the entries against serial number 3 for item (iii) in column (3) and the entries relating thereto in the Notification No. 1/2018- Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018, were substituted with (v) Composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 , supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works pertaining to,- (a) railways, excluding monorail and metro; attracting the duty rate at the rate of 12 per cent.

Later, vide Notification No. 1/2018- Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018, the Notification No. 8/2017-Integrated Tax (Rate), was amended and the word `excluding' was substituted by 'including' also classifying that the Composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 provided by a sub-contractor to the main contractor providing services specified in item (iii) or item (vi) above to the Central Government, State Government, Union territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity would attract duty at the rate of 12 per cent.

Since, in the instant case, the composite supply of work contract is being provided by a sub-contractor to the main contractor i.e. Government Authority, the same shall be covered under the above amendment carried out vide the above notification dated 25-1-2018, the same shall now attract duty at the rate 12 per cent.[Para 9.4]

In view of the above, both the members unanimously rule as under;

(i)

A contract shall be treated as Composite Contract under GST if it involves making of supply of goods and services which are inter-connected and inter­-dependent on each other even though BOQ mentions separate value of goods and services.

(ii)

A pre-GST period contract shall be treated as Composite Contract in GST if it satisfies the condition of Composite Supply.

(iii)

A contract for designing, installation and setting up of Automatic Fare Collection System for Lucknow Metro Project will amount to Work Contract.

(iv)

GST will be charged at the rate of 12 per cent in terms of Notification No. 1/2018- Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 being composite services supplied to a Government entity procured by the said entity in relation to work entrusted to it by the Central and State Government.[Para 10]

dated 28-6-2017 are services specific. The service provider and the service recipient are immaterial for the determination of beneficiary of this concessional rate of GST. That is, if the works contract services provided by the main contractor or sub-contractor are pertaining to the railways, the concessional rate of 12 per cent GST is allowed to the person who carries out such works contract pertaining to railways. The only condition in (a) of item (v) is that,

(a) There should be a composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section (2) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

(b)

It should be by way of construction, erection, commissioning, or installation of original works pertaining to railways.

If the above conditions are fulfilled then works contract services provided by the sub-contractor would be covered by item (v).

In view of aforesaid, there is no reason to interfere with the ruling given by the Advance Ruling Authority. [Para 11]

No. 24/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017  (NR)

FACT: The applicant, a Central Government Department, awarded a works contract to Tata Projects Ltd. for design, fabrication, procurement, instrumentation and control and commissioning of Trisonic Wind Tunnel with Ejector System. The work involves fabrication of machineries, transportation of equipments to be attached to the system, construction of civil structure where the machinery is to be installed. It sought advance ruling in respect of the following question:

If the above supply is considered as works contract, whether it would be covered under Entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 24/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017 attracting GST at the rate of 12 per cent.

HELD: Being a works contract awarded by the Central Government Department by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, of a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry or any other business or profession will attract 12 per cent GST as per Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. [Para 3]

Ruling

The work of design, realisation, integration and commissioning of Trisonic Wind Tunnel as a turnkey project will fall under the definition of works contract under section 2(119) of the CGST Act, 2017.

The service provided to the applicant by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out of a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession will attract 12 per cent GST as per Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. [Para 4]

Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 and inserted new entries at Serial No. 3(ix), 3(x), 3(xi) and 3(xii). The composite supply of works contract services provided by a sub-contractor to the main contractor were dealt with in entries at Serial No. 3(ix) & 3(x) of the amended Notification No. 11/2017. [Para 20] The said entries at Serial No. 3(ix) and 3(x) pertained to works contract services provided by the sub-contractor to the main contractors who were in turn providing services to Central Government, State Government, Union territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity. The new entries at Serial No. 3(ix) and 3(x) inserted vide Notification dated 25-1-2018 prescribed GST rate for sub-contractor services pertaining only to the services provided by the main contractor to the Governments/Government entity which were covered in Serial No. 3(iii), Serial No. 3(vi) and Serial No. 3(vii) of the principal rate Notification No. 11/2017. [Para 21]

The entry at Serial No. 3(vi) concerned with works contract services provided by a sub-contractor to the main contractor where the main contractor is providing works contract services to a Government Entity by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion of (a) a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession; (b) a structure meant predominantly for use as (i) an educational, (ii) a clinical, or (iii) an art or cultural establishment; or (c) a residential complex predominantly meant for self-use or the use of their employees or other persons specified in paragraph 3 of the Schedule-III to the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017. [Parra 22]

Vide Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate) dated 25-01-2018 a new entry no. 3(ix) was inserted in the principal rate Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate) dated 28-06-2017 vide which 'composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 provided by a sub-contractor to the main contractor providing services specified in item (iii) or item (vi) above to the Central Government, State Government, Union territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government entity' was made taxable at the rate of 12 per cent. The said amended Notification came into effect from the date of issue of the Notification. Hence, the said Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate) dated 25-1-2018 was issued on 25-1-2018 and in the opening paragraph of the said Notification the following is mentioned, 'In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (1) of section 9, sub-section (1) of section 11, sub-section (5) of section 15 and sub-section (1) of section 16, the Central Government, on the recommendations of the Council, and on being satisfied that it is necessary in the public interest so to do, hereby makes the following further amendments in the notification of the Government of India, in the Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated the 28-6-2017, published in the Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 3, Sub-section (i), vide number G.S.R. 690(E), dated the 28-6-2017, namely'. Accordingly, the said Notification is also published on the date of Notification in the Gazette of India. Further, an amendment in the Notification is prospective in nature, unless clearly specified to be clarificatory. Also the effective date of a Notification is always date of issue of Notification unless it is specified date of effect of the Notification. The Notification always came into effect from the date it was published in the Gazette of India and the subject Notification was issued in the Gazette of India on 25-1-2018 i.e. on the date it was issued. Therefore, Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate) dated 25-1-2018 is applicable/came into effect prospectively and from the date of issue i.e. from 25-1-2018. [Para 23]

In view of the above it is held that the GST rate of 12 per cent prescribed under Sr. No. (ix) vide Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 is effective from the date of issue of said Notification i.e. 25-1-2018. [Para 25]

Needless to mention that such supply shall not qualify for exemption as envisaged under Sr. No. 3(vi) to the Notification No. 11/2017 - C.T. (Rate), inasmuch as the said supply is a 'Pure Service' and not in the nature of works contract service. [Para 4.6] The works entrusted to the applicant namely construction of 800 seater boys hostel, 200 seater girls hostel, Construction of lecture hall complex, Construction of Student Activity Centre, Dispensary, Construction of 1000 capacity Auditorium, Construction of Central Research and Instrumentation facilities, Construction of Central Workshop, Play grounds are within the purview of sub-clause (b) of clause (vi) of Sl. (Rate) under CGST Act and corresponding notification under OGST Act, 2017, and hence merit exemption where the applicable tax rate is 12 per cent (6 per cent under CGST & 6 per cent under OGST Act, 2017). [Para 4.7]

The works contract so executed by the applicant includes Sewerage disposal (Sewerage and STP) unit and construction of water works are covered vide Sl. No. (iii) (c) to the said notification and merit exemption where the applicable tax rate is 12 per cent (6 per cent under CGST & 6 per cent under OGST Act, 2017). [Pra 4.8]

Now coming to the issue of construction of Directors Bungalow and construction of staff-faculty quarters. It is seen that the applicant has been awarded construction of Directors Bungalow, 40 nos. staff quarters, 84 nos. Faculty Quarters in the IIT Campus, Bhubaneswar. It is also observed that the civil construction of residential quarters is not the primary work entrusted to IIT, Bhubaneswar. Accordingly, why the benefit of concessional rate at the rate of 12 per cent GST should be available to this particular works contract awarded to the applicant? The intention of the Legislature has been to allow concessional rate to such work which has been entrusted to a Government entity for public interest in general, but extrapolating and extending this concessional rate to any or all activities of IIT, Bhubaneswar will not only be unwarranted but also defeat the very purpose of concessional rate. Hence, construction of Directors Bungalow and construction of staff/faculty quarters is out of purview of exemption provided under Notification No. 11/2017-C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and would attract GST at the rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST). [Para 4.9]

In view of the discussions foregoing, it is held that the works entrusted to the applicant by IIT, Bhubaneswar under contract/agreement dated 2-5-2016 cannot be termed as composite supply and, thus, entire work under the said contract shall not be entitled to concessional rate in terms of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. However, it is also held that the supply of goods and/or services or both which squarely fall within the ambit of scope of work entrusted to IIT, Bhubaneswar by Government of India shall be entitled for concessional rate under Sl. No. 3(vi) to Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), 28-6-2017 (R). In the instant case, it is seen that the applicant is providing composite supply of works contract in respect of Metro but the reduced rate of tax is available only if the work is of the type of original works. Original works would mean all new constructions; all types of additions and alterations to abandoned or damaged structures on land that are required to make them workable; erection, commissioning or installation of plant, machinery or equipment or structures, whether pre-fabricated or otherwise, etc. In the instant case, the work done by the applicant does not appear to be original works. The applicant itself has stated that here it would like to draw your attention to the fact that the scope of work does not include construction of entire project of metro stations, railway line, power supply, civil structures, etc. but scope include Shifting LT, HT Overhead lines crossing which are obstructing metro railway path and providing LT, HT underground cables for Nagpur Metro Rail Project. The work is not construction of metro rail project but this is shifting of existing utilities obstructing metro railway path and providing supplying and installation of new underground cable along with its accessories.

In view of the aforesaid, it is seen that in the instant case the contract is not related to any original work and is in the nature of composite supply of works contract. Hence the activity of the applicant is nothing but a composite supply of works contract, not being original works and they will be covered under Sr. No. 3, item (ii) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 and attract 18 per cent GST (9 per cent each of CGST and Maharashtra GST). The contracts in question are classifiable as works contract as per GST Law and Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 1/2018 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 is applicable to the instant case and the GST at the rate of 18 per cent would be applicable. HEADNOTE: Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, read with section 2(119) of the West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Railway - Whether construction of a private railway siding for carriage of coal and oil fuel to thermal power station by applicant, a project management consultant, in terms of agreement with Region Development Corporation is a composite supply of works contract taxable at rate of 12 per cent under Serial No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Para 7]GST: Construction of a private railway siding for carriage of coal and oil fuel to thermal power station by applicant project management consultant in terms of agreement with Region Development Corporation is a composite supply of works contract taxable at rate of 12 percent under Serial No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

FACT: The instant Application for Advance Rulings states that Damodar Valley Corporation ('DVC') has appointed the Applicant as Project Management Consultant for construction of railway infrastructure, including commissioning of the railway system to handle coal and oil fuel traffic of Raghunathpur Thermal Power Station (RTPS). The scope of work includes awarding contracts on behalf of DVC for construction of railway infrastructure. The work includes construction of a private siding between Joychandipahar and Bero stations in Adra division of SE Railway, enabling carriage of coal and oil fuel to RTPS. The Applicant is responsible for passing the bills of the vendors and contractors after necessary scrutiny, and making the payments from a specially designated escrow account in which DVC deposits the requisite amount, and making deduction of statutory taxes and deposit of the same, issuance of tax deduction certificates etc.

HELD: According to Serial No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate) dated 28/06/2017, as amended from time to time, the composite supply of works contract as defined under section 2(119) of the GST Act, supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning, or installation of original works pertaining to railways, including monorail and metro, is taxable at the rate 12 per cent. Original work, as defined under para 2(zs) of Notification No. 12/2017-CT (Rate) dated 28/06/2017, means all new construction involving (i) all types of additions and alterations to abandoned or damaged structures on land that are required to make them workable, and (ii) erection, commissioning or installation of plant, machinery or equipment or structures, whether pre-fabricated or otherwise. The term 'railways' is not defined in the GST Act. It, however, is defined under section 2(31) of the Railways Act, 1989, meaning a railway, or any portion of a railway, for the public carriage of passengers or goods. [Para 4]

It is evident from the above discussion that the scope of work, as outlined in the Applicant's agreement with DVC, is that of works contract, as defined under section 2(119), fit to be called an 'original work' within the meaning ascribed to the term in para 2(zs) of Notification No. 12/2017-CT (Rate) dated 28-06-2017, and pertains to 'railways', provided it is meant for public carriage of passengers or goods. [Para 5]

The courts generally held that the phrase 'public carriage of passengers or goods' cannot be construed in such manner as to exclude from the ambit of 'railways' the sidings built and owned by organizations other than the government. [Para 6]

[Para 8] The revenue has challenged the ruling given by the Advance Ruling Authority by contending that the activities carried out by the sub-contractor will not fall under item (v) of Sr. No. 3 of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by the Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018, since there is no specific inclusion of works contract services provided by sub-contractor to main contractor. It further submitted that items (ix) and (x) inserted in the amending Notification No.1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 provide for the concessional rates of 12 per cent and 5 per cent GST to those sub-contractors, who are providing works contract services to the main contractor providing services, specified in item (iii) or item (vi) and item (vii) of the Sr. No. 3 of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) as amended by the Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 to the Central Government, State Government, Union territory, a local authority; a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity. Thus the amendment carried out in the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 does not provide the concessional rate of GST to the sub-contractor providing composite supply of the works contract to the main contractor who is given works contract by railways. It further argued that the works contract services provided by the sub-contractor to the main contractor should be covered under the residuary entry (xii) of the Notification dated 28-6-2017. The applicant vehemently countered this argument by deposing that the description of the activities covered under item (v) of Sr. No. 3 of the Notification No. 11/2017 -Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by the Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 are services specific due to the presence of the clause 'pertaining to'. Thus there is no relevance for the provider or recipient of the services in the instant case. If the services fulfil the criteria of the activities/services having description contained the above item (v), then it is immaterial that who is providing services to whom. [Para 9]

There is no merit in the above mentioned contention of the revenue as from the plain reading of item (v) of Sr. No. 3 of the Notification dated 28-6-2017, it is very much clear that any supply of works contract pertaining to the railways including monorail and metro is subject to concessional rate of 12 per cent GST. In the instant case, though the applicant is providing works contract services to its main contractor who has entered into works contract agreement with railways, the composite supply of works contract being carried out by the applicant is ultimately going to the use of railways without being subjected to any change or modification. Thus the said works contract, though undertaken by the sub-contractor, is undoubtedly pertaining to the railways and no one else. Thus the condition specified under item (v) of Sr. No. 3 of Notification dated 28-6-2017 is completely fulfilled. Therefore, the services provided by the sub-contractor would attract concessional rate of 12 per cent GST. [Para 10]

As regards the revenue's contention that there is no specific mention of sub-contractor providing services in Sr. No. 3(v) as provided in items (ix) and (x) which were incorporated into the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 by the amending Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018. There was no need to include such sub-contractors in item (v) of the Notification dated 28-6-2017 as there was no confusion whether the sub-contractor will be eligible to such concessional rate of GST, since the activities described under item (v) of Sr. No. 3 of the Notification dated 28-6-2017 are services specific. The service provider and the service recipient are immaterial for the determination of beneficiary of this concessional rate of GST. That is, if the works contract services provided by the main contractor or sub-contractor are pertaining to the railways, the concessional rate of 12 per cent GST is allowed to the person who carries out such works contract pertaining to railways. HELD: As the question number I & II asked by the applicant are interrelated, both the questions are taken-up together for discussion. (R), dated 28-6-2017, it is observed that the said Entry No. (iv) reads as follows :

'(iv) Composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2, supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of, —

(a)

a road, bridge, tunnel, or terminal for road transportation for use by general public;

Whereas the Entry No. (vi) of the said Notification reads as :

'Composite supply of works contract as defined under clause (119) of section 2, provided to the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of -

and in both the cases the applicable rate of GST is at the rate of 12 per cent including CGST and SGST.

Now, it is observed that the question to be decided is :

(i)

Whether the supply made by the applicant to the NHAI is a 'composite supply of works contract', and, if yes,

(ii)

Whether the said supply is being used for construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of a road, bridge, tunnel, or terminal for road transportation for use by general public, or

(iii)

Whether the said supply is being provided to the Central Government, Government, Union Territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of -

(a)

a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession;

(iv)

Which classification will be more appropriate among Entry (iv) or Entry (vi) of the CGST Rate Notification. [Para 10]

As per the sub-section (30) of section 2 , the 'Composite supply' is defined to mean a supply made by a taxable person to a recipient consisting of two or more taxable supplies of goods or services or both, or any combination thereof, which are naturally bundled and supplied in conjunction with each other in the ordinary course of business, one of which is a principal supply.

Further the term 'works contract' is defined in sub-section (119) of section 2 to mean a contract for building, construction, fabrication, completion, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, modification, repair, maintenance, renovation, alteration or commissioning of any immovable property, wherein transfer of property in goods (whether as goods or in some other form) is involved in the execution of such contract. [Para 11]

It is observed that the agreement entered into between the applicant and NHAI is for the 'Development of six lane Eastern Peripheral Expressway : ITS (Intelligent Transport System) Installation Project', which involves design, supply, installation, testing, commissioning of ITS which primarily includes Advanced Traffic Management System (ATMS), Toll Management System (TMS) and Digital Transmission System along with operation and maintenance of ATMS for a period of 4 years on turnkey basis. From this, it appears that the scope of work involves supply of goods as well as services, which are in conjunction with each other to complete the ITS installation. [Para 12]

As per the General Conditions of the contract entered between the applicant and NHAI, each item of plant and materials shall become the property of the NHAI and free from liens and other encumbrances at the earlier of the (a) when it is incorporated in the works (b) when the applicant is paid the corresponding value of the plant and materials. [Para 13]

The courts generally held that the phrase 'public carriage of passengers or goods' cannot be construed in such manner as to exclude from the ambit of 'railways' the sidings built and owned by organizations other than the government. [Para 6] Article 366(20) of the Constitution excludes from the ambit of 'railway' only (a) a tramway wholly within a municipal area and (b) any line of communication wholly situate in one State and declared by Parliament by law not to be a railway. The Parliament excludes by law, apart from the tramways, the lines of rails mentioned under section 2(31)(ii) of the Railways Act, 1989, being rails built solely for the purpose of recreation. The term 'public carriage', therefore, cannot be given any meaning that may add more exclusion than specifically provided under section 2(31)(ii) of the Railways Act, 1989. DVC - a public sector undertaking - is the owner of the railway siding being built. It is meant for carriage of coal and oil fuel to RTPS. The purpose of the carriage of goods is, therefore, not recreation, but producing public goods like electricity. It is, therefore, not excluded under section 2(31)(ii) of the Railways Act, 1989. The construction of the private siding that the applicant refers to, therefore, pertains to 'railways'. In view of the foregoing, it was to be ruled that construction of a private railway siding for carriage of coal and oil fuel to RTPS, as described in the agreement between the applicant and DVC, is a composite supply of works contract taxable at the rate of 12 per cent under Serial No 3(v)(a) of Notification no 11/2017-CT(Rate) dated 28-06-2017. Thus, it is seen that it is not a fact that the applicants are only involved in erection, commissioning or installation of machinery belonging to some other person but are installing and commissioning the equipments supplied by them. FACT: Nuclear Fuel Complex (NFC) had awarded contract to the applicant for civil, structural and PH works for plant and non-plant buildings (both RCC and Pre-Engineered buildings) along with other allied structures for PFFF & ZFF facilities at Nuclear Fuel Complex.

The applicant sought advance ruling on question as to what is the GST rate applicable for this project.

HELD: Nuclear Fuel Complex (NFC) had awarded contract to the applicant. NFC is an industrial arm established under Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India, therefore, supply under the contract is given to a Central Government by the applicant. The contract is for 'Contract for Civil, Structural and PH works for plant and Non-Plant Buildings (both RCC and Pre-Engineered Buildings) along with other allied structures for PFFF & ZFF Facilities at Nuclear Fuel Complex.' The supply is a mix of goods and services.

The supply of goods and services is a kind of works contract service. The works contracts has been defined in section 2(119) of the CGST Act, 2017.

It is observed that the term works contract has been restricted to contract for building construction, fabrication etc. of any immovable property only. As per Para 6(a) of Schedule II to the CGST Act, 2017, works contracts as defined in section 2(119) of the CGST Act, 2017 shall be treated as a supply of services. Thus, there is a clear demarcation of a works contract as a supply of service under GST. The rate of GST for Works Contract service supply to a Central Government has been prescribed in serial number 3 of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax(Rate) dated 28-6-2017 as amended from time to time.

The activity is a work contract supply undertaken for Central Government. The limitation under this notification is that activity/supply is meant predominantly for use other than commerce, industry or any other business or profession.

The activity, thus, may fall under the definition of business as NFC is engaged in manufacture and enrichment of fuel which will ultimately be used for production of electricity. The activity of manufacture of fuel from NFC is, thus, leading to ultimate production and distribution of electricity which is a commercial activity. The supply, thus, provided by the applicant to the NFC is a works contract service (construction service) falling at Serial No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended from time to time and will attract GST at the rate of 18 per cent (SGST 9 per cent + CGST 9 per cent) [Para 5].

Thus, the GST rate applicable on the project undertaken by the applicant is 18 per cent (SGST 9 per cent + CGST 9 per cent). [Para 6]

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Supply and installation - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFFCCIL) has awarded a contract to one 'A' (main contractor) for performance of works relating to design, construction, supply, installation, testing and commissioning of electrification, signaling, telecommunication and associated works of double track railways lines under construction for Bhaupur-Khurja section - 'A' (main contractor) has subcontracted performance of certain works and services of main contract to applicant - Whether contract work of applicant to main contractor is covered under Entry No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and liable to tax at 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST or 12 per cent IGST) with effect from 22-8-2017 - Held, yes [Paras 4.10 and 5][In favour of assessee]GST: Where Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited has awarded a contract to one 'A' (main contractor) for performance of works relating to railways and 'A' has sub-contracted performance of certain works and services of main contract to applicant, contract work of applicant to main contractor is covered under Entry No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

FACT: The Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFFCCIL) has awarded a contract to one 'A' (main contractor) for performance of the works relating to the design, construction, supply, installation, testing and commissioning of electrification, signaling, telecommunication and associated works of double track railway lines under construction for Bhaupur-Khurja section.

'A' (main contractor) has subcontracted the performance of certain works and services of the main contract to the applicant consisting supply and installation, testing and commissioning of automatic signaling equipment of indoor and outdoor, LC gates required as per the requirement of DFFCCIL under the main contract.

The applicant sought advance ruling in respect of the following questions:

(a)

What is the rate of tax for the subcontractor who executes the works contract work like supply of goods or services or both pertaining to Railways based on the order received from the main contractor who got the work order directly from Railways.

(b)

Does the rate of tax of 6 per cent as per Sl. No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax, dated 28-6-2017, as amended, applicable to subcontractors or not.

(c)

If the answer to the question No. (b) is yes, then from which date it is applicable.

HELD: The contract of the applicant with the main contractor should satisfy the following conditions to get covered under Entry No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017:

(a)

The contract must be a composite supply of works contract.

(b)

The works must be a construction, erection, commissiong or installation of original works.

(c)

It must pertain to Railways. [Para 4.4]

In the instant case, the contract is for supply and installation, testing and commissioning of automatic signaling equipment of indoor and outdoor, LC gates and involves excavation of pits, casting and plastering and other parts which involve construction, erection, commissioning and installation of original works. Hence the second condition is satisfied.

As the contract is related to an immovable property, the entire contract is covered under the definition of works contract under section 2(119). Hence the first condition is also satisfied. [Para 4.5]

The main issue is whether this is a contract pertaining to Railways. The main contractor has obtained the contract from Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited and then subcontracted to the applicant. The work is related to supply and installation, testing and commissioning of automatic signaling equipment of indoor and outdoor, LC gates as per the requirement of DFCCIL. [Para 4.6]

Since the works related to railways network, the contract can be said to be pertaining to Railways. The term pertaining to Railways is more expansive and includes other establishments other than Indian Railways. Hence the contract is pertaining to Railways. [Para 4.8]

MPPGCL has been established by the Government of Madhya Pradesh and the Government of Madhya Pradesh has a 100 per cent shareholding in the company and is also exercising full control over the activities of the said company. Thus, MPPGCL qualifies to be called and termed as a 'Government Entity' for the purpose of GST law, as it fulfils the necessary and sufficient conditions laid down under notification No. 11/2017. [Para 5.4] Now, the said Government Entity i.e. MPPGCL has been entrusted with the work of power generation in the State of Madhya Pradesh. The essential and sole work entrusted to MPPGCL by the Government of Madhya Pradesh is of electricity (power) generation. MPPGCL has awarded a works contract for construction of 599 residential quarters to the applicant. However, the civil construction of residential quarters is neither the primary work entrusted to MPPGCL nor it has any bearing on the work i.e. power generation by any means. Thus, the benefit of concessional rate of 12 per cent GST should not be available to this particular works contract awarded to the applicant. The intention of the legislature has been to give concessional rate to such work which has been entrusted to a Government entity for public interest in general. Any work having direct involvement in the entrusted work i.e. power generation would merit exemption envisaged under Sr.No.3(vi)(c) of the Notification No.11/2017-CT (Rate) under CGST Act and corresponding notification under MPGST Act 2017, but extrapolating and extending this concessional rate to any or all activities of MPPGCL will not only be unwarranted but also defeat the very purpose of concessional rate. [Para 5.5]

The activity in question definitely did not have any relation to the principal work of power generation entrusted by the State Government to MPPGCL, and, thus, the works contract service of construction of residential quarters would attract GST at the rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) in terms of Notification No.11/2017-CT Rate dated 28-6-2017 and corresponding notification under MPGST Act, 2017. [Para 5.6]

Thus, the impugned activity of the applicant would attract GST at the rate of 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) classifiable under SAC 9954 read with Notification No.11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) and corresponding notification under MPGST Act 2017. [Para 5.7]
