At the outset, we would like to make it clear that the provisions of both the CGST Act and the MGST Act are the same except for certain provisions. Therefore, unless a mention is specifically made to such dissimilar provisions, a reference to the CGST Act would also mean a reference to the same provisions under the MGST Act.

The present appeal has been filed under Section 100 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and the Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 [hereinafter referred to as "the CGST Act and MGST Act"] by the Assistant Commissioner, Central Tax, Division-I (Talegaon), Pune-I Commissionerate (herein after referred to as the "Appellant") against the Advance Ruling No. GST-ARA-09/2018-19/B-65 Mumbai, Dt. 11.07.2018

BRIEF FACTS OF THE CASE

A.

M/s. Shree Construction (hereinafter referred to as 'the party') are providing works contract service as sub-contractor to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to Railways. They execute and undertake composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

B.

It is the opinion of the party that as per Notification No-20/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 22-08-2017 the GST is 12% for composite supply of works contract supplied by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works pertaining to railways. As per Sr.No-12 in press release of 25th meeting of GST council held at New Delhi on 18-01-2018, the rate of GST applicable to main contractor should be levied by sub-contractor.

C.

Further, it is stated by the party that as per Notification No-01/2018- Central Tax( Rate) dated 25-01-2018 the service provided by sub-contractor to main contractor for railway original works contract services is not specified in the notification. The party say that they are sub-contractor providing service to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways, and they should charge 12% GST only and not 18% as applicable in other cases. The contract for original works pertaining to railways remains the same works contract. As there is difference of opinion after reading of press release of 25th meeting of GST council dated 18-01-2018 and notification No 1/2018 dated 25-01 -2018, the party are not in position to levy correct rate of GST on original sub-contracting work pertaining to railways carried on by them for their main contractor. Accordingly, Advance Ruling was sought for clarification for rate of tax to be levied by the sub-contractor to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways.

D.

The Advance Ruling Authority passed an order under section 98 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and the Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and the questions were answered as under —

Q. No. 1 : What Tax rate to be charged by the sub-contractor to main contractor on Works Contract Services (WCS) pertaining to railways original works contract?

Answer: The tax rate to be charged by the sub-contractor to the main contractor would be @ 6% of CGST and 6% of SGST, in the present case.

Q. No. 2: Whether to charge tax rate of 12% GST or 18% GST?

Answer: The tax rate to be charged would be 12% in the present case.

E.

Aggrieved by the said ruling of Authority for Advance Ruling, the department has preferred the present appeal.

It is pertinent to note that only those works contract services covered under (a) above are to be treated as "original works" and not those covered under related to (b) and (c). The meaning of the words "structures on land" needs to be analysed as only these qualify for the reduced rate of tax. 11. According to Cambridge Dictionary, "structure" means "something that has been made or built from parts, especially a large building" or "something built, such as a building or a bridge". Both the contextual meaning in relation to railways is the structure should be something which is built from parts, i.e. a building, or other constructed ones. Secondly, these constructed structures should be on land to be covered under the scope of the entry. All these point to the scope of the entry that the structures which are directly on the land are included. Further, these structures must be damaged to the extent that the same cannot be used and the activity of works contract services, if executed to make these unusable structures reusable, would cover under this entry for reduced rate of tax.

Provided that where the services are supplied to a Government Entity, they should have been procured by the said entity in relation to a work entrusted to it by the Central Government, State Government, Union territory or local authority, as the case maybe."

The Railways Department is a Central Government Department and hence it is clear that the services provided to them if it is for a purpose other than for business, then the same would be covered under entry 3(vi). Since the Railways is undertaking the transportation services of goods and passenger, the services provided cannot be covered under entry 3(vi)(a). However, the services of repairs, maintenance, renovation and alterations of residential complex meant for use of the Railway employees are covered under entry 3(vi) of the Notification and hence eligible for tax at 6% CGST.

15. As far as the question of rate of tax, it is submitted by the applicant that the contract is a single contract and it consists of multiple works. On the question whether this contract amounts to a composite supply or mixed supply or a bunch of separate supplies, it is seen that the same cannot be a composite supply of works contracts as there is no principal supply and the works are not naturally bundled. It cannot be a mixed supply also because the valuations of each of the supply of works are valued separately and they would amount to separate contracts. Hence, there is no common price for all the contracts. Hence it can be safely decided that each of the works mentioned in a schedule is a separate contract in itself and this is bolstered by the fact that the works are not in the same place and also are different in nature.

5 [

Liability to pay tax on transfer of property in goods involved in execution of works contract

14. (1) Notwithstanding anything contained elsewhere in this Act, any transfer of property in goods (whether as goods or in some other form) involved in the execution of a works contract in West Bengal shall be deemed to be a sale of those goods by the person making the transfer and a purchase of those goods by the person to whom such transfer is made.

(2) Every dealer, who is liable on the day immediately before the appointed day to pay tax under section 15 of the West Bengal Sales Tax Act, 1994, and who would have continued to be so liable under the said Act on such appointed day had this Act not come into force, shall, in addition to the tax, if any, payable by him under any other provisions of this Act, be liable to pay tax on all transfers of property in goods involved in the execution of works contract referred to in sub-section (1), from such appointed day, at the rate specified in section 18.

(3) Every dealer to whom the provisions of sub-section (2) do not apply and whose contractual transfer price calculated from the commencement of the year ending on the day immediately before the appointed day exceeds the amount prescribed under section 15 of the West Bengal Sales Tax Act, 1994, on the last day of such year shall, in addition to the tax, if any, payable by him under any other provisions of this Act, be liable to pay tax on all transfers of property in goods involved in the execution of works contract referred to in sub-section (1), from such appointed day, at the rate specified in section 18.

(4) Every dealer to whom the provisions of sub-section (2) or sub-section (3) do not apply, shall, if his contractual transfer price calculated from the commencement of any year, exceeds 6[twenty lakh rupees] at any time within such year, be liable, in addition to the tax, if any, payable by him under any other provisions of this Act, to pay tax on all transfers of property in goods involved in the execution of works contract referred to in sub-section (1) at the rate specified in section 18 on and from the day immediately following the day on which such contractual transfer price first exceeds 7[twenty lakh rupees].

(5) Every dealer who has been registered under sub-section (2) of section 24 for his application under clause (b) of sub-section (1) of that section, on any date prior to the date on which his contractual transfer price exceeds 8[twenty lakh rupees], shall be liable to pay tax on all transfers of property in goods involved in the execution of works contract referred to in sub-section (1) at the rate specified in section 18 on and from the date of such registration.

(6) Every dealer who incurs liability to pay tax under sub-section (3) of section 27C, shall, notwithstanding that his contractual transfer price does not exceed 9[twenty lakh rupees], also be liable, in addition to the tax, if any, payable by him under any other provisions of this Act, to pay tax on transfer by him of property in goods involved in the execution of works contract referred to in sub-section (1) at the rate specified in section 18 on and from the date of transfer of business.

(7) Every dealer who incurs liability to pay tax under section 10 or section 11, he shall, notwithstanding that his contractual transfer price does not exceed 10[twenty lakh rupees], also be liable, in addition to the tax payable by him under any other provisions of this Act, to pay tax on transfer by him of property in goods involved in the execution of works contract referred to in sub-section (1) at the rate specified in section 18 on and from the day he incurs liability to pay tax under that section.

(8) Every dealer who has become liable to pay tax under this section, shall continue to be so liable until the expiry of three consecutive years commencing on or after the appointed day, during each of which his contractual transfer price does not exceed 11[twenty lakh rupees] and such further period after the date of such expiry as may be prescribed, and on the expiry of such three years or further period, his liability to pay such tax shall cease:

Provided that where a dealer has become liable to pay tax under sub-section (7) and has not incurred liability to pay tax under sub-section (4), he shall continue to be so liable until his liability ceases under section 10 or section 11.

Tax on buildings

(b) If any part or space of a building is leased for the first time on or after 1st April, 2011, then the entire building shall be deemed to have been leased for the first time on or after 1st April, 2011.

7[Explanation : No tax under this section shall be levied in respect of the transactions which are in the nature of works contract and on which tax is payable under section 9 as a works contractor.]

(2) (a) Such value of land, as may be prescribed, assigned to the building shall be deducted from its market value of both land and building to determine its capital value.

(b) If the sale price of a building is more than its market value, then its sale price will be taken as its market value for the purpose of determining its capital value.

(3) Every builder liable to pay tax under sub-section (1) and who is not liable to pay tax under section 9, shall get himself enrolled in the manner as may be prescribed.

(4) An enrolled builder and a registered dealer who is liable to pay tax under sub-section (1), in respect of goods specified in Schedule II other than those specified in 1[Part-Ill and Part-IIIA] of the said Schedule purchased within the State of Madhya Pradesh from a registered dealer after payment to him input tax for consumption or use in the construction of buildings, shall claim or be allowed in such manner and within such period as may be prescribed, input tax rebate of the amount of such input tax:

2a [ (4A) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in sub-section (4), where a builder makes an application for grant of an enrolment certificate under sub-section (3) after the prescribed period but before 30th June, 2013, he shall be eligible to claim or be allowed input tax rebate in accordance with the provisions of this section. ]

(5) No rebate under this section shall be claimed or be allowed in respect of the goods as the State Government may, by notification, specify:

3[Provided that the purchase value of goods, on which tax under the Act has been paid at the time of purchase and no input tax rebate is admissible on such purchase, shall be deducted from the capital value of the building.]

(6) The rebate under sub-section (4) shall be adjusted towards the tax payable under sub-section (1).

(7) The provisions of this Act shall mutatis mutandis apply to a builder who is liable to pay tax under sub-section (1).]

Levy of tax on transfer of property in goods involved in the execution of Works Contract

13. (1) Every dealer shall pay for each year, a tax under this Act on his taxable turnover for transfer of property in goods (whether as goods or in some other form) involved in the execution of works contract determined at the rates specified for the same goods in the Schedules mentioned in section 12:

Provided that all amounts towards labour charges and other like charges not involving any transfer of property of goods actually incurred in connection with the execution of works contract, shall be allowed to be deducted from gross turnover of such dealer in determining his taxable turnover:

1[Provided further that if the amount towards labour charges and other like charges not involving any transfer of property in goods, actually incurred in connection with the execution of works contract are not ascertainable from the books of accounts manitained and produced by a dealer before the appropriate assessing authority, such dealer shall be allowed to deduct from his gross turnover such amount to wards labour charges and other like charges as the said authority shall determine on the basis of the nature of works, records available before him and making such verification as may be necessary, but not exceeding forty percent of the total value of the works executed by such dealer:

Provided further that the appropriate assessing authority shall determine the turnover taxable as applicable as per the rates of tax specified in the Schedules from the total taxable turnover ascertained after allowing deductions on account of labour charges and other like charges, on the basis of the records available before him and making such verifications as may be necessary in this behalf:

Provided also that the appropriate assesssing authortiy shall record in writing the reasons of determination of taxable quantum and applicable tax rate on such taxable quantum.]

(2) Where the dealer proves to the satisfaction of the prescribed authority that tax on the turnover of goods supplied by him in the course of execution of works contract, has been paid by his sub-contractor, the dealer shall not be liable to pay tax again on the turnover of such goods.

(3) Where a sub-contractor proves to the satisfaction of the prescribed authority that the tax leviable under sub-section (1) has, actually been paid by the dealer (his principal contractor) on the turnover of goods supplied to him by the dealer in the course of execution of works contract, the sub- contractor shall not be liable to pay tax again on the turnover of such goods.

(4) A dealer shall pay for each year, a tax under this Act on his taxable turnover in respect of the right to use any goods (whether or not for a specified period) at the rates specified in the Schedules under section 12 for the same goods had they been sold otherwise than by the transfer of the right to use them:

Provided further if the transfer of the right to use any goods is made by a dealer on more than one occasion in a year to the same or different party, the tax shall be leviable on each such occasion.

Explanation I: For the purposes of this section, the transfer of property in goods or transfer of right to use any goods for any purpose (whether or not for a specified period) shall be deemed to have taken place in Sikkim if the goods transferred are within the State at the time of their transfer or use application or appropriation for the execution of works contract, irrespective of the place where the agreement for the works contract is made and whether the consent of the other party, prior or subsequent to such use, application or appropriation has been obtained or not.

Explanation II: The levy of tax under this section shall be made whether the works contract is executed fully or partly during a year or abandoned or terminated before completion.

(5) The State Government may in the form and manner prescribed that every person making any payment to contractors executing the works contract shall deduct such amount as the tax deducted at source at two per cent or 1[at such per centum] of the said amount, as the State Government may by notification, determine.

17. (1) Notwithstanding anything contrary contained in section 20, every person making any payment or discharge or any liability on account of valuable consideration payable—

(a)

for the transfer of property in goods, whether as goods or in some other form, involved in the execution of works contract, and

(b)

for the transfer of property in goods on account of sales of such goods made to the Government of India or to any State Government,

shall deduct an amount not exceeding four percentum, as may be prescribed, purporting to be a part or full of the tax payable on such sales, from the bills or invoices raised by the works contractor or by the dealer selling such goods, as payable by the person:

Provided that no deduction of such amount shall be made in respect of any transfer of property in goods, the turnover of which is deductible, from the dealer's gross turnover, under sub-section (3) of section 6:

Provided further that no such payment or discharge of any bill raised by the works contractor of the dealer selling such goods shall be made without deductions:

Provided further that if the State Government is satisfied that it is necessary to do so in the interest of the State revenue, it may notify the names/posts of such persons who shall be competent persons to make such deduction.

(2) The deduction referred to in sub-section (1) shall be made in the manner, as may be prescribed, and the payment of such deduction into the Government treasury shall be the responsibility of the person making such deduction.

(3) The person making such deduction shall issue deduction certificate in the prescribed manner to the person or dealer from whose bill or invoice, such deduction has been made.

(4) If any person contravenes any or all of the provisions of sub-section (1) or (2) or (3), the prescribed Authority shall, after giving an opportunity of being heard, by an order, in writing, direct that such person shall pay by way of penalty, a sum 1[equal to the amount of tax deductible under sub-section (1)].

(5) The provisions of sections 25 and 27 for recovery of any amount of tax due from a dealer shall mutatis mutandis apply for recovery of any amount of tax, deducted and/or any penalty imposed but not deposited under this section.

Illustration:

Suppose an instalment is due at the time of completion of a particular floor and that floor is completed on 27th August, 2017. In present service tax regime, the developer can issue its invoice within 30 days i.e. up to 26th September, 2017. However, in GST regime, the invoice have to be issued before or at time of completion of service i.e. 27th August, 2017.

Effective Rate of Tax As per the draft list of rates released by the GST council after its meeting on 18.05.2017, rate of GST applicable on construction sector is 12%, where the value of land is included in the purchase consideration. There is no further abatement/composition on this rate. Further, person cannot claim refund of Input Tax Credit (ITC) accumulated on account of higher tax rates on inputs/input services than on the rate of output. In other words, in case of accumulation of ITC because of the fact that tax rates on some inputs or input services will be 18% or even 28%, its refund will not be allowed to the assessee.

Further, if the value of land is not included, then the rate of tax applicable would be 18% (under service of Works Contract).

In addition, all special services provided by builders like preferential location charges (PLC), power backup charges (PBC), club service, administrative charges, cheque return, booking transfer charges etc. would be chargeable at the rate of 18%.

However, one issue for consideration is the treatment of car parking charges that are recovered separately from a flat buyer. Some people might argue that buying flat is a pre-requisite for buying such car parking space and hence supply of flat and car parking space are naturally bundled in course of business and will thus fall under the category of composite supply and accordingly rate of 12% will be applicable on the car parking charges also. It would a close call on the part of developers and would definitely invite litigation from the GST department. Thus, to be safer side the builder might charge 18% rate on car parking charges.

The government also released a classification for services as per Service Accounting Code (SAC) under GST regime. As per the said scheme, a separate Section (Section 5: Construction Services) has been provided for the Construction service which is further sub-divided into headings and groups. Developers need to ascertain their category and SAC for various purposes under GST regime.

Further, rate chart for major significant inputs used in the construction industry and their rates in present as well as GST regime is given below:

Facts in the case of Harekrishna Developers, In re [2008] 14 STT 175 (AAR - New Delhi) 3.2 The applicant-firm intends to develop on its own plot of land a residential complex having more than twelve residential units with a club house and other common facilities. It will sell plots of land inside the complex to prospective buyers who will enter into a works contract with the applicant for the construction of residential units. The applicant itself will execute a part of the works contract [‘activity No. 3’] and for remaining part, the applicant will further enter into a works contract with other contractors [‘activity No. 4’]. However, goods for construction will be purchased/acquired by the applicant and the property in those goods will be transferred to buyers of the housing units and such transfer would be exigible to tax as sale of goods. The applicant sought advance ruling of the Authority on questions of its liability in these two types of activities, and also on question of rate of tax in case of activity No. 3.

The applicant contends that since the works contract in activities 3 and 4 involves construction of a new building-such an activity can only be covered under(ii)( b) in the Explanation to section 65(105)(zzzza). Since the new building proposed to be constructed in the course of the execution of the works contract is a residential one, and is not for the purpose of commerce or industry, such a works contract will not fall under (b) and therefore, will not attract service tax. The applicant further states that a works contract for construction of a new building for residential purposes is also not covered under any of the remaining classifications in (ii) of the Explanation to clause (zzzza). The classification (c) which covers ‘construction of a new residential complex or a part thereof’ is not applicable in applicant’s case as the works contract is for construction of an individual residential unit and not for construction of a residential complex.

Decision in the case of Harekrishna Developers (supra )

3.3 Authority for Advance Ruling held:

1. To attract service tax under sub-clause (zzzza) of section 65(105), a works contract has to meet the two conditions: (i) and (ii) in the Explanation to sub-clause (zzzza). The facts narrated by the applicant indicated that condition (i) is met in the instant case as the transfer of property in goods involved in the execution of the works contract is exigible to tax as sale of goods under the local Sales Tax Act. To meet condition (ii), the activity involved in the works contract in activity Nos. 3 and 4 has to be covered by at least one of the classifications (a ) to (e) in the Explanation to sub-clause (zzzza). Proceeding serially, one finds that building of a residential house on a sub-plot in a residential complex is clearly not covered in (a). As pointed out by the applicant itself, it is also not covered by (b) which covers construction of a new building intended primarily for commerce and industry and does not cover construction of a new building. Item (c) of sub-clause (zzzza) of clause (105) covers ‘construction of a new residential complex or a part thereof’.

2. As per the draft of the works contract submitted, it is clear that such contracts will be for construction of individual houses on sub-plots located within the plot owned by the applicant on which the applicant proposes to develop a residential housing project. As per the applicant’s own narration, the residential project to be constructed on this plot would have at least 12 residential units, a club house and other common facilities and the layout of the project would be approved by the prescribed authority under the relevant law in force. Such a project constructed as per activity Nos. 3 and 4 squarely conforms to the definition of a ‘residential complex’ given in clause (91a) of section 65, and the individual houses constructed get covered under the definition of a ‘residential unit’ contained therein. Execution of the works contract, thus, involves construction of a part of a new ‘residential complex’ and is covered by (c).

8. Section 7 CGST defines supply in an inclusive manner meaning it is a widened and broadened connotation. Essentially, a flat under construction and intended to be sold to a buyer is sale of immovable property, but when it is undergoing construction there is an element of service and consequently, it was necessary to treat construction of flats as a supply of service vide Section 7(1)(d) read with item no 5(b) of Schedule II. 9. Schedule of Goods and Service Tax rates for services approved by GST Council laying down fitment of rates of services states at entry 19 that "Construction of a complex, civil structure or part thereof intended for sale to a buyer wholly or partly" will bear GST at 12.5% with full input tax credit, but no refund of overflow of input tax credit. The entry also explains that the value of land is included in the amount charged from the service recipient. Simultaneously, rate of GST for composite works contract as defined in Section 2(119) vide entry 27 is 18% with full input tax credit. In substance and effect, though construction of flat is treated as a service yet it is akin to a works contract. Drawing such a cue implies that concession of 6% is given to factor in value of land thereby leading to a calculation of 33% of abatement on the total consideration. However, prescription of such a standard rate of abatement [assumed] does not take into realities of cheap, medium, semi-luxury, luxurious and elite segments where composition of land value would considerably vary. Moreover, in semi-rural developing towns, presumed rate of 33% in respect of land value may be on higher side leading to excess input credit over 12% output tax inasmuch as input supplies for builders mostly carry a rate of 18% to 28% which as per schedule of rates as seen above is not refundable. In cases, where input tax credit falls short of GST rate of 12% profits of builders will truncate or lead passing of burden on to consumers. In my opinion, this matters ought to have been formulated by the legislature in a flexible manner through a methodology by way of rules to reckon local factors.

10. Another daunting controversy that may arise is whether the overflow of input tax credit is to be worked per project or on a net basis for all projects put together. Section 16 of CGST provides that every person shall subject to such terms and conditions as may be prescribed and in the manner specified in Section 49 be entitled to the credit of any input tax in respect of any supply of goods and services or both to him which are used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of his business and the amount shall be credited to the electronic ledger of such person. In my opinion, looking at the wording of Section 16 aforesaid read with Section 17 better view appears to be that an overall picture of all projects will have to be undertaken and not project wise. No guidance is found either in the Act or the relevant rules as what are the implications of GST in a case when a project undertaken by the builder where he has to give flats to the owner of land in discharge of consideration for obtaining development rights. Assuming in a particular case, the developers have to provide 100 flats to owners and there other 200 flats for free sale; in former case he will be a contractor levying GST at 18% with input tax credit, whereas in the latter case, the rate would be 12% with full input tax credit but no refund of overflow credit in a situation where flats are sold before they are fully developed. In the aforementioned example, there can controversy as to how the overflow of input tax credit to be computed being the difference between the rate of GST on input supplies and 18% GST rate more particularly, after considering common input supplies and capital goods employed for both types of flats. Moreover, disputes will arise as to what is time of supply of the 100 units to be allotted to owners more specifically, if land is not parted physically at one go, but in stages. Can we say the supply of flats is complete when possession of land is given despite the fact that flats are yet to be constructed? If the free sale flats are sold in stages question will emanate as to whether input tax credit is to be accumulated or can be claimed while construction is progressing without any sale? It would be best to issue clarifications on these and other potential roadblocks that may lead to avoidable litigation.

CONSTRUCTION NOT IN RESPECT OF RAILWAYS - TAXABLE

1. Our company has executed works contract for Central Rail Side Warehousing Corporation Ltd. (CRWC) at Ranchi (Jharkhand). The nature of works is construction, erection and installation of PEB structures of steel and incidental works for warehouse complex. The period of contract executed is 1st April, 2007 to 31st March, 2012. The service tax department is asking for payment of service tax for the contract value of this work of say Rs. 1 crore.

We understand that Railways is exempted from service tax. The definition of railways as given in the Railways Act includes its warehouses. So, our company should not be liable to service tax on such works contract of construction, erection and installation of warehouses. Use of the warehouses is not exempted but construction of railway warehouses is exempted.

Constitution of CRWC is as follows: Indian Railways have entered into a MOU with the Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC) as its strategic partner for development of integrated railside warehouse complexes. CWC has created a SPV as its subsidiary, named as CRWC with the sole purpose of developing railside warehousing complexes (not other complexes). The Indian Railways has provided land near various railway terminals and the CRWC has constructed and erected railway warehousing complexes on the land by contracting with our company. Indian Railway will get its share of profit by way of profit sharing from CRWC.

Kindly enlighten us whether the stand of the company is correct that construction of railside warehousing by Indian Railways in partnership with CRWC should not be taxable.

Railway is defined in section 2(31) of the Railways Act, 1989; the same is reproduced below -

"railway" means a railway, or any portion of a railway, for the public carriage of passengers or goods, and includes-

"(a)

all lands within the fences or other boundary marks indicating the limits of the land appurtenant to a railway;

(b)

all lines of rails, sidings, or yards, or branches used for the purposes of, or in connection with, a railway;

(c)

all electric traction equipments, power supply and distribution installations used for the purposes of, or in connection with, a railway;

(d)

all rolling stock, stations, officers warehouses, wharves, workshops, factories, fixed plant and machinery, roads and streets, running rooms, rest houses, institutes, hospitals, water works and water supply installations, staff dwellings and any other works constructed for the purpose of, or in connection with, railway;

(e)

all vehicles which are used on any road for the purposes of traffic of a railway and owned, hired or worked by a railway; and

(f)

all ferries, ships, boats and rafts which are used on any canal, river, lake or other navigable inland waters for the purposes of the traffic of a railway and owned, hired or worked by a railway administration,

but does not include-

(i)

a tramway wholly within a municipal area; and

(ii)

lines of rails built in any exhibition ground, fair, park or any other place solely for the purpose of recreation.

The relevant taxable services, viz., Commercial construction services and works contract services exclude services/works contracts in respect of roads, airports, railways, transport terminals, bridges, tunnels and dams.

The query can be answer solely on basis of clause (d) of the definition, as it lists various places to be considered as 'railways'.

Services provided by railway include transport of passengers and goods and, constructions necessary therefor are covered by the term 'railways'. The words "officers warehouses"... "rest houses"... "any other works" … "for the purpose of railways" or "in connection with railways" are wide enough to cover warehouses meant for storage of goods transported by the railways.

If that is the case, the services will be considered as having been provided in respect of construction of warehouse for use of the railways.

However, construction of warehouses meant for commercial use by railways and not for use of railways will not be covered under 'railways' and services provided would be not considered as 'in respect of' railways.

Please note that the services must be provided "in respect of" railways and not merely "to" railways.

Hence, it appears that the services provided by your client would be liable to service tax.

On basis of various suggestions received, fresh model laws have been released by GST Council Secretariat on 26-11-2016. Following three drafts have been released—

1.

Model GST Law

2.

Model IGST Law

3.

Draft Goods and Service Tax (Compensation to the States for Loss of Revenue) Bill, 2016

Many changes have been made compared to earlier draft. It is heartening to note that many suggestions from trade and industry have been considered and suitable changes have been made.

These drafts have already been discussed at officers' level. Now, these will be placed before GST Council which is scheduled to meet on 2-12-2016. Finishing touches may be given in the meeting.

After approval of GST Council, the Bill will be presented before Parliament in week commencing on 5-12-2016.

If all goes well, the Bills may be passed in winter 2016 session of Parliament and the GST will see light of day on 1-4-2017. Of course there are many slips between cup and the lip.

Detailed write up is attached. The highlights of major changes vis-à-vis Model Laws released in June, 2016 are given below.

Ceiling on GST Rates

The new Model Law specifies ceiling on GST rates as follows - SGST - 14%, CGST - 14% and IGST - 28%.

Of course, this ceiling is illusory as section 8 of GST (Compensation to the States for Loss of Revenue) Bill, 2016 makes provision for levy and collection of GST Compensation Cess on supplies of goods and services. This cess will be non-vatable.

Thus, all what is achieved by GST can be lost through such cess. Only solace is that this cess can be levied by Central Government and not individual State Governments.

Definition of 'supply without consideration' pruned and made more practical

The earlier definition of 'supply without consideration' as contained in Schedule I was very broad. It covered transactions which were for private use. This would have created huge amount of litigation, particularly because as per provisions of input tax credit, input credit of expenses not related to business was anyway not available. Thus, this would have created double whammy.

The revised definition of 'supply without consideration' in Schedule I is as follows—

1.

Permanent transfer/disposal of business assets where input tax credit has been availed on such assets.

2.

Supply of goods or services between related persons, or between distinct persons as specified in section 10, when made in the course or furtherance of business.

3.

Supply of goods—

(a)

by a principal to his agent where the agent undertakes to supply such goods on behalf of the principal, or

(b)

by an agent to his principal where the agent undertakes to receive such goods on behalf of the principal.

4.

Importation of services by a taxable person from a related person or from any of his other establishments outside India, in the course or furtherance of business.

The transactions between agent and principal will be subject to GST on goods only when Agent receives the goods (like C&F Agency or Consignment Agent). If the Agent is commission agent and does not receive goods, he will be liable only to GST on his commission.

Definition of 'works contract' restricted to services relating to immovable property

The earlier model law was covering works contracts of 'movable property' also. Now, only works contracts relating to immovable property will alone be covered (though first part of definition of 'works contract' still contains the words 'transfer of property in goods is involved in the execution of such contract', which are likely to cause confusion and litigation).

The revised definition as per section 2(110) of new Model Law is as follows—

"works contract" means a contract wherein transfer of property in goods is involved in the execution of such contract and includes contract for building, construction, fabrication, completion, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, modification, repair, maintenance, renovation, alteration or commissioning of any immovable property.

10. India is planning to introduce anti-profiteering measures to ensure that the benefits arising out of GST regime should be passed on to the consumers.

Comments

Key procedural provisions and Definitions

11. Taxpayer is required to file return of his outward supplies in GSTR-1 format. Now, it is provided that the registered person shall not be allowed to furnish the details of outward supplies during the period from 11thto 15th day of the month succeeding the tax period. Taxpayer is required to file return of his inward supplies in GSTR-2 format. Now, it is provided that the taxpayer shall either accept or reject the details so communicated, on or before the 17th day, but not before the 15th day, of the month succeeding the tax period.

A registered person engaged in taxable activity is required to issue an invoice. However, GST law provides that an invoice may not be issued a as tax invoice if the value of the goods or services or both supplied is less than INR 200, subject to prescribed conditions.

Most of the definitions as provided under the earlier Draft GST law have been retained except some changes in the definition of works contract, business, etc.

Our company has executed works contract for the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) by way of supply and erection of PEB structures for six elevated stations of DMRC in New Delhi during 1st April, 2008 to 31st March, 2010. The value of the contract is say of Rs. 1 crore. The service tax department is asking for payment of service tax on works executed for DMRC. The company is of the view that DMRC is railways, and the works executed for railway is exempted in service tax. But the service tax department says that DMRC is not included in railways, as it is a separate corporation from the Indian Railways. We understand that the definition of 'railways' as per the Railways Act is not restricted to the Indian railways. It says "Railways means a railway or any portion of a railway, for the public carriage of passengers or goods." Thus, whether it is DMRC or Indian Railways, both are railways and works contract executed to any of them is exempted.

You may kindly enlighten us whether the stand of the company is right that the works contract of supply and erection of PEB structures for six elevated stations of DMRC is exempted.

As per section 2(31) of the Railways Act, 1989, "railway" means a railway, or any portion of a railway, for the public carriage of passengers or goods. It doesn't include a tramway wholly within a Municipal area.

The relevant taxable services, viz., commercial construction services and works contract services exclude services/works contract in respect of roads, airports, railways, transport terminals, bridges, tunnels and dams.

As per clause (20) of section 2 the aforesaid Act :

(20) "Government railway" means a railway owned by the Central Government;

As per clause (g) ibid :

(g) "railway administration", in relation to-

(a)

a Government railway, means the General Manager of a Zonal Railway; and

(b)

a non-Government railway person means the person who is the owner or lessee of the railway or the person working for the railway under an agreement;

As per the meaning given to it "railway" means a railway, or any portion of a railway, for the public carriage of passengers or goods. Thus, railways may be Government owned or private owned. Even private-owned railways is railways within the meaning of the Act. However, a 'tramway' is excluded.

Further, present section 66D(o) provides that service of transportation of passengers, with or without accompanied belongings, by-

(i)

a stage carriage;

(ii)

railways in a class other than-

(A)

first class; or

(B)

an air-conditioned coach;

(iii)

metro, monorail or tramway;...

shall be in the negative list.

Thus, the present law conceives of 'railways' differently from 'metro or monorail or tramway'.

As per Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, a tram-train is a light-rail public transport system where trams run through from an urban tramway network to main-line railway lines which are shared with conventional trains. This combines the tram's flexibility and accessibility with a train's greater speed, and bridges the distance between a main railway station and a city centre. There is also a train-tram, which is a train modified to run also on tramlines. Generally, the tram-train and train-tram are interchangeable, although a train-tram is based on a train design modified to also run as a tram and a tram-train is based on a tram design modified also to run on a train line.

Hence, it appears that Delhi Metro is a 'tramway' and not a 'railway'. The services may not be eligible for exemption.

[A useful reference may also be made to : http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/Mumbai-Metro-Is-it-a-tramway-or-a-railway/Article1-763834.aspx]

Illustration 2 - M/s. XYZ Ltd. are engaged in carrying out works contract liable to VAT under the State-VAT laws. They had started a works contract on 1-6-2012 and had opted for composition scheme for payment of VAT and service tax both. On 1-7-2012, since the composition scheme stands withdrawn, their works contract (not being original works) falls under rule 2A(ii)(C) of the Service Tax (Determination of Value) Rules, 2006 (value cannot be determined on actual basis under Rule 2A(i) ibid). How should they determine their liability to pay service tax in respect of the said works contract in the following situations -

(i) service provided, bills raised and amounts received prior to 1-7-2012 ;

(ii) service provided and bill raised prior to 1-7-2012, but, amounts received on or after 1-7-2012 ;

(iii) service provided prior to 1-7-2012, but bill raised and amount received on or after 1-7-2012 ;

(iv) service provided, bill raised and amounts received on or after 1-7-2012.

Solution - Works Contract Service is notified as continuous supply of service for which Point of Taxation is determinable under rule 3 of the Point of Taxation Rules, 2011. However, in case of change in effective rate of tax, rule 4 ibid shall apply, as rule 4 ibid has overriding effect.

Under composition scheme, M/s. XYZ Ltd. was liable to pay service tax @ 4.8% of total amount charged, while, w.e.f. 1-7-2012, the effective rate of service tax shall be @ 7.2% of total amount charged (12% of 60% of total amount). This is a case of change in effective rate of tax for which the Point of Taxation shall be determined under rule 4 of the Point of Taxation Rules, 2011.

Accordingly, -

(i) service provided, bills raised and amounts received prior to 1-7-2012 - Point of taxation shall be prior to 1-7-2012 and composition rate 4.8% will apply ;

(ii) service provided and bill raised prior to 1-7-2012, but, amounts received on or after 1-7-2012 - Point of taxation shall be the date of invoice i.e., prior to 1-7-2012 and composition rate 4.8% will apply - Rule 4(a)(ii) of the Point of Taxation Rules, 2011.

(iii) service provided prior to 1-7-2012, but bill raised and amount received on or after 1-7-2012 - The point of taxation shall be date of payment or issuing of invoice, whichever is earlier i.e., on or after 1-7-2012 and new valuation under rule 2(ii)(C) and effective rate of 7.2% shall apply - rule 4(a)(i) of the Point of Taxation Rules, 2011.

(iv) service provided, bill raised and amounts received on or after 1-7-2012 - Point of taxation shall be on or after 1-7-2012 and new valuation under Rule 2(ii)(C) and effective rate of 7.2% shall apply.

POT - CONSTRUCTION SERVICES - REVISION IN ABATEMENT - APPLICABILITY OF RULE 4

7. We are builders and are engaged in providing construction services falling under Section 66E(b) of the Finance Act, 1994. We were constructing a new commercial complex with 20 identical units priced at Rs. 90 lakh each since 1-3-2013. A payment of Rs. 50 lakhs on each unit had already been received up to 7-5-2013 and corresponding bills had also been raised and construction was done accordingly. A part of the construction would be carried out on or after 8-5-2013 and bills would be raised accordingly. We have opted for abatement under Notification No. 26/2012-ST. What will be the service tax implication in this case ?

Construction services provided in respect of non-residential construction priced below Rs. 100 lakhs was eligible for abatement at 75% up to 7-5-2013.

However, w.e.f. 8-5-2013, the rate of abatement has been reduced to 70%. This would amount to change in the rate of service tax and Rule 4 of the Point of Taxation Rules, 2011 would apply accordingly (Rule 4 has an overriding effect over Rule 3 of the Point of Taxation Rules, 2011, i.e., Rule 4 applies even if the service amounts to a continuous supply of services.)

Under Rule 4, to the extent invoice has been issued and payment received prior to change in rate of tax, the rate of service tax would continue to be old one, i.e., 75% abatement would be available. However, in respect of bills raised and collections made, taking place on or after 8-5-2013, the rate of abatement would be at 70%.

In certain cases, where the service has been provided prior to 8-5-2013 and bills have been raised before 8-5-2013, but payment only has been received on or after 8-5-2013, the rate of abatement would continue to be 75%.

POT - SERVICES TAXED FOR FIRST TIME

8. Ours is an institute affiliated to the National Skill Development Corporation. Services provided by us were covered in negative list up to 9-5-2013. In one case, said Services forming part of negative list were provided on 1-5-2013 (Value Rs. 25,000) Invoice therefor was issued on 9-5-2013 and payment thereof was received by way of account-payee draft on 9-5-2013 itself. The said draft was presented to the bank on 14-5-2013 and credited to bank account on 16-5-2013. Would the services be liable to service tax ?

In this case, since payment is received by a banking instrument, Rule 2A would be applicable. Since payment is credited in the bank on 16-5-2013 (after 4 working days from 10-5-2013, being date of charge of service tax on such services for the first time), hence, date of payment = date on which payment was credited to bank = 16-5-2013.

Rule 5(a) and 5(b) of the Point of Taxation Rules, 2011 requires that payment must have been received prior to charge of service tax for the first time, which is not the case herein.

Conclusion

4. A works contract service is defined to mean a contract wherein transfer of property in goods in the course of execution of contract is subject to Sales tax/VAT charge. In the 2007-08 Finance Act/Budget, it is pointed out that specified works contract which attract VAT/Sales tax involving transfer of property are alone to be covered under the new sub-clause (zzzza) and such works contract include erection, commissioning or installation, commercial or industrial construction, construction of complex and turnkey projects.

Thus, persons taking up mining activities on turnkey basis or acting as erection contractor may avail the benefit under the composition scheme notwithstanding sub-clauses (zzh) and (zzzy) in the Act.

SUDHIR HALAKHANDI*

The Finance Minister with a sole motto, ‘when transfer of property involved in works contract is taxable, then why the transfer of services involved in works contract is not taxable’ proposed one more complicated levy of service tax on works contract vide the Finance Bill, 2007. Now the contractors involved in works contract will have to pay service tax on transfer of services. This write-up highlights the types of contract where the levy is attracted, where the levy is not attracted and the composition scheme while making reference to departmental clarification in this regard. The rules of valuation and the composition scheme will be declared later though anticipating the requirement of opting for composition scheme, the law-makers have already disclosed the rate of composition as 2 per cent on the whole amount of contract.

Introduction

1. Transfer of property in goods involved in works contract is taxable under the State tax i.e. VAT or sales tax. This levy under the State sales tax laws was a very complicated levy and the complications further increased on the introduction of VAT. Most of the contractors have opted for composition schemes introduced by the State Governments. The service tax was introduced in 1994 with a sole motto ‘When goods are taxable why not services’. On the same ground the Finance Minister seems to have a thought that ‘When transfer of property involved in works contract is taxable, then why the transfer of services involved in works contract is not taxable’ and, hence, he proposed one more complicated levy of service tax on works contract. Now the contractors involved in execution of works contract will have to pay service tax on transfer of services also. The rules of valuation and the composition scheme in this regard will be declared later though, anticipating the requirement of opting for composition scheme, the law makers have already disclosed the rate of composition as 2 per cent on the whole amount of contract.

Finance Minister’s speech

2. The relevant portion of the Finance Minister’s Speech is as under :

"154. State Governments levy a tax on the transfer of property in goods involved in the execution of a works contract. The value of services in a works contract should attract service tax. Hence, I propose to levy of service tax on services involved in the execution of a works contract. However, I also propose an optional composition scheme under which service tax will be levied at only 2 per cent of the total value of the works contract."

Service tax on works contract

3. The levy of service tax and its taxability is defined and explained in section 65(105)(zzzza ), which is proposed to be added to the Finance Act, 1994 by the Finance Bill, 2007.

This section reads as under :

"Taxable service means a service provided or to be provided :

to any person, by any other person in relation to the execution of a works contract, excluding works contract in respect of roads, airports, railways, transport terminals, bridges, tunnels and dams.

Explanation.—For the purposes of this sub-clause, ‘works contract’ means a contract wherein,—

(i )Transfer of property in goods involved in the execution of such contract is leviable to tax as sale of goods, and

( a)Erection, commissioning or installation of plant, machinery, equipment or structures, whether pre-fabricated or otherwise, installation of electrical and electronic devices, plumbing, drain laying or other installations for transport of fluids, heating, ventilation or air-conditioning including related pipe work, duct work and sheet metal work, thermal insulation, sound insulation, fire proofing or water proofing, lift and escalator, fire escape staircases or elevators; or

A contractor is constructing railway station for Metro Rail Project. Another contractor is installing telecommunication system for the Metro Rail Project. Are these contractors required to pay service tax?

No, these activities would not attract service tax liability. One can rely upon decision of the Supreme Court in the case of Shahdara (Delhi) Saharanpur Light Rly. Co. Ltd. v. Municipal Board, Saharanpur AIR 1967 SC 1747 wherein it was held that definition of ‘railway’ is very wide and would include every structure or mechanical/communication/electrical system set up for the Metro Rail Project through the contractors for this rail transit system and it is not restricted to the railway tracks.

The same meaning should apply to the word ‘railways’ figuring in section 65(105)( zzzza) of the Finance Act, 1994. When the definition of ‘taxable services’ itself states that works contract in respect of ‘railways’ would not come within its scope, it would mean that each and every activity mentioned in the definition which is for a railway system, is outside its scope. Accordingly, construction of station building or setting up of telecommunication system for use in the Metro Rail Project is not subject to service tax under the category of ‘execution of works contract’.

The municipal corporation of a metro city is constructing a multi-storied building. It is to use 50 per cent of the space in the building for civic purposes and would rent the balance 50 per cent to various offices for commercial use. Whether the contractor is required to pay service tax on the construction of his building?

No, this activity would not fall under the category of ‘execution of works contract service’. One can rely upon the decision of the Supreme Court in the case of State of Orissa v. Joginder Patjoshi AIR 2004 SC 1039 wherein it was held that the expression ‘primary’ is used in contradiction with ‘secondary’. The main objective is referred to primary and a subsidiary objective as secondary. The thing which comes first is primary. For example, the primary education is followed by secondary education.

The municipal corporation will use civic centre primarily for its activities in the role of a civic body. It is only when there is space left after the purpose of municipal corporation is satisfied that it will give such surplus space on rent for use as office. Even, in such a case, it would not give more than 50 per cent of the space in the building on rent. If more than 50 per cent of the space is not given on rent, then it cannot be said that the building is used primarily for renting of space for commercial use. Hence, the building being constructed by the contractor would not be used ‘primarily’ for commerce or industry. Therefore, construction of the building of the municipal corporation is not taxable under the category of ‘Execution of works contract service’.

Whether a contractor who started executing the contract prior to June 1, 2007, is required to pay service tax on the amount received subsequent to this date?

Service tax on execution of works contract has been introduced from June 1, 2007. The value on which service tax is to be paid for a works contract has been prescribed in law. Rule 2A of the Service Tax (Determination of Value) Rules, 2006, prescribes the value which gets transferred in the execution of the contract to the customer, and VAT or sales tax on such transfer are to be deducted from the gross amount charged for the works contract. Thus, the whole of the works contract has been treated as a single transaction, the value of which is the starting point for computation of taxable value. There is no scope for considering the gross amount charged for the works contract to be less than the lump sum price. Therefore, computation of service tax based on a fraction of a contract price is not envisaged in law. For a contract, where execution started before June 1, 2007, it is not permissible to bifurcate the contract to pay service tax on the basis of quantum of activities performed on or after June 1, 2007, while considering the part performed prior to this date as not taxable.

GST on ongoing project/contracts

Construction projects normally last for 3-4 years which is generally categorized as "continuous supply of service" in service tax as well as under GST. In transitory phase of GST, many projects are half-finished from their completion stage which creates lot of ambiguity in minds of businesses and professionals that whether such incomplete projects are liable under service tax/VAT or under GST.

As per section 142(11)(c) of CGST Act, 2017, where both VAT and Service Tax has been paid on any supplies which are to be made under the GST regime, GST shall be payable on the said supplies under GST Act and the person shall be entitled to take credit of VAT or Service Tax paid under the existing law to the extent of the said supplies made in the GST regime.

This provisions specifically provides that if any activity done by a builder is covered under the scope of supply under GST, then GST is payable on invoices issued after 1st July, 2017 and if any service tax and VAT is paid, then amount of tax paid earlier is eligible as credit for payment of GST.

Therefore, it can be seen that on all the advances received by developers in present regime for which supply have to be made in GST regime, GST will be applicable and it would a compliance burden to match invoices with the advances received earlier and their tax treatment.

Other Critical issues and implication of GST on such issues

1.

Valuation of Works contract: Currently, developers have to bifurcate the service of works contract in to "original works" or "other than original works" in Service Tax Law for different valuation provisions. Further, different classifications were also given in different state VAT Laws. In GST, whole service of works contract is deemed as a pure service as per Schedule II of CGST Act, 2017 and accordingly rate of 18% will be leviable on whole amount ending earlier litigation.

2.

Reverse Charge Mechanism: Currently, under reverse charge mechanism in Service Tax, developers have to pay tax as service receiver in respect of many services. Majority of the services on which developers have to pay significant tax in Service Tax are works contract services, manpower or security services, rent-a-cab etc. Reverse Charge Mechanism (RCM) have been continued in GST regime as well, but these services which constituted major portion of tax payments for developers are not covered under RCM in GST and therefore will provide a major relief to Real estate sector.

However, a new concept of reverse charge is introduced in GST in which, every registered person have to pay tax under reverse charge on supplies received from unregistered person. Thus, developers have to pay tax under RCM on all purchases from unregistered person. It might have significant impact in case any developers has significant availment of services from unregistered sub - contractors as amount of such transaction is also very high.

INTEREST ON CREDIT CARD OUTSTANDINGS NOT LIABLE TO SERVICE TAX

5. I am a user of credit cards. I use the same for payment of my utility bills, purchases, etc. Often, on account of one reason or the another, I delay in payment of the credit card outstandings and interest is charged for such delay (generally, no interest is charged when payment is made within due date, but some ancillary charges are debited). While going through my credit card bills, I find that the bank has charged service tax even on the interest amount. I understand that credit card management services may be liable to service tax, but, there can't be any charge of service tax on interest amount. Please clarify.

Interest on loans is excluded from charge of service tax by virtue of negative list entry under section 66D(n) of the Finance Act, 1994. As per section 65B(30), interest means interest payable in any manner in respect of any moneys borrowed or debt incurred (including a deposit, claim or other similar right or obligation).

Interest for delayed payment of consideration of services is excluded from value by virtue of Rule 6(2) of the Service Tax (Determination of Value) Rules, 2006.

In this regard, the Guidance Note, dated 20-6-2012 has clarified that charges for late payment of dues on credit card outstandings are not excludible from taxable value for the following reasons :

(i)

No exclusion under Rule 6(2) of Valuation Rules : Interest for delayed payment of any consideration for the sale of goods or provision of service has been specifically excluded from value by Rule 6 of the Valuation Rules. However, in the case of credit cards the credit extended is not for the delayed payment of consideration for the provision of services. The services in the case of the credit card are by way of levy of issuing charges or the commission charged from merchants, etc. The interest is not for the consideration for the use of the card. Thus, exclusion under valuation rules will not be available.

(ii)

No exclusion under the negative list : Such credit extended will also not amount to loans or advances. Loans and advances are meant to signify amounts contractually negotiated as such (loan or advance) and not merely a failure to pay an amount at the due date. The exorbitant charges have also no relationship with the prevailing interest rate for the same class of creditworthiness and are in the nature of consideration for the services rendered for using the convenience of using the services by way of a credit card and, hence, are taxable.

In a prima facie view expressed by the Tribunal in Canara Bank v. CCE&C (LTU), [2013] 29 taxmann.com 157 (Bang. - CESTAT), it was held that interest on credit card dues partakes character of 'interest on loan' and, therefore, it shall not form part of value of credit card related services.

The said prima facie view appears to be correct view, as 'interest' will fall under section 66D(n), even if rate is exorbitant. The view of the Department appears to be more based on economic sense rather than legal interpretation. The same doesn't appear to be correct.

Accordingly, as far as charge of interest by bank is concerned, you may bring this to the notice of the bank. If the bank refuses to accept this view (which is likely, so as to avoid any conflict and further, because burden is transferred to clients), you may seek action against the Bank or file a claim for refund of service tax paid by you under section 83 of the Finance Act, 1994, read with section 11B of the Central Excise Act, 1944.

In Daelim’s case, it was held that a composite contract cannot be vivisected so as to levy tax on the service component. In BSNL’s case also, the Supreme Court favoured the assessee. So in order to nullify these favourable decisions, this new category has been introduced.

This service proposes to levy service tax on transfer of property in goods involved in the execution of a works contract which is liable to VAT/sales tax and it should fall in the following four categories:

(i)Works contract for carrying out erection, commissioning or installation.

(ii)Works contract for commercial or industrial construction.

(iii)Works contract for construction of complex.

(iv)Works contract for turnkey projects including Engineering, Procurement and Construction or Commissioning (EPC) projects.

Works contracts involving infrastructure projects, viz ., roads, airports, railways, transport terminals, dams, tunnels and bridges are excluded from taxability.

A new scheme of composition only for this category of service providers is also proposed for. As per this scheme, the assessee can pay 2 per cent of the value of the works contract as service tax provided he does not avail CENVAT Credit on capital goods, inputs and input services required for use in the works contract. The other alternative is to pay service tax on the value of works contract after deducting value of materials as per Notification No. 12/2003, dated June 20, 2003. Here CENVAT Credit in respect of input services and capital goods may be claimed. Taxable value for the purpose of service tax will be that value of works contract which is relatable to service provided in the execution of works contract. It is to be determined on actual basis, based on records maintained by the assessee.

Issues: The Legislature has accepted the principle that the works contracts could not be taxed under the basic category itself and, therefore, new category was created. Therefore, no service tax was payable in the past in cases where works contract tax was payable. Even in future, except in case of specified works contracts, there can be no levy of service tax on other admitted works contracts (for example, repairs services).

3. We are builders engaged in construction of residential complex and have got ourselves registered under works contract scheme. But, we are discharging service tax based on Notification No. 26/2012, Sr. No. 12. Please clarify whether our payment is in order and whether we have to register ourselves under construction services with a view to obtain benefit of notification 26/2012 Sr. No. 12.

Your query is replied in following parts :

1.

Classification : The first step is to classify whether aforesaid work is chargeable to VAT in your State. If it is so, it is works contract and in any other case, it would be construction services and liable to service tax accordingly.

2.

Entry 12 : Entry 12 of the Notification No. 26/2012-ST uses the particulars "Construction of a complex, building, civil structure or a part thereof, intended for a sale to a buyer, wholly or partly except where entire consideration is received after issuance of completion certificate by the competent authority", which is identical to the expression employed under section 66E(b) of the Finance Act, 1994. Thus, Entry 12 refers to section 66E(b), viz., construction services and not works contract services, which are dealt with separately under section 66E(h).

3.

If works contract : If the services are works contract services falling under section 66E(h) of the Finance Act, 1994, the service will be valued as per rule 2A of the Service Tax (Determination of Value) Rules, 2006 mandatorily [Two options : Actual basis under rule 2A(i) and Deemed Basis under rule 2A(ii)]. In other words, if VAT is leviable on supply of goods portion, the service would be classified under section 66E(h) and value will be determined as per rule 2A. A works contract service provider cannot, therefore, avail of the benefit of Entry 12 of Notification. No. 26/2012-ST.

4.

If construction service : However, if VAT is not leviable on construction work, then service will fall under section 66E(b) and benefit of Entry 12 of Notification No. 26/2012-ST would be available.

5.

Registration not relevant : The heading/service category under which you have registered yourself is not material. The nature of service is relevant.

22.6 Distinction between construction service and works contract service

There is no doubt that construction contract is also a 'works contract'. However, under GST, distinction has been made between 'works contract service' and 'construction of complex'.

The distinction is that in case of works contract, a customer (recipient of supply of service) approaches the supplier of service (contractor) to undertake construction as per his requirements. In almost all the cases, the land is owned by or taken on lease by customer. The contractor enters into contract with customer and then undertakes construction with his own material. If the material is supplied by recipient himself (customer), then it is not works contract. It is simple contract for work.

In construction of complex, the builder or developer normally does not have any identified customer. Even if he has some identified customers before commencement of construction, he is undertaking construction activity on his own and not on basis of contract with customer. The land never belongs to the customer.

23.1-8 Redevelopment is subject to GST

Generally in re-development project, land is owned by a society, comprising members of the society with each member entitled to his share by way of an apartment. When it becomes necessary after the lapse of a certain period, society or its flat owners may engage a promoter (builder/developer) for undertaking re-construction. Society/individual apartment owners give 'No Objection Certificate' (NOC) or permission to the promoter (builder/developer), for re-construction. The promoter (builder/developer) constructs apartments with same or different carpet area for original owners of apartment and additionally may also be involved in one or more of the following: (i) construct some additional apartments for sale to others (ii) arrange for rental accommodation or rent payments for society members/original owners for stay during the period of re-construction (iii) pay an additional amount to the original owners of flats in the society.

Under this model, the promoter (builder/developer) receives consideration for the construction service provided by him, from two categories of service receivers. First category is the society/members of the society, who transfer development rights over the land (including the permission for additional number of apartments), to the promoter (builder/developer). The second category of service receivers consist of buyers of apartments other than the society/members. Generally, they pay by cash.

In both the cases, GST is payable as in first case, the promoter receives consideration in form of TDR and in other cases, by cash.

23.4 Value for GST when total amount charged includes value of land

When the total amount charged for sale of residential or commercial apartment includes value of land, the tax is payable on total amount charged less value of land. The value of land will be taken as one third of total amount charged.

The statutory wording is as follows -

In case of supply of service specified in column (3), it item (i); (ia), (ib), (ic), (id), (ie) and (if) against Serial No. 3, involving transfer of land or undivided share of land, as the case may be, the value of such supply shall be equivalent to the total amount charged for such supply less the value of transfer of land or undivided share of land, as the case may be, and the value of such transfer of land or undivided share of land, as the case may be, in such supply shall be deemed to be one third of the total amount charged for such supply - para 2 of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate) and 8/2017-IT (Rate) both dated 28-6-2017 as amended w.e.f. 1-4-2019.

For the purpose of paragraphs 2 and 2A, 'total amount' means the sum total of (a) Consideration charged for such service and (b) amount charged for transfer of land or undivided share of land, as the case may be, including by way of lease/sub-lease - explanation to para 2 of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate) and 8/2017-IT (Rate) both dated 28-6-2017 as amended w.e.f. 1-4-2019.

23.4-1 Is the deeming provision in respect of value of land legally valid?

The deeming provision states that value of land will be 'deemed to be one third of total amount charged.

There is no option available to promoter to deduct actual value of land involved in sale of apartment instead of deemed value - FAQ (Part I) No. 36 issued by CBI&C vide circular F No. 354/32/2019-TRU dated 7-5-2019.

Land value as per deeming provision is required to be taken even if actual land value is available - Karma Buildcon, In re [2020] 119 taxmann.com 299 (AAR - Gujarat)- view upheld in Karma Buildcon, In re [2022] 133 taxmann.com 306 = 89 GST 400 (AAAR - Gujarat).

The provision applies even when the promoter enters into two agreements - one for sale of undivided share in land and other for construction of superstructure - Kara Property Ventures LLP, In re (2019) 73 GST 289 = 103 taxmann.com 279 (AAR- TN).

23.1-1 Statutory provisions in respect of construction of complex

Following is 'supply of service' as per para 5(b) of Schedule II of CGST Act.

Construction of a complex, building, civil structure or a part thereof, including a complex or building intended for sale to a buyer, wholly or partly, except where the entire consideration has been received after issuance of completion certificate, where required, by the competent authority or after its first occupation, whichever is earlier.

Explanation.- For the purposes of this clause- (1) the expression "competent authority" means the Government or any authority authorized to issue completion certificate under any law for the time being in force and in case of non-requirement of such certificate from such authority, from any of the following, namely - (i) an architect registered with the Council of Architecture constituted under the Architects Act, 1972; or (ii) a chartered engineer registered with the Institution of Engineers (India); or (iii) a licensed surveyor of the respective local body of the city or town or village or development or planning authority.

(2) the expression "construction" includes additions, alterations, replacements or remodeling of any existing civil structure.

Residential Complex - "Residential complex" means any complex comprising of a building or buildings, having more than one single residential unit - para 2 of Notification No. 12/2017-CT (Rate) and No. 9/2017-IT (Rate) both dated 28-6-2017, effective from 1-7-2017.

Single Residential Unit - "Single residential unit" means a self-contained residential unit which is designed for use, wholly or principally, for residential purposes for one family - para 2 of Notification No. 12/2017-CT (Rate) and No. 9/2017-IT (Rate) both dated 28-6-2017, effective from 1-7-2017.

16.2

Coverage of 'works contract' under service tax

For purpose of service tax, the term 'works contract' has been defined as follows—

'"Works contract" means a contract wherein transfer of property in goods involved in the execution of such contract is leviable to tax as sale of goods and such contract is for the purpose of carrying out construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, alteration of any movable or immovable property or for carrying out any other similar activity or a part thereof in relation to such property - section 65B(54) of Finance Act, 1994 as introduced w.e.f. 1-7-2012.'

Coverage of services under works contract service - Though the definition of works contract under service tax and CST/State Vat Acts are quite different, practically most of the works contracts taxable under State Vat laws will get covered under service tax also. This is because definition of 'works contract' under service tax covers wide range of activities relating to both movable and immovable property.

This view has also been expressed in para 6.8.6 of CBE&C's 'Taxation of Services : An Education Guide' published on 20-6-2012.

Thus, following will get covered under this definition :

(a)

Erection, commissioning or installation of plant, machinery, equipment or structures

(b)

Construction of buildings and civil structures

(c)

turnkey projects

(d)

maintenance services relating to goods where goods and service both are involved as composite contract (e.g. Annual Maintenance Contracts)

(e)

Job work (which does not amount to manufacture) where job worker uses some of his own material (which may be even minor) [Job work will get covered under the term 'alteration']

Departmental clarification - Laying of pipeline or conduit, erection, commissioning of machinery, equipment and structures, painting of building, renovation of building, flooring, repairs of building would be covered under 'works contract' - Paras 5.8.2 to 5.8.6 of Annexure A of MF(DR) TRU DO F. No. 334/1/2012-TRU dated 16-3-2012.

The circular stated that works contract will not cover 'tailoring or development of photograph'. However, in view of revised definition of 'works contract' under service tax law w.e.f. 1-7-2012, even tailoring or development of photograph will come under 'works contract' service.

State Vat/CST should be payable - One basic requirement is that the activity should be subject to tax as sale of goods. (The activity may be relating to movable or immovable property)

Laying of pipeline is not erection and commissioning service - Pipeline is not a plant, machinery, equipment or structure. The activity is not taxable as erection, installation and commissioning service - CCE v. Surindra Engineering (2015) 79 VST 436 (CESTAT).

In Indian Hume Pipe Co. Ltd. v. CCE (2008) 16 STT 136 = 26 VST 63 (CESTAT), assessee was manufacturing and supplying pre-stressed concrete pipes for water supply. He also undertook contract for construction of pipeline by excavation, conveying and lowering pipes and joining material, laying to proper grade and alignment, refilling trenches, construction of air valves. It was held that this is not installation and commissioning service. In case of laying of pipeline, appellant were not undertaking activity of erection of pipeline. The appellant did not set up a pipeline but constructed one. Long distance pipeline is not a 'plant'. - followed in Lalit Constructions v. CCE (2012) 37 STT 687 = 27 taxmann.com 194 (CESTAT).

In Strategic Engineering v. ACCE (2012) 49 VST 381 (Mad HC), it was held that laying of pipes for transportation of fluid is not erection, commissioning service.
