FACT: The applicant is engaged in works contract by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration.

The applicant is seeking Advance Ruling on questions as to what is rate of tax applicable to the composite supply of works contract as undertaken by the supplier (applicant) i.e., whether the GST rate 18 per cent or 12 per cent is to be charged by the supplier? and whether the amendment through Notification No. 20/2017 and 24/2017 to Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 wherein the GST rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) has been notified in respect of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 will be effective from the date of Notification No. 11/2017 and whether it would be in order for the applicant (supplier) to charge GST at the rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) or is the GST rate 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) applicable to the nature of works contract undertaken by the applicant?

HELD: Regarding the rate of GST on the Composite Supply of Works Contract, it may be noted that the rate applicable is dependent on the nature of the supply. The amendments made by Notification Nos. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) and 24/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) have notified different rates for different nature of works. In Notification Nos. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) Entry No. (iii) of the Notification has specified the recipient of the supply for which the rate is applicable. Entry Nos. (iv) and (v) are for specific type of supply within the four corners of a Composite Supply of Works Contract.

Again, in Entry No. (vi) in Notification No. 24/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), service as well as the recipient has been specified.

Thus the notifications clearly state the rate applicable on satisfaction of twin condition of the nature of the supply and the recipient.

The applicant has neither given the particulars of the specific nature of the work done by the applicant nor the particulars of the recipient of the supply. Copies of work orders are also not on record. Therefore, in the absence of the relevant and necessary information, the first query of the applicant relating to the rate of tax applicable to the Composite Supply of Works Contract provided by the applicant cannot be answered. FACT: The applicant is carrying on business in the housing and construction sector. They are engaged in providing services of construction including materials and labour as per the tender requirements. They have received a work order from Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre for the construction of a building for space transportation system. It is a composite contract which includes supply of materials as well as service. They have also received another work order from a Public Private Partnership Company promoted by Government of Kerala, for the development of Medical College, Thiruvananthapuram which includes construction of road, bridges and other infrastructure.

The applicant has requested for advance ruling on the rate of tax applicable for the above works contracts awarded by the Government authorities.

HELD: As per section 2(119), 'works contract' means a contract for building, construction, fabrication, completion, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, modification, repair, maintenance, renovation, alteration or commissioning of any immovable property wherein transfer of property in goods (whether as goods or in some other form) is involved in the execution of such contract.[Para 5]

On a perusal of the work orders and the agreements entered by the applicant it is clear that the services rendered by the applicant clearly falls within the definition of works contract under section 2(119).[Para 6]

Since the services provided by the applicant under both the contracts fall under the definition of works contract under section 2(119) and the services being provided to the Central Government and State Government, the applicant is eligible for the concessional rate of GST of 12 per cent prescribed in Sl. No. 3(vi)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 as amended.

In view of the observations stated above, it is ruled that the services provided by the applicant under both the contracts being composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 provided to the Central Government and State Government by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry or any other business or profession is covered under entry at Sl. No. 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 as amended and attract GST at the rate of 12 per cent [6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent SGST].

HEADNOTE: Classification of services - Supply of materials and erection work - Heading No. 9954 - Madhya Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Applicant, a Government entity, is engaged in construction of electricity distribution lines, sub-stations and other infrastructure, which are meant predominately for sell of electricity in urban and/or rural area - It had awarded work to successful bidder for supply of materials and erection work respectively - Whether contract entered by applicant with bidder for supply of materials and erection work is squarely covered under 'works contract services' and falls under Heading No. 9954 and applicable rate of tax is 18 per cent (9 per cent under CGST Act and 9 per cent under SGST Act) - Held, yes [Para 7.8]CGST/Madhya Pradesh GST: Where applicant, a Government entity, is engaged in construction of electricity distribution lines, sub-stations and other infrastructure and it had awarded work to a vendor for supply of materials and erection work, contract entered by applicant with vendor is squarely covered under 'works contract services' and falls under Heading No. 9954 and applicable tax rate is 18 per cent

FACT: The applicant, a Government entity, is engaged in construction of electricity distribution lines, sub-stations and other infrastructure, which are meant predominately for sell of electricity in urban and/or rural area.

It had awarded work to the successful bidder for supply of materials and erection work respectively.

It filed an application before the Authority for Advance Ruling seeking ruling on the following question: whether clause (vi)(a) of Serial No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is applicable on the works contract services received by it and determination of liability to pay tax.

HELD: As per the Memorandum of Association of the applicant, main objects to be perused by the applicant on its incorporation is to carry on the business of purchasing, selling, importing, exporting, selling, trading of electrical energy, including formulation of tariff, billing and collection thereof; to execute Power Purchase Agreements with the bulk supplies, generating companies, Central and State generating stations, regional Electricity Board/neighbouring States/utilities and other entities; to execute agreements for sale of power to other distribution companies and other persons and to coordinate, aid and advise on the activities of other companies and concerns, including subsidiaries, associates and affiliates, engaged in generation, transmission, distribution, supply and wheeling of electrical energy. [Para 7.7]

Thus the projects undertaken by the applicant and all other schemes of the Governments are carried out for business purpose and the benefit of concessional rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent under CGST Act and 6 per cent SGST Act) as per Notification No. 24/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017 read with Notification No. 31/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017 is not available to the applicant on works pertaining to construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation or alteration, which are carried out in respect of projects undertaken by it and all other schemes of the Governments as the same is undertaken for the business purpose.

Further section 2(119) defines 'works contract' as a contract for building, construction, fabrication, completion, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, modification, repair, maintenance, renovation, alteration or commissioning of any immovable property wherein transfer of property in goods (whether as goods or in some other form) is involved in the execution of such contract.

The composite supply of works contract as defined under section 2(119) is treated as supply of service in terms of Serial No. 6 of Schedule II of the CGST Act and the Madhya Pradesh GST Act.

In the instant case, the applicant had awarded work to the successful bidder for supply of materials and erection work respectively. Therefore, the contract entered by the applicant is squarely covered under the works contract and falls under Entry No. (ii) of Serial No. 3 of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended from time to time and corresponding notifications under the Madhya Pradesh GST Act and the applicable rate of tax is 18 per cent (9 per cent under CGST Act and 9 per cent under SGST Act). [Para 7.8]

Ruling

Central Government, State Government, Union territory, a local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity. The said entries prescribe GST rate for sub-contractor services pertaining only to the services provided by the main contractor to the Government/Government Entity which are covered in Sl. No. 3(iii), Sl. No. 3(vi) and Serial No. 3(vii)of the aforesaid Notification No. 11/2017. [Para 18] The entry at Sl. No. 3(iii) concerns with works contract services provided by a sub-contractor to the main contractor where the main contractor is providing works contract services to a Government Entity by way bf construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion of a historical monument/archaeological site, canal/dam or other irrigation works, pipeline, conduit or plant for water supply/water treatment, etc.

The entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) concerns with works contract services provided by a sub-contractor to the main contractor where the main contractor is providing works contract services to a Government Entity by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion of (a) a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession;(b) a structure meant predominantly for use as (i) an educational, (ii) a clinical, or (iii) an art or cultural establishment; or (c) a residential complex predominantly meant for self use or the use of their employees or other persons specified in paragraph 3 of Schedule III of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

The entry at Sl. No. 3(vii) concerns with works contract services provided by a sub-contractor to the main contractor where the main contractor is providing works contract services to a Government Entity which involves predominantly earth work (i.e., constituting more than 75 per cent of the value of the works contract) provided to the Central Government, State Government, Union territory, local authority, a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity. [Para 19]

In the instant case, the applicant has sought advance ruling only in respect of a situation where the main contractor is providing works contract services in respect of construction/widening of roads for NHAI, which are not covered by entries at Sl. No. 3 (iii), (vi) and (vii) but are covered only under entry at Sl. No. 3(iv). Moreover before amendment of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 vide Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 introducing specific entry on rate of services provided by the sub-contractor to main contractor, the activity of the applicant was covered under scope of Sl. No. 3(iv) of the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended), which provides the rate of GST on the services supplied by way of construction of road/bridges. Thus the services provided by the applicant as sub-contractor to principal contractor continues to be covered under Serial No. 3(iv) of the principal rate Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. [Para 20]

Ruling

The services pertaining to construction, erection, commissioning and completion of bridges provided by the applicant as a sub-contractor in respect of construction contract pertaining to construction/widening of roads for the National Highways Authority of India fall under the scope of Sl. No.3(iv) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended) and attract GST at the rate of 12 per cent (CGST 6 per cent + SGST 6 per cent). [Para 21]

Work Contract Services - Composite supply pertaining to railways - Construction service - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Period 2018-19 to 2022-23 - Assessee was a joint venture formed for executing various railway projects in India - Assessee was assigned works contract by RVNL for ‘Doubling of track, construction of roadbed, minor bridges, platforms, buildings, water and effluent treatment facilities, wagon/coach maintenance infrastructure, supply of ballast, installation of tracks and other electrical, signalling, and telecommunication infrastructure’ - During period April, 2018 to March, 2019, assessee paid GST at rate of 12 per cent on above contract - Assessee had discharged taxes at rate of 12 per cent on premise that said contract constitutes works contract services of original works pertaining to Railways covered under Sl. No. 3(v)(a) Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) - Further, assessee was served with an intimation in Form GST DRC-01A - Said notice proceeds on premise that said contract between assessee and RVNL was liable to tax at 18 per cent, instead, assessee had erroneously discharged taxes at a lower/concessional rate of 12 per cent on works contract executed by assessee - Thereafter demand order was also confirmed by revenue for differential tax of 6 per cent - HELD : Expression ‘pertaining to’ employed in said notification with reference to railways is one of very wide import - Use of expression ‘pertaining to’ would show that legislation intended to give an expansive meaning to expression ‘Railway’ - Phrase ‘pertaining to’ has been interpreted in previous Supreme Court rulings as broad and inclusive, covering activities closely related to primary subject - In instant case assessee's contract clearly relates to railway development and expression ‘pertaining to’ ensures that infrastructure projects were aiding railway operations; even if carried out by a subsidiary like RVNL, same would still constitute original work pertaining to railway for purpose of subject notification and, thus, covered under Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of said notification - Thus, activity of assessee would be covered under concessional rate and there was no reason to exclude assessee’s works contract from ambit of 12 per cent rate [Section 9, read with section 73, of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Tamil Nadu Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 16.1 16.2, 17.2 and 18.4] [In favour of assessee]

Railway infrastructure construction - General Construction services of highways, streets, roads, railways, etc - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional rate - Advance ruling is sought on whether civil works undertaken for Indian government enterprise for railways in connection with construction of rail infrastructure for providing railway siding for dispatch of washed and raw coal is eligible for concessional rate of GST at 12 per cent - HELD: GST is applicable at 12 per cent only when service provided relates to construction and in nature of composite supply of works contract and should qualify as original works pertaining to railways - Work undertaken is covered under "General construction services of highways, streets, roads, railways, airfield runways, bridges and tunnels" classifiable under Heading 9954 - Work undertaken amounts to composite supply or cannot be conclusively answered in absence of sufficient evidence - Although it is apparent from work undertaken that it is supply in relation to immovable property, there must also be transfer of property in goods in execution of contract - Work undertaken for RITES qualifies as original works pertaining to railways which will be liable to GST at 12 per cent if same qualifies as composite supply of works contract [Chhattisgarh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 8] [In favour of assessee]   Circulars  Notifications : Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-06-2017; Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-06-2017; Notification No. 01/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-01-2018; Notification No. 22/2021-Central Tax (Rate), dated 31-12-2021

No. 126 of Schedule I to Notification No. 01/2017-Central Tax (Rate) [Para 12] [In favour of assessee]   Circulars  Notifications : Sl. No. 126 of Schedule-I of Notification No. 01/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017; Sl. - Classification of services - Andhra Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Composite supply of works contract services - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Section 2(119), of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 /Section 2(119) of the Andhra Pradesh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant engaged in electrification work of system improvement project for erection of indoor sub stations and their connected lines on-semi turnkey basis under Integrated Power Development Scheme (IPDS) to Andhra Pradesh Southern Power Distribution Company Limited (APSPDCL) has sought advance ruling on applicable rate of GST on work agreement entered into with APSPDCL - It is found that contract with APSPDCL is a single composite contract for supply of works on semi-turnkey basis under IPDS - Further, works have been undertaken by applicant to execute/implement various schemes for constructing substations, providing bore wells, erection of lines and required conductors etc. - Moreover, above works undertaken by APSPDCL are for business purpose and hence, benefit of concessional rate of 12 per cent in terms of Notification No.24/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017, read with Notification No.31/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017 is not available to applicant - Whether therefore, contract entered by applicant squarely falls under works contract under entry No. (ii) of S.No.3 of table of Notification No.11/2017- Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6- 2017, as amended from time to time and applicable rate of tax is 18 per cent GST - Held, yes [Para 6]

No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 till omission of said entry vide Notification No. 3/2022- Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017][Paras 4.5, 4.6, 4.9 and 4.10] [In favour of assessee]GST : Construction of new railway siding is 'works contract' and also qualifies to be 'original works' pertaining to railways; same is taxable at rate of 12 per cent under Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 till its omission

Railway infrastructure construction - General Construction services of highways, streets, roads, railways, etc - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional rate - Advance ruling is sought on whether civil works undertaken for Indian government enterprise for railways in connection with construction of rail infrastructure for providing railway siding for dispatch of washed and raw coal is eligible for concessional rate of GST at 12 per cent - HELD: GST is applicable at 12 per cent only when service provided relates to construction and in nature of composite supply of works contract and should qualify as original works pertaining to railways - Work undertaken is covered under "General construction services of highways, streets, roads, railways, airfield runways, bridges and tunnels" classifiable under Heading 9954 - Work undertaken amounts to composite supply or cannot be conclusively answered in absence of sufficient evidence - Although it is apparent from work undertaken that it is supply in relation to immovable property, there must also be transfer of property in goods in execution of contract - Work undertaken for RITES qualifies as original works pertaining to railways which will be liable to GST at 12 per cent if same qualifies as composite supply of works contract [Chhattisgarh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 8] [In favour of assessee]GST : Where works were undertaken for Indian government enterprise for railways namely, RITES qualifies as original work pertaining to railways, GST at 12 per cent will be available if said work qualifies as composite supply of works contract

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Heading No. 9954 [Construction Services] - Applicant a Private Limited Company entered into a works contract agreement with National Centre for Biological Sciences(NCBS) for construction of Hostel building at NCBS Campus in Bangalore - It sought advance ruling on whether it should charge GST at rate of 12 per cent for service provided to NCBS as per Notification No 24/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 21-9-2017- It is found that NCBS, which is a separate centre of Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR), receives grant from Department of Atomic Energy, Government of India and that NCBS is neither set-up by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature nor was established by any Government, but is an autonomous body under aegis of TIFR - Moreover, council administering this institute has only 4 members appointed by Government and therefore Government does not have more than 90 per cent control over it - Thus, NCBS is not covered under definition of a 'Government Entity' as per clause (x) of para 4 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax(Rate) dated 28-6-2017 - Furthermore, Institute is not established to carry out a function entrusted by Government, thus, it is not covered by clause (vi) of serial no. 3 of Notification - Whether therefore, service supplied by applicant to NCBS is not taxable at concessional rate of 12 per cent and is taxable at 18 per cent under residual item no. (xii) of Serial No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Paras 5 and 6]GST: Works contract service provided by applicant to National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS) for construction of hostel building on campus is taxable at 18 per cent GST under residual item no. (xii) of Serial No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017- Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017

Works contract service to government entity - IT tower construction - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional rate - Service recipient is wholly owned by Government of Telangana and it qualifies as Government entity - Works contract services provided to government entity is subject to GST of 12 per cent in terms of entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax(Rate) - Memorandum of Association of Telangana State Infrastructure Corporation (TSIIC) states that company pursues objectives to implement incentive schemes formulated by Government of Telangana - IT towers constructed are meant for commerce/industry or any other business - Works contract service by way of construction of IT towers for TSIIC falls under exception to entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax(R) as structure is meant for commerce/industry or any other business - GST is payable at 18 per cent on works contract service provided [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Telangana Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 7] [In favour of revenue]GST : Concessional GST rate of 12 per cent is not applicable on works contract service of construction of IT towers for Government entity as it is meant for commerce/industry; GST is payable at 18 per cent

Slum infrastructure - Construction service - Works contract service for State Slum Development Board - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Construction of houses and infrastructure in slums for Karnataka Slum Development Board under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana as a main contractor are liable to 12 per cent GST till 17-7-2022, in terms of Sl. No. 3(iv)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended by Notification Nos. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017 and 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 and thereafter, such services are liable to 18 per cent GST in terms of Sl. No. 3(xii) of said Notification as amended by Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 - Such services when rendered as a sub-contractor, are not covered under Sl. No. 3(ix) and liable to 18 per cent GST in terms of Sl. No. 3(xii) of said Notification [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10 to 12 and 16 to 18]GST : Construction of houses and infrastructure in slums for State Slum Development Board under Government Scheme as a main contractor is liable to 12 per cent GST till 17-7-2022 and thereafter, to 18 per cent GST; however, these services when provided by sub-contractor are also liable to 18 per cent GST  GST : Construction services provided to State Housing Board with respect to construction of Police Station as a main contractor/sub-contractor are liable to 18 per cent GST  GST : Construction services provided to a SPV of State Government and Municipal Corporation, for development of market under smart city project are liable to 18 per cent GST irrespective of whether such services are provided by main contractor or sub-contractor

Construction of Roads and Bridges - Construction Services - Heading 9954 - Classification - Applicant is a contractor engaged in construction of roads and bridges - Applicant seeks advance ruling on what is GST rate on works contract services provided by a Government Contractor to KSTP, construction of Roads and bridges for public use?- Held : In instant case, recipient of applicant i.e., Kerala State Transport Project (KSTP) is a wing constituted under Kerala Public Works Department was to execute externally aided projects and specialized projects - Main aim of this wing is upgradation of State highway roads - Strategic option study made for upgradation of State highways and major district roads led to formation of KSTP under Kerala Public Works Department - Government had accepted study report and accorded administrative sanction for upgradation of 1719.46 kilometers of roads vide GO (MS). 142/97/PWD dated 22-12-1997 of Public Works (D) Department, Government of Kerala through KSTP with aid of World Bank - Hence, works contract services provided by applicant to KSTP by way of construction of roads and bridges is for use of general public - As such, rate of tax for works contract services provided by applicant to KSTP by way of construction of roads and bridges for public use will be taxable at 12 per cent (CGST at rate 6 per cent and SGST at rate 6 per cent) - Further, as per Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 amended by Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022, it is evident that till 17-7-2022, rate of tax for works contract services by way of construction of roads and bridges for public use was 12 per cent (CGST at rate 6 per cent and SGST at rate 6 per cent), if, time of supply as determined in accordance with section 14 falls any date prior to 18-7-2022, otherwise it will be taxable at 18 per cent (CGST at rate 9 per cent and SGST at rate 9 per cent) [Kerala Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 7.6-7.10] [Against assessee]

Works contract services - Government entity - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Kudala Sangama Development Board was established under Kudala Sangama Development Board Act, 1994 - More than 90 per cent of members of board are from State Government and all administrative expenses of board are covered by grants given by State Government; hence, it qualifies to be considered as a Government Entity - Works contract services executed for construction of International Center and Museum are liable to GST at 18 per cent with effect from 1-1-2022 as per entry No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended vide Notification No. 22/2021-Central Tax (Rate), dated 31-12-2021 and Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 [Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10.2 and 14] [In favour of revenue]

Works contract service - Services provided to government entity - IT tower construction - Heading No. 9954 - Concessional rate - Service recipient Telangana State Infrastructure Corporation Limited (TSIIC) is wholly owned by Government of Telangana and qualifies as government entity - Works contract services provided to government entity is subject to GST of 12 per cent in terms of entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) - Memorandum of Association of TSIIC states that company pursues objectives to implement incentive schemes formulated by Government of Telangana - IT towers constructed are meant for commerce/industry or any other business - Works contract service by way of construction of IT towers for TSIIC falls under exception to entry at Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT(R) as structure is meant for commerce/industry or any other business - GST is payable at 18 per cent on works contract service provided [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Telangana Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 7] [In favour of revenue]GST : Concessional GST rate of 12 per cent is not applicable on works contract service of construction of IT towers for government entity as it is meant for commerce/industry; GST is payable at 18 per cent

Work contract - Composite supply - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - GST rate on composite supply of works contract as defined in section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 is 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent CGST) till 21-8-2017 as stipulated under 'Sl.No. 3, Heading No. 9954' of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax(Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Thereafter, GST Rate on composite supply of works contract is 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent CGST) from 22-8-2017 as per 'Sl.No. 3, Heading No. 9954' of Notification No. 20/2017-Centrai Tax(Rate), dated 22-8-2017 - Legislation presumed not to be intended to have retrospective operation unless expressly provided - Thus, amendment to Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, made vide Notification No. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017 and Notification No. 24/2017-Central Tax(Rate), dated 21-9-2017 is effective from 22-8-2017 and 21-9-2017 respectively and not from date of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 [Chhattisgarh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 5.2(vii), (viii) and 6] [In favour of revenue]GST : GST rate on composite supply of works contract is 18 per cent till 21-8-2017; thereafter, GST rate is 12 per cent from 22-8-2017

Railway track repair and renovation - Construction Service - Works contract services - Heading No 9954 - Classification - Applicant-assessee is a joint venture firm that are engaged in providing works contract services by way of repairing/renovation and other improvements works for railway track for SECL - HELD : Activities of renewal/renovation and other improvements of railway tracks falls within purview of Heading No. 9954 and Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is applicable on aforesaid services and same would be leviable to GST at rate of 18 per cent, as stipulated under Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 lastly amended vide 3/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019 [Chhattisgarh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 5.2.7] [In favour of revenue]   Circulars and Notifications : Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and Notification No. 03/2019-Central Tax (Rate), dated 29-3-2019

Construction of commercial complex - Construction services - Heading No. 9959 - Classification - Applicant-assessee is engaged in construction of Commercial Complex - It mainly undertook work contract tendered by Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation (RIICO) - GST rates of works contract involving construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration rendered to Government or Local authority increased to 18 per cent vide Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax Rate, dated 28-6-2017 as amended vide ultimately by Notification No. 03/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 - Thus, applicant should pay tax in accordance to latter amendment of Notification - Section 9 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Rajasthan Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 [Para 10] [In favour of revenue]GST : Applicant engaged in construction of commercial complex for Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation will be liable to pay GST at 18 per cent in light of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended ultimately by Notification No. 03/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Supply and installation - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFFCCIL) has awarded a contract to one 'A' (main contractor) for performance of works relating to design, construction, supply, installation, testing and commissioning of electrification, signaling, telecommunication and associated works of double track railways lines under construction for Bhaupur-Khurja section - 'A' (main contractor) has subcontracted performance of certain works and services of main contract to applicant - Whether contract work of applicant to main contractor is covered under Entry No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and liable to tax at 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST or 12 per cent IGST) with effect from 22-8-2017 - Held, yes [Paras 4.10 and 5][In favour of assessee]GST: Where Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited has awarded a contract to one 'A' (main contractor) for performance of works relating to railways and 'A' has sub-contracted performance of certain works and services of main contract to applicant, contract work of applicant to main contractor is covered under Entry No. 3(v) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

Works contract services - Government entity - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Works of construction of Airport Terminal Buildings/facilities and associated works awarded by Public Works Department of Government of Karnataka, are work supplied to State Government – However, said works for construction of airport terminal building or airport are predominantly meant for commerce and, hence, are not covered under Entry 3(iii),(vi),(ix) and (x) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Said works are covered under entry 3(xii) liable to 18 per cent tax [Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10.4 and 14] [In favour of revenue]

Classification of services - Rajasthan Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract service - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Section 2(119) of the Central Goods And Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Rajasthan Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Nuclear Fuel Complex (NFC) had awarded contract to applicant for civil, structural and PH works for plant and non-plant buildings (both RCC and Pre-Engineered Buildings) along with other allied structures for PFFF  ZFF facilities at Nuclear Fuel Complex - Whether activity of manufacture of fuel from NFC is leading to ultimate production and distribution of electricity which is a commercial activity and, thus, supply provided by applicant to NFC is a works contract service (construction service) falling at Serial No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and will attract GST at rate of 18 per cent (SGST 9 per cent + CGST 9 Per cent) - Held, yes [Paras 5 and 6] [In favour of revenue]GST : Supply of works contract service to Nuclear Fuel Complex for manufacture of fuel which is a commercial activity is taxable at rate of 18 per cent GST

Classification of services - Rajasthan Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Erection, Commissioning of Electricity Infrastructure - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services)/Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Rajasthan Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Applicant is engaged in business of supply of material and services of erection, testing and commissioning of supplied material in relation to electricity infrastructure - AVVNL which provides Rural Electricity Infrastructure for household electrification awarded contract for erection of lines, erection of single phase 11KV sub-station and release of BPL domestic connections to applicant - Applicant seeks clarification on two questions as to whether contract entered into with AVVNL for supply, erection, testing and commissioning of materials/equipments for providing rural electricity infrastructure qualifies as a supply for work contract under section 2(119) and whether such supply, would be taxable at rate of 12 per cent in terms of Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Whether work undertaken by applicant of supply of materials/equipments and erection, testing and commissioning of materials/equipments in building of rural electricity infrastructure is a composite supply of works contract - Held, yes - Whether though AVVNL is a Government entity but it is engaged in business of purchasing, selling, importing, exporting, wheeling, system operation, trading of power, including formulation of tariff, billing and collection thereof and since work undertaken by appellant is predominantly used for or incidental to main activity of AVVNL, i.e., transmission (sale) of electricity, it is not covered under Entry No. 3(vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and, consequentially, is not eligible to be taxed at lower rate of 12 per cent (SGST 6 per cent + CGST 6 per cent) and, hence, liable to be taxed at rate of 18 per cent (CGST 9 per cent + SGST 9 per cent) - Held, yes [Para 6]GST : Where applicant entered into contracts with AVVNL which provides electricity infrastructure for erection of lines, erection of single phase 11 KV sub-station and release of BPL domestic connections, supply of materials/equipments and erection, testing and commissioning of materials/equipments in building of rural electricity infrastructure is a composite supply of works contract and it is not covered under Entry No. 3 (vi)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017 - CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 and liable to tax at rate of 18 per cent

Construction of railway siding - Construction service - Works contract - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Public sector undertaking, Rites Limited has, for and on behalf of Eastern Coalfields Limited, awarded applicant different works in connection with construction of new railway siding - Works undertaken by applicant is in relation to immovable property and involve transfer of property in goods thereby qualify to be 'works contract' - Construction work in connection of new railway sidings undertaken by applicant is to be considered as original works as defined in clause 2(zs) of Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Ministry of Railways, Government of India in its Freight Marketing Circular No. 11 of 2016 issued on 22-8-2016 has also recognized 'private siding' for railway freight services - Therefore, construction of private sidings pertains to railways and is taxable at rate of 12 per cent under Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 till omission of said entry vide Notification No. 3/2022- Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/West Bengal Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017][Paras 4.5, 4.6, 4.9 and 4.10] [In favour of assessee]   Circulars and Notifications : Sl. No. 3(v)(a) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017; Notification No. 1135 F.T., dated 28-6-2017; Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017; Notification No. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017; Notification No. 24/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017; Notification No. 31/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017; Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018; Notification No. 3/2022- Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022; Notification No. 25/2012-ST, dated 20-6-2012 and Ministry of Railways Freight Marketing Circular No. 11 of 2016 dated 22-8-2016

Earthwork - Works contract service - Supply of works contract services involving predominantly earth work to Indian Railways as a main contractor or in capacity of a sub-contractor is covered under entry at Sl. No. 3(vii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) and GST is payable at 12 per cent [Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10 and 11] [In favour of assessee]

Classification of services (NR) - Works contract services to main contractor - Whether sub-contractor providing works contract services by way of construction, erection, commissioning, or installation to main contractor in respect of original contract works pertaining to railways would be covered for concessional rate of GST at rate of 12 per cent as given under Serial No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017 as amended - Held, yes [Para 5] [In favour of assessee]GST : Sub-contractor providing works contract services by way of construction, erection, commissioning, or installation to main contractor in respect of original contract works pertaining to railways would be covered for concessional rate of GST at rate of 12 per cent

Fire-fighting installation with pump house -  Construction of a complex, building, civil structure or a part thereof, including a complex or building intended for sale to a buyer, wholly or partly - Heading No. 9954 - Exemption - Appellant-assessee is a partnership firm and a civil contractor engaged in construction of roads, buildings, civil structures or various other civil works as awarded from various Governmental and non-Governmental organizations - AAR has held that appellant, is liable to pay GST at rate 18 per cent - What will be GST rate for work undertaken by appellant for service recipient under bid - HELD : It is observed that services provided by appellant are covered under Item number (vi) in Column (3) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended - Therefore, said services are liable to attract GST at 12 per cent (i.e. 6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent SGST) during contracted period only up to 31-12-2021, as after that, in Column No. (3) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 words 'Governmental authority or a Government entity' has been omitted vide Notification No. 22/2021-Central Tax(Rate), dated 31-12-2021 with effect from 1-1-2022 [Section 11 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Rajasthan Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para11] [Partly in favour of assessee]

Work contract - Composite supply - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - GST rate on composite supply of works contract as defined in section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 is 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent CGST) till 21-8-2017 as stipulated under 'Sl.No. 3, Heading No. 9954' of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax(Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Thereafter, GST Rate on composite supply of works contract is 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent CGST) from 22-8-2017 as per 'Sl.No. 3, Heading No. 9954' of Notification No. 20/2017-Centrai Tax(Rate), dated 22-8-2017 - Legislation presumed not to be intended to have retrospective operation unless expressly provided - Thus, amendment to Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, made vide Notification No. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017 and Notification No. 24/2017-Central Tax(Rate), dated 21-9-2017 is effective from 22-8-2017 and 21-9-2017 respectively and not from date of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 [Chhattisgarh Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 5.2(vii), (viii) and 6] [In favour of revenue]   Circulars and Notifications : Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017; Notification No. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017 and Notification No. 24/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017

Classification of services - Gujarat Goods and Services Tax Act 2017 - Construction services - Heading No. 9954 - Applicant has entered into a contract for construction of a medical college with HITES which is a Government of India enterprise - Applicant has submitted that it was a sub-contractor to main contractor HITES as it is an executive agency of Central Government - Accordingly, it sought an advance ruling on question as to whether service of work contract provided by applicant as sub-contractor is taxable at rate of 12 percent for period prior to 25-1-2018 when Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 was amended by Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 - Whether GST rate of 12 per cent prescribed under Serial No. (ix) of Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 is effective prospectively from 25-1-2018 - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, service of work contract provided by applicant as sub-contractor is not taxable at rate of 12 per cent for period before 25-1-2018 i.e. prior to issuance of amended Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate) dated 25-1-2018 - Held, yes [Paras 25 and 26]GST : Service of work contract for construction of a medical college provided by applicant as sub-contractor to a Government enterprise is not taxable at rate of 12 per cent for period before 25-1-2018 i.e., prior to issuance of amended Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate) dated 25-1-2018

Works contract service - Government entity - State Industrial Infrastructure Corporation TSIIC being wholly owned by Government of Telangana qualifies to be Government entity - TSIIC works to further policies of State Government, Central Government and Local Government for development of industries in State of Telangana - Construction of administrative building is not meant for commerce/industry or any other business - TSIIC has procured works contract service in relation to work entrusted to it by State Government - Construction of administrative building for TSIIC is taxable at 12 per cent GST - Works executed for Governmental authority or governmental entity from 1-1-2022 shall attract GST at 18 per cent as phrase 'Governmental authority or Governmental entity' is excluded as per amendments [Para 7] [In favour of applicant]GST : Concessional rate of 12 per cent GST on works contract is applicable on services provided to, state industrial infrastructure corporation wholly owned by State Government till 31-12-2021; GST at rate of 18 per cent is applicable to such services from 1-1-2022

Slum infrastructure - Construction service - Works contract service for State Slum Development Board - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Construction of houses and infrastructure in slums for Karnataka Slum Development Board under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana as a main contractor are liable to 12 per cent GST till 17-7-2022, in terms of Sl. No. 3(iv)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended by Notification Nos. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017 and 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 and thereafter, such services are liable to 18 per cent GST in terms of Sl. No. 3(xii) of said Notification as amended by Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 - Such services when rendered as a sub-contractor, are not covered under Sl. No. 3(ix) and liable to 18 per cent GST in terms of Sl. No. 3(xii) of said Notification [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10 to 12 and 16 to 18]  Housing construction - Construction service - Works contract service for State Housing Board - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Construction services are provided to Karnataka Housing Board with respect to construction of Police Station as a main contractor/sub-contractor - Karnataka Housing Board having been established under Karnataka Housing Board Act, 1962 and carrying out functions entrusted by State Government is to be considered as Government Entity as defined under Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 31/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017 and liable to 18 per cent GST in terms of Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended by Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 13, 14 and 16 to 18]  Market construction - Construction service - Works contract service for Government SPV - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Construction services are provided to Belagavi Smart City Limited, a Special Purpose Vehicle company incorporated by Government of Karnataka and Belagavi City Corporation on 50:50 shareholding basis, as a main contractor/sub-contractor for development of modern market under a smart city project - Said company neither being a Governmental Authority nor a Government Entity as defined under Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended by Notification No. 31/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017, construction services provided to it with respect to development of modern market is liable to 18 per cent GST in terms of Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 irrespective of whether such services provided as a main contractor or sub-contractor [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 15 to 18]   Circulars and Notifications : Notification No. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017; Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018; Notification No. 15/2021-Central Tax (Rate), dated 18-11-2021; Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017; Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 and Notification No. 31/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017

Works contract services - Government entity - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Karnataka Residential Educational Institutions Society (KRIES) is formed under societies Registration Act and Government of Karnataka may appoint persons to review progress of society and to hold inquiries into affairs of society and give directions; hence, qualifies to be considered as a Government Entity - Works contract services executed for Construction of Residential school complex are liable to GST at 18 per cent with effect from 1-1-2022 as per Entry No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended vide Notification No. 22/2021-Central Tax (Rate), dated 31-12-2021 and Notification No. 03/2022 - Central Tax (Rate), dated : 13-7-2022 [Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 10.3 and 14] [In favour of revenue]

Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Classification of services - Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Installation, commissioning and fitting out of a civil structure - Heading No. 9954 (Construction services) - Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre, Department of Space, Government of India entered into a contract with Tata Projects Ltd., Mumbai [applicant] for design, realization, integration and commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel at Thiruvananthapuram - Work involves aerodynamic structural and control design analysis, detailed design, detailed engineering, fabrication, procurement, inspection, third party inspection, loading and unloading of material, transportation to site, civil and electrical works, integration of systems, training, documentation, acceptance, testing and commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel - Whether supply under contract can be considered as supply of equipment eligible for concessional rate of GST as per Sl. No. 243B of Schedule I of Notification No. 1/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, no - Whether work of design, realization, integration and commissioning of 1.2m Trisonic Wind Tunnel as a turnkey project will fall under definition of works contract - Held, yes - Whether service provided by applicant to Central Government by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out of a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession will attract 12 per cent GST as per Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Para 6] [Partly in favour of assessee]GST : Where Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre entered into a contract with Tata Projects Ltd., Mumbai [applicant] for design, realization, integration and commissioning of Trisonic Wind Tunnel, supply under contract cannot be considered as supply of equipment and work as a turnkey project will fall under definition of works contract and service provided by applicant will attract 12 per cent GST

Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Section 2(119) of the Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract -  Applicant, a Central Government Department, awarded a works contract to one 'T' for design, fabrication, procurement, instrumentation and control and commissioning of Trisonic Wind Tunnel with Ejector System - Work involves fabrication of machineries, transportation of equipments to be attached to system, construction of civil structure where machinery is to be installed - Whether work of design, realisation, integration and commissioning of Trisonic Wind Tunnel as a turnkey project will fall under definition of works contract - Held, yes [Para 4] [In favour of assessee] Classification of services - Kerala State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction, erection, commissioning, installation of a civil structure - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Applicant, a Central Government Department, awarded a works contract to one 'T' for design, fabrication, procurement, instrumentation and control and commissioning of Trisonic Wind Tunnel with Ejector System - Work involves fabrication of machineries, transportation of equipments to be attached to system, construction of civil structure where machinery is to be installed - Whether service provided to applicant will attract 12 per cent GST as per Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Para 4] [In favour of assessee]  Circulars and Notifications: Sl. No. 3(vi) of Notification No. 8/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, Notification No. 1/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, Notification No. 7/2018 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018 and Notification No. 24/2017 - Integrated Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017  (NR)

Classification of services - Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Construction of residential colony - Heading 9954 (Construction services) - Applicant is engaged in construction of residential and commercial complexes - It has been awarded a contract by Airport Authority of India for construction of residential colony staff and employees - Whether construction of residential colony by applicant attracts GST at rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) as per entry at SI. No. 3(vi)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 - Held, yes [Para 10]GST : Where applicant has been awarded a contract by Airport Authority of India for construction of residential colony for staff and employees, construction of residential colony by applicant attracts GST at rate of 12 per cent as per entry at Sl. No. 3(vi)(c) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017

I. Construction, maintenance, housekeeping and security of goods shed - - Composite and mixed supplies - Heading No. 9954 - Classification and rate - Applicant has been given contract for development and maintenance of infrastructural facilities at Kalamboli Goods Shed as a common user facility through private investment in lieu of share of Terminal Charges/Terminal Access Charges and Commercial activities as permitted for a period of 10 years - Applicant will have to maintain existing as well as developed infrastructure at his own cost - They are also responsible for security of said facility - Consideration for said work would be in form of 90 per cent share in Terminal charges and terminal access charges for all inward and outward traffic dealt at Kalamboli goods shed for a period of 10 years from date of completion of work - In addition to said payment applicant shall have license to erect hoardings for advertisement and to run a catering stall in said premises - Common user traffic facility developed by applicant shall become property of railway administration and licensee shall have no claim to these assets - HELD : Services provided by applicant of reconstruction, maintenance, housekeeping and security of Kalamboli goods shed to Central Railway would not qualify as a composite supply of service - It would rather be treated as a mixed supply of service - Applicant is providing mixed services including works contract, maintenance, housekeeping and security services to Railway and by no stretch of imagination can it be held that applicant is providing services of transportation of goods by rail - Applicant is providing supply of services such as works contract service, repairs and maintenance, housekeeping services and security services to Central Railway which can be considered as a supply of mixed service, with works contract (repairs and maintenance) having highest rate of tax of 18 per cent - Services provided by applicant are appropriately classifiable under Heading No. 995419 (repairs and maintenance) and chargeable to tax at rate of 18 per cent GST in terms of Section 8 of CGST Act [Section  9 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Para 6]GST : Where applicant has given contract for development, reconstruction, maintenance, housekeeping and security of goods shed as a common user facility through private investment in lieu of share of Terminal Charges/Terminal Access Charges for a period of 10 years, said services provided by applicant are appropriately classifiable under Heading No. 995419 (repairs and maintenance) and chargeable to tax at rate of 18 per cent GST  GST : Advance ruling cannot be pronounced on admissibility of input tax credit to recipient of supply as such ruling would not be binding on recipient and further, recipient would not be able to file appeal against advance ruling order

Housing construction - Construction service - Works contract service for State Housing Board - Heading No. 9954 - Classification - Construction services are provided to Karnataka Housing Board with respect to construction of Police Station as a main contractor/sub-contractor - Karnataka Housing Board having been established under Karnataka Housing Board Act, 1962 and carrying out functions entrusted by State Government is to be considered as Government Entity as defined under Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as amended by Notification No. 31/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017 and liable to 18 per cent GST in terms of Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, as amended by Notification No. 3/2022-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-7-2022 [Section 2(119) of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017/Karnataka Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017] [Paras 13, 14 and 16 to 18]

Classification of services - Maharashtra Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Services provided by sub-contractor to main contractor pertaining to railways - Heading No. 9954 [Construction services] - Applicant is providing works contract service as sub-contractor to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways - It executes and undertakes composite supply of works contract - Whether tax rate to be charged by applicant to main contractor would be at rate of 6 per cent of CGST and 6 per cent of SGST - Held, yes [Para 11] [In favour of assessee]GST: Where applicant is providing works contract service as sub-contractor to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways and it executes and undertakes composite supply of works contract, tax rate to be charged by applicant to main contractor would be at rate of 6 per cent of CGST and 6 per cent of SGST

facts.text:
The applicant is contractor with railways and it has been awarded a contract with KSR Bengaluru City Railway Station and service buildings at Bangalore.

The contract includes new works, repair works, addition and alteration to existing structures.

The applicant states that the Railway is considering all service buildings as business/commerce establishments and rate charged is 18 per cent (even for original works) and works related to all welfare buildings (i.e., only colonies) are charged at 12 per cent.

The applicant is seeking advance ruling as regards applicability of GST rate for works contract services doing original works with Railways.

The applicant has been awarded a contract by one Rites Limited, which is a Public Sector Undertaking. Said contract is awarded for execution of works of laying of track as per layout plan, pavement along the track, construction of Admin building, Warehouse, Electrical works and Fire-fighting works, etc. at Khodiyar Gandhinagar, Gujarat. Further contract is involving both supply of goods and services and is a composite supply in the nature of works contract supply.

The applicant sought advance ruling in respect of the following question:

Whether the said work can be covered under clause 3(v)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, i.e., works contract by way of construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works pertaining to railways so as the entitle it for charging rate of GST at the rate of 12 per cent instead of 18 per cent.

The applicant was engaged in providing works contract service as sub-contract to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways. The assessee filed instant application to sought clarification for rate of tax to be levied by it to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways. The assessee submitted that it should be charged 12 per cent GST only and not 18 per cent as applicable in other cases.

The applicant is providing works contract service as sub-contractor to main contractor for original contract work pertaining to railways. It executes and undertakes composite supply of works contract.

It sought advance ruling on the following questions:

1.

What tax rate to be charged by the applicant to main contractor on works contract services pertaining to railways original works contract.

2.

Whether to charge tax rate of 12 per cent GST or 18 per cent GST.

The Authority for Advance Rulings ruled that

-

The tax rate to be charged by the applicant to the main contractor would be at the rate of 6 per cent of CGST and 6 per cent of SGST.

-

The tax rate to be charged would be 12 per cent.

On appeal to Appellate Authority for Advance Ruling by revenue:

The applicant a proprietary concern entered into subcontract agreement with MEIL (Principal Contractor), for design, testing, commissioning of transmission of towers and was awarded subcontract works by the Principal Contractor on 12-10-2018, to execute the substation and terminal bay works.

The above said works were mainly awarded to the Principal Contractor by the state government entities such as Krishna Bhagya Jala Nigam Limited, Karnataka Neeravari Nigam Limited and Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation Limited. The said works have been awarded prior to GST but the same have been amended during the post-GST period.

The applicant has sought advance ruling in respect of the following question:

1.

What is rate of tax applicable to the composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of Section 2 of Central Goods and Services Act, 2017 (The Act), undertaken by the supplier (applicant) i.e., whether the GST rate 18 per cent or 12 per cent is to be charged by the supplier?

2.

If the GST rate 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST+ 9 per cent SGST) as prescribed in serial No. 3, against heading No. 9954 (construction services), specified in Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, is the rate applicable to the nature of works contract undertaken by the applicant, kindly clarify the following related aspects also:

The Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, has been amended by:

i.

Notification No. 20/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 22-8-2017;

ii.

Notification No: 31/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 13-10-2017;

iii.

Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate), dated 25-1-2018;

Wherein the GST rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) has been notified in respect of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2.

If so, whether it would be in order for the applicant (supplier) to charge GST at the rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST+6 per cent SGST) or is the GST rate 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST+ 9 per cent SGST) applicable to the nature of works contract undertaken by the applicant?

The applicant is engaged in works contract by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration.

The applicant is seeking Advance Ruling on questions as to what is rate of tax applicable to the composite supply of works contract as undertaken by the supplier (applicant) i.e., whether the GST rate 18 per cent or 12 per cent is to be charged by the supplier? and whether the amendment through Notification No. 20/2017 and 24/2017 to Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 wherein the GST rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) has been notified in respect of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 will be effective from the date of Notification No. 11/2017 and whether it would be in order for the applicant (supplier) to charge GST at the rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) or is the GST rate 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) applicable to the nature of works contract undertaken by the applicant?

HITES which is a Government of India enterprise and executive agency of Ministry of Health & Welfare, Government of India, floated a tender for the construction of a medical college. Accordingly, the applicant has entered into a contract for construction of a medical college with HITES. The applicant submitted that scope of work included construction of multi storied building including water supply, sanitary and plumbing comprehensive firefighting/protection system, internal & external electrification, HVAC works, Lifts, WTP, STP, ETP, CCTV and security system, solar panel, PA system, EPABX/communication system, LAN system, site development works such as internal road & site levelling, sewer and storm water drainage work etc.

The applicant has sought an advance ruling on question as to whether the service of work contract provided by the applicant as sub-contractor is taxable at rate of 12 per cent for period prior to 25-1-2018 when Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 was amended by Notification No. 01/2018-CT (Rate), dated 25-1-2018.

The applicant is engaged in electrification work in the rural and urban areas.

The applicant for the above purpose also receives work contract services from vendors for supply and erection work under various projects.

The applicant wishes to know whether clause (vi)(a) of Sr. No. 3 of table of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is applicable on the works contract services received by it and for determination of liability to pay tax.

The department submitted that the nature of works contract undertaken by the applicant doesn't come under the category for which the notified rate of tax is 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST and 6 per cent SGST) but it will attract 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST and 9 per cent SGST).

The applicant-company (MPPGCL) is engaged in carrying out the works contract in relation to construction of road, bridges, buildings, civil structures of Government, semi-Government and private undertakings.

The applicant was awarded a contract for construction of 599 flats by MPPGCL.

During the course of carrying out the construction work, the applicant company raised Running Bills (RA bills) for the portion of work completed at a point of time to MPPGCL by charging CGST and SGST at the rate of 9 per cent each, in view of Notification No. 11/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017.

MPPGCL is of the opinion that in the work under reference, the applicable rate of GST should be 12 per cent (6+6), as per Notification No.11/2017 Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017, by treating itself as a Government entity and the work allocated to the service provider is the work which is the work supplied to it by the Government.

The applicant seeks advance ruling on issue as to whether MPPGCL is a 'Government Entity' and whether the work contract service of construction of 599 residential quarters allotted to the applicant company, will be charged under the GST rate of 12 per cent (6+6) or 18 per cent (9+9).

The applicant is a joint venture between Sociedad Iberica De Construcciones Electricas, S.A (SICE), a foreign company incorporated under the laws of Spain and VAAAN Infra Private Limited (VAAAN), a company incorporated under the laws of India.

The applicant has executed a contract with 'NHAI for development of six lane Eastern Peripheral Expressway : ITS (Intelligent Transport System) Installation Project', which includes Advanced Traffic Management System (ATMS), Toll Management System (TMS) and Digital Transmission System.

The applicant has submitted application in which it has sought clarification and Advance Ruling as follows :-

(I)

On appeal:

The appellant as Joint venture associate, has entered into contract with Power grid corporation of India Ltd. ('PGCIL'), one of the major Public Sector Undertakings in the State of Haryana on a Joint Venture (JV) basis along with Siemens AG, Germany as the Lead Partner and Sumitomo Electric Industries Ltd. Japan as another Partner. The contract entered by appellant with PGCIL is for on-shore and offshore supply of goods and services for complete execution of +320KV, 2 X 1000MW VSC based HVDC Terminals and DC XLPE Cable system between Pugalur and North Trichur. The said contract of supply of goods and services is divided into 6 contracts by Joint Venture.

The six contracts cover specific and detailed nature of supply of various goods and services to be executed by members of JV. Out of these 6 contracts two contracts i.e. third and fifth contracts are required to be executed by the appellant as a JV's associate. The Third Contract ('on-shore Supply Contract/Third Contract') provides for supply of equipment and materials including mandatory spares except +320KV HVDC Cable (including some of its associated items) from within India and Type Testing (as applicable), required for the complete execution of +320KV, 2 X 1000MW VSC based HVDC Terminals and DC XLPE Cable system between Pugalur and North Trichur. The Fifth Contract termed as 'onshore Service Contract (VSC part) (NOA-V)' ('on shore Service Contract/Fifth Contract') provides for the subject package, for performance of all other activities inter alia including port handling of the plant and Equipment including mandatory Spares (except +320KV HVDC Cable and some of its associated items) to be supplied from abroad, loading, inland transportation and insurance for delivery at site, insurance, unloading, storage and handling at site, installation including civil works, testing and commissioning including Performance Testing in respect of all Plant and Equipment supplied under both 'First Contract' and 'Third Contract' and any other services specified in the Bidding Documents referred to hereinabove. The scope of work under this contract as referred in the Fifth Contract is as follows:

a.

Local transportation, insurance and other incidental services

b.

Installation charges

c.

Training charges

The appellant is entrusted with the responsibility of delivery of the goods at PGCIL's site. For this, the appellant engages local transporters who issue consignment notes to the appellant for such transportation of goods and issue their freight invoices on the appellant. The appellant discharges the GST liability under reverse charge mechanism on such freight amount being paid by it to these transporters as provided under Notification No. 13/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. The appellant charges local transportation from the PGCIL as per the terms of the Service Contract. However, since the consignment note is already issued by the transporters engaged by the appellant, no subsequent additional consignment note is issued by the appellant. With respect to the local transportation charges recovered by the appellant under the aforesaid contract from the PGCIL without issuance of a consignment note, the appellant sought Advance Ruling on the applicability of tax exemption as provided under Serial No. 18 of the Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

The Advance Ruling Authority observed that the First Contract including onshore Ex-works supply of all equipment and materials cannot be executed independent of the Second Contract which is for the onshore supply of services. The two contracts are linked by a cross fall breach clause deeming that any breach in either of the contracts is to be considered to be a breach of the other contract as well. Thus, it provides the recipient with an absolute right to either terminate both the contract or claim damages accordingly. That the 'cross fall breach clause', settles unambiguously that supply of goods, their transportation to the contractee's site delivery and related services are not separate contracts, but only form parts of an indivisible composite works contract supply, as defined under section 2(119), with single source responsibility. Thus, contracts are in nature of 'Composite Supply of Works Contract', therefore should be taxable at the rate of 18 per cent.
