Hence, the supply of the applicant is a composite supply and this criterion is satisfied. [Para 11.2]

The next criterion to be examined is whether the said composite supply is a 'Works Contract' as defined under section 2(119). From the definition, a work shall be treated as Works Contract if that work is done for land or earth or for immovable property and there is transfer of property in goods involved in the execution of such contract. Immovable property cannot be moved. It cannot be separated from the land or earth. If it is detached it shall have to destroy. In the case at hand, the 'Employer's Requirements, Particular Specifications-4B Telecommunication General Specification' - gives the outline summary of the various systems and sub-systems which are applicable to the Telecommunication scope and the outline description of the works said to be the works of the applicant. On going through same, it is observed that the work involves installation of the individual systems at platforms, stations, other select locations along the corridor and is integrated at the Operation Control Corridor (OCC) at Koyambedu and the Telecommunications Infrastructure implementation is to be synchronized with the civil construction phases. Further the scope of works of the applicant like Public Address and Voice Alarm System, CCTV System, Passenger Information Display System, Office Telephone System, etc. requires installation on specific locations, namely ceiling and the like and these goods once installed, may not necessarily be damaged while removing. The applicant has not established with documents that the works contracted to them are to be executed on immovable property as required under definition of 'Works Contract' given above. The applicant has stated that in the Pre-GST regime, under Service Tax, the applicant being a supplier of Works Contract Service relating to infrastructure project of railways, in capacity of sub-contractor was exempted from service tax and had claimed the benefit of entry 3(v) of Notification 11/2017 - C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 as above. The definition of 'Works Contract' as it existed in the 'Service Tax' law is different from that defined under section 2(119) of GST Act. Under GST, only those defined works carried out on any immovable property is covered under 'Works Contract'. Thus without documentary proof of the works contracted/undertaken like related diagrams/plans/schedules/Pictures/detailed write-up on the works, etc. in the absence of submission of the entire sub-contract agreement, it is not possible for this Authority to conclude that the works are done on the immovable property and once installed, the goods/equipments cannot be dismantled without damage so as to hold that the work undertaken is 'Works Contract' as per section 2(119) of the Act. As the applicant has stated that it will not be possible for them to furnish the entire sub-contract agreement which contains the requisite details, in the absence of the documentation works could not be said as 'Works Contract' as per section 2(119). [Para 11.3]

The other criteria to be satisfied are the supply should be by way of 'construction, erection, commissioning or installation of original works' pertaining to railways, including monorail and metro. Original work is defined in Para 2(zs) of the Notification No. 12/2017 - C.T. (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

HEADNOTE: Section 2(119) of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 - Works contract - Whether work involving repair, maintenance and fitting of railway tracks and also transfer of property in goods in course thereof is a composite supply of labour and goods in nature of works contract as defined under section 2(119) and is, therefore, classifiable under (ii) of column 3 [Description of Service] of Heading 9954 (Construction services), taxable at rate of 18 per cent - Held, yes [Paras 3  6][In favour of revenue]CGST: Works contract service of maintaining existing railway tracks is a composite supply of labour and goods and is taxable at rate of 18 per cent

FACT: The applicant is an enlisted contractor engaged by the Railways for maintenance work of railway tracks.

Applicant wants a ruling on the classification and rate of tax when maintenance of railways tracks is done by it by providing contractor's labour only in cases where the Railways supply materials free of cost and when maintenance of railways tracks is done by them by providing, both, contractor's material and labour.

HELD: The applicant is a supplier of services as per work order issued for execution by the Railways. From examination of the LOA and the annexed Schedules, it is clear that the work to be executed involves repair, maintenance and fitting out of immovable property, namely, Railway Tracks, and also transfer of property in goods in course thereof. It is, therefore, a 'Composite Supply' of labour and goods in the nature of Works Contract, as defined under section 2(119) and is, therefore, classifiable under (ii) of Column 3 (Description of Service) of Heading 9954 (Construction services) of column 2 under serial No. 3 of column 1 of the Table in Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 under the CGST Act, 2017 (1135-FT, dated 28-6-2017 under the WBGST Act, 2017. The services rendered by the applicant are to be classified under SAC (Service Code Tariff) Heading 9954, Group 99542, Sub-group 995429. [Para 3]

The works contract service of maintaining railway track as per the above LOA is, taxable at the rate of 18 per cent under the Serial No. 3(ii) of the Rate Notification. Thus, the applicant supplies works contract service, as defined under section 2(119) of the GST Act, of maintaining existing railway tracks, which is taxable at the rate of 18 per cent under serial No. 3(ii) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 under the CGST Act, 2017 (1135-FT, dated 28-6-2017 under the WBGST Act, 2017). The appropriate SAC (Service Code Tariff) is. Heading 9954, Group 99542, Sub-group 995429. [Para 6]

FACT: The applicant is engaged in works contract by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration.

The applicant is seeking Advance Ruling on questions as to what is rate of tax applicable to the composite supply of works contract as undertaken by the supplier (applicant) i.e., whether the GST rate 18 per cent or 12 per cent is to be charged by the supplier? and whether the amendment through Notification No. 20/2017 and 24/2017 to Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 wherein the GST rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) has been notified in respect of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 will be effective from the date of Notification No. 11/2017 and whether it would be in order for the applicant (supplier) to charge GST at the rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) or is the GST rate 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) applicable to the nature of works contract undertaken by the applicant?

HELD: Regarding the rate of GST on the Composite Supply of Works Contract, it may be noted that the rate applicable is dependent on the nature of the supply. The amendments made by Notification Nos. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) and 24/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) have notified different rates for different nature of works. In Notification Nos. 20/2017 - Central Tax (Rate) Entry No. (iii) of the Notification has specified the recipient of the supply for which the rate is applicable. Entry Nos. (iv) and (v) are for specific type of supply within the four corners of a Composite Supply of Works Contract.

Again, in Entry No. (vi) in Notification No. 24/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), service as well as the recipient has been specified.

Thus the notifications clearly state the rate applicable on satisfaction of twin condition of the nature of the supply and the recipient.

The applicant has neither given the particulars of the specific nature of the work done by the applicant nor the particulars of the recipient of the supply. Copies of work orders are also not on record. Therefore, in the absence of the relevant and necessary information, the first query of the applicant relating to the rate of tax applicable to the Composite Supply of Works Contract provided by the applicant cannot be answered. [Para 7.3]

A combined reading of the provisions of sections 9(1), 2(80) and the Apex Court order in the matter of Ganesh Das Bhojraj leads to the conclusion that the effective date of a Notification is the date of its publication in the Official Gazette. [Para 7.6]

HELD: As per the Memorandum of Association of the applicant, main objects to be perused by the applicant on its incorporation is to carry on the business of purchasing, selling, importing, exporting, selling, trading of electrical energy, including formulation of tariff, billing and collection thereof; to execute Power Purchase Agreements with the bulk supplies, generating companies, Central and State generating stations, regional Electricity Board/neighbouring States/utilities and other entities; to execute agreements for sale of power to other distribution companies and other persons and to coordinate, aid and advise on the activities of other companies and concerns, including subsidiaries, associates and affiliates, engaged in generation, transmission, distribution, supply and wheeling of electrical energy. Further section 2(119) defines 'works contract' as a contract for building, construction, fabrication, completion, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, modification, repair, maintenance, renovation, alteration or commissioning of any immovable property wherein transfer of property in goods (whether as goods or in some other form) is involved in the execution of such contract.

The Government of India, vide Notification No.11/2017- Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, notified the rate of GST applicable on supply of services. Under this notification for heading 9954 the applicable rate of GST is 9 per cent.The said notification has been amended from time to time and till date Five Notifications are issued by the Government of India.

As per Notification No. 31/2017- Central Tax(Rate), dated 13-10-2017, issued under CGST Act, 2017 and corresponding Notification under APGST Act, 2017, Government Entity means an authority or a board or any other body including a society, trust, corporation,

(i)

set up by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature; or

(ii)

established by any Government, with 90 per cent or more participation by way of equity or control, to carry out a function entrusted by the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory or a local authority.

The applicant Contractee i.e. APSPDCL is a Government Company i.e. wholly owned by the Government of Andhra Pradesh. When a copy of Audited Annual Accounts of APSPDCL for the Financial Year 2016-17, is examined, it is evident from the schedule of Equity Share Capital of the Annual Statement that 100 per cent share capital is held by the Government of Andhra Pradesh in the name of Governor of Andhra Pradesh. Thus, based on the above facts, it is concluded that the Government of Andhra Pradesh is having full control over the APSPDCL and covered under the definition of Government Entity.

Now, the nature of work undertaken by the applicant is examined. The applicant is engaged in execution of works awarded by Southern Power Distribution Company of Andhra Pradesh Limited for (1) Construction of indoor substation with control room and civil works; (2) Electrical Works; (3) Providing bore well (4) Erection of 33KV line with 100 sqmm AAA Conductor (DC); (5) Erection of 11 KV line with100 sqmm Conductor; (6) Erection of 33 KV UG cable; (7) Erection of 11 KV UG cable; (8) 33 KV Railway crossing. Furthermore, materials such as Power Transformers, 100 sq mm Conductor and Station transformer will be supplied by the Department. The contract with APSPDCL is a single composite contract for supply of the said works on semi-turnkey basis under IPDS.

Now the works under discussion have been undertaken to execute/implement various schemes for constructing substations, providing bore wells, erection of lines and required conductors etc. Moreover, the above works undertaken by APSPDCL are for business purpose and the benefit of concessional rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent under Central tax and 6 per cent State tax) as per Notification is NOT available to the applicant.

22.3-1 Works Contract is supply of service for rate of tax under GST

Works contract as defined in section 2(119) of CGST Act is a composite supply and shall be treated as 'supply of service' - Para 6(a) of Schedule II of CGST Act.

General rate of GST on composite supply of works contract services is 18%. This is irrespective of GST rate on individual goods used in execution of works contract.

Works Contract is deemed sale of goods as per Constitution - A tax on the transfer of property in goods (whether as goods or in some other form) involved in the execution of a works contract is deemed sale of goods under Article 366(29A) of Constitution of India. [Note that this Article in the Constitution of India is continuing even after Constitutional amendment].

Works contract is not limited to construction - The term 'works contract' is not limited to construction services. It covers all activities relating to plant, machinery or equipment which are immovable.

22.3-2 Works contract service of renewable energy plant and equipment

General rate on works contract services is 18%. If composite contract of supply of goods plus service of construction, installation, commissioning of renewable energy plant is executed, it becomes works contract and GST rate becomes 18% on whole contract. Thus, whole purpose of promoting renewable energy sources gets defeated.

Hence, it is provided that in case of such composite contract, value of goods will be taken as 70% and GST rate will be 5%. Value of services will be 30% attracting GST @ 18%. The provisions are as follows -

No. 3(vi)(a) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 is the relevant entry which prescribes GST rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST+6 per cent SGST) in respect of services provided to the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority, a Government Authority or a Government Entity by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession. Now it is required to examine the question whether the contractee in the instant case, i.e., TSSPDCL falls under the specified categories of recipient viz. Central Government/State Government/Union Territory/local authority/Governmental Authority/Government Entity on not. The phrase 'Government Entity' is defined under the Explanation appended to Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. The same reads as:

'Government Entity' means an authority or a board or any other body including a society, trust, corporation.

(i)

Set up by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature; or

(ii)

Established by any Government,

with 90 per cent or more participation by way of equity or control, to carry out a function entrusted by the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory or a local authority.

It is apparent from the schedule concerning 'shareholding of promoter' of the annual accounts of TSSPDCL that 100 per cent shares of the company were held by the Governor of Telangana. This clear indicates that the Government of Telangana have 100 per cent control over TSSPDCL. Thus TSSPDCL is evidently covered under the definition of 'Government Entity'.

The next issue to be decided in this regard is whether the impugned services supplied by the applicant are for the works which are used for other than commerce, industry, or any other business or profession. As per the details furnished by the applicant, the works undertaken are for execution/implementation of various projects for (i) Capacitor Bank Works in Nalgonda etc., (ii) HVDS-High Voltage Distribution Systems in Suryapet used for agricultural feeders. Thus TSSPDCL is not rendering any non-commercial services inasmuch as it is getting reimbursed for its activity on behalf of its customers. Therefore, this activity cannot be termed as other than commercial/business purposes.

The impugned works undertaken are for business/commercial purposes. Therefore, the benefit of concessional rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) is not applicable to the services supplied by the applicant. Further the services supplied by the applicant are subjected to 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) in terms of Sl. No. 3(xii) of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

Ruling

The applicant is not entitled for the benefit of concessional rate of GST at 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) in respect of the works quoted in application in terms of Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 2-6-2017 or any other concessional rate.

Whether a particular person is a Governmental Authority or a Government Entity is to be decided in terms of the definition adduced under Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 by applying the facts of each case.

The impugned works are used for commercial/business activities in view of the facts and circumstances and accordingly the same are taxable under GST Act.

The applicable rate of tax is 18 per cent (9 per cent CGST + 9 per cent SGST) for the services referred to by the applicant. [Para 8]

Andhra Pradesh State Financial Corporation (APSFC) is a term lending institution established in 1956 for promoting small and medium scale industries in Andhra Pradesh under the provisions of the State Financial Corporation Act, 1951. The functions of the corporation are to launch entrepreneur friendly schemes to provide term loans, working capital term loans, special and seed capital assistance, etc.

The APSFC is established by the Government and the Government of Andhra Pradesh is having more than 90 per cent of control over it. Thus it is covered under the definition of 'Government Entity'. Therefore, the APSFC is a 'Government Entity' for the purpose of GST matters.

The applicant agreed for construction of office building to APSFC, which includes procurement and supply of goods and services for agreed consideration. The activity of construction includes both supply of goods and also services.

Section 2(119) defines 'works contract' as a contract for building, construction, fabrication, completion, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, modification, repair, maintenance, renovation, alternation or commissioning of any immovable property wherein transfer of property in goods (whether as goods or in some other form) is involved in the execution of such contract.

The composite supply of works contract under section 2(119) is treated as supply of service in terms of Serial No. 6(a) of Schedule II of the CGST Act.

The Government of India vide Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 notified the rate of GST applicable on supply of services. Under this Notification for Heading No. 9954, the applicable rate of GST is 9 per cent.

Vide Notification No. 24/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017, Government of India by inserting entry (vi) notified concessional GST rate of 6 per cent for the construction services provided to Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, a local authority or a Governmental Authority by way of construction, erection, commissioning, installation, completion, fitting out, repair, maintenance, renovation, or alteration of —

(a)

a civil structure or any other original works meant predominantly for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession;

(b)

a structure meant predominantly for use as (i) an educational, (ii) a clinical, or (iii) an art or cultural establishment; or

(c)

a residential complex predominantly meant for self-use or the use of their employees or other persons specified in paragraph 3 of the Schedule III of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

The applicant is engaged in construction work of office building for APSFC, which is meant for governance of corporation activities. The applicant is of the view that the use of the said construction (building) is not for any business or so.

As seen from the Annual Reports for the years 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2017-18 as made available by APSFC in its website, it is engaged in providing financial services to industries and entrepreneurs. The income it is getting is from interest on loans and advances and also service charges, upfront fee/commitment fee, sale of application forms, profit on sale of assets, commission on insurance, rent received, etc. Therefore, the activities of APSFC are business activities and not otherwise. The applicant informed that the said building is for use as office by APSFC. Therefore, it appears that the said construction is for office use for conducting business activities of APSFC. Moreover the applicant did not provide any information or documentary proof evidencing that the construction/building is for use other than for commerce, industry, or any other business or profession to be eligible for concessional rate of 12 per cent (6 per cent CGST + 6 per cent SGST) available under Notification No. 24/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 21-9-2017.

In the instant case, the contract entered by the applicant is classifiable under Heading No. 9954 under construction services and it falls under entry (ii) of Sl. No. 3 of Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017, i.e., composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and the applicable rate of tax is 18 per cent (9 per cent under Central Tax and 9 per cent under State Tax).

Ruling

The activity of the applicant under the agreement with APSFC is a composite supply of works contract as defined in clause (119) of section 2 of Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

There is no doubt that the project undertaken by the applicant pertains to an affordable housing project. In the subject project, the applicant will be constructing dwelling units of less than 60 sq. mtrs. carpet area as well as dwelling units having carpet area greater than 60 sq. mtrs. [Para 5.14.1] It is found that common amenities form part of the overall construction service and are always naturally bundled when offered to the customer. Therefore, such services will qualify as composite supply of works contract service, where the principal supply would be, construction services. Accordingly, the rate applicable to the principal supply will also be applicable to common amenities. The word 'housing project' cannot be confined only to dwelling units, it would also include within its fold, other common amenities, structures, etc. Common amenities form part of the overall construction service and are always naturally bundled when offered to the customer. Therefore, such services will qualify as composite supply of works contract service wherein provision of construction services is the principal supply. Accordingly, the rate applicable to the principal supply will also be applicable to common amenities i.e. in respect of dwelling units having area less than 60 sq. mtrs., the GST rate would be 12 per cent and in cases of dwelling units having area greater than 60 sq. mtrs. the GST rate would be 18 per cent. [Para 5.14.2]

It is held that the applicant's case is covered under the concessional rate of 12 per cent (8 per cent GST after deducting value of land), under Heading 9954 (Construction Services), (v)(da) of above mentioned Notification No. 11/2017, as amended since the project undertaken by them falls under the definition of 'Affordable Housing'. The benefit of reduced rate would be available to them only in the cases of supply effected after 25-1-2018 i.e., the date on which Notification No. 1/2018-Central Tax (Rate) was issued and the benefit of this reduced rate would be applicable only in case of amenities pertaining to only those flats which are of carpet area upto 60 sq. mtrs. In case of amenities provided to purchasers of flats which have carpet area more than 60 sq. mtrs., the applicant would be required to pay GST at normal applicable rate i.e. at the rate of 18 per cent GST. [Para 5.14]

Subject project consists of both, dwelling units less than and also greater than 60 sq. mtrs. Benefit of concessional rate is only available to 'Affordable Housing' as already discussed above. The definition of 'Affordable Housing' is confined to dwelling units with carpet area of not more than 60 square meters. Thus, concessional rate available to applicant is only in respect of low cost houses along with amenities constructed by the applicant. The common amenities and areas are a part of 'Affordable Housing Project' and therefore the applicant will be entitled to benefit of concessional rate for the same, only when they are a part of low cost houses, i.e. units less than 60 sq. mtrs. The applicant will thus have to discharge GST at the rate of 12 per cent (after deducting value of land) on works contract services provided for the construction of the units and common areas and amenities, which do qualify the criteria of low cost houses. Since concessional rate would be available only for construction services pertaining to dwelling units less than 60 sq. mtrs. Including common areas and amenities on pro rata basis, construction services including common areas and amenities on pro rata basis, performed by the applicant in respect of dwelling units exceeding 60 sq. mtrs. would be liable to full rate of GST, i.e., 18 per cent. 22.6 Distinction between construction service and works contract service

There is no doubt that construction contract is also a 'works contract'. However, under GST, distinction has been made between 'works contract service' and 'construction of complex'.

The distinction is that in case of works contract, a customer (recipient of supply of service) approaches the supplier of service (contractor) to undertake construction as per his requirements. In almost all the cases, the land is owned by or taken on lease by customer. The contractor enters into contract with customer and then undertakes construction with his own material. If the material is supplied by recipient himself (customer), then it is not works contract. It is simple contract for work.

In construction of complex, the builder or developer normally does not have any identified customer. Even if he has some identified customers before commencement of construction, he is undertaking construction activity on his own and not on basis of contract with customer. The land never belongs to the customer.

23.1-8 Redevelopment is subject to GST

Generally in re-development project, land is owned by a society, comprising members of the society with each member entitled to his share by way of an apartment. When it becomes necessary after the lapse of a certain period, society or its flat owners may engage a promoter (builder/developer) for undertaking re-construction. Society/individual apartment owners give 'No Objection Certificate' (NOC) or permission to the promoter (builder/developer), for re-construction. The promoter (builder/developer) constructs apartments with same or different carpet area for original owners of apartment and additionally may also be involved in one or more of the following: (i) construct some additional apartments for sale to others (ii) arrange for rental accommodation or rent payments for society members/original owners for stay during the period of re-construction (iii) pay an additional amount to the original owners of flats in the society.

Under this model, the promoter (builder/developer) receives consideration for the construction service provided by him, from two categories of service receivers. First category is the society/members of the society, who transfer development rights over the land (including the permission for additional number of apartments), to the promoter (builder/developer). The second category of service receivers consist of buyers of apartments other than the society/members. Generally, they pay by cash.

In both the cases, GST is payable as in first case, the promoter receives consideration in form of TDR and in other cases, by cash.

Introduction

1. Goods and Services Tax (GST) may be Good and Simple for others, but not for the God. Dream of residence for the God is costlier now as GST is payable @ 18% on construction of a religious place. "Dharma" is one of the important pillars in Indian culture and has a capacity to save human from an evil within a human. And this may be the reason why we all respect religion by one way or another way. It can be seen in the history of Indian taxation that religious trusts are kept out of the tax net. However, this trend seems to be unsettled by introduction of GST in India.

Construction of Religious building In GST net

2. Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28th June, 2017 exempts various services. In fact very first entry of the said notification exempts services provided by an entity registered under Section 12AA of the Income Tax Act, 1961 by way of charitable activities and words 'charitable activities' are defined to include advancement of religion, spirituality or yoga. Thus, charitable services provided by such trust are out of GST.

However, services received by a trust are not covered under the above entry and a person providing services to such trust has to pay GST. Construction of a building is a service and construction of temple building is also subject to GST and no exemption from GST is granted for construction of religious place like a Temple, Church, Gurudwara, Mosque etc.

Religious places are being built by non-profit motive trusts and those are dependent on donations and have very limited resources. If GST is payable at 18%, practically 18% less temples will be built in India, due to GST.

In terms of Entry Number 3 to the Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28th June, 2017, in case of construction services 9% CGST (and so 9% SGST, total 18%) is required to be paid. Further, if construction contract is a composite contract, effective rate would be 12% provided value of land is also included in the contract value. Generally, land is not included in the price paid to the contractor who is awarded contract for construction of a temple and hence rate of 12% will not be applicable in such case. Hence, practically, construction of any religious place attracts 18% GST.

Conclusion

3. Construction of a religious place was exempt from levy of service tax under entry number 13(c) of the Notification No. 25/2012-ST. Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) dated 28th June, 2017 is issued as mega exemption notification in GST and it doesn't include any entry which exempts construction of temple from levy of GST. Many entries in the Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate) are carried forwarded from existing Notification 25/2012-ST of service tax. However, for unknown reason, entry related to construction of religion place is not carried forwarded to new notification under GST. This may be intention of the Government or may be unintentionally taxed under GST. Whatever may be the reason, but today, the fact is that construction of any religious place, including Ram Mandir, will attract GST of 18%.

If intention of the Government is not to collect GST on construction of Ram Mandir, some exemption is required to be granted by the Government.

This concessional rate has been withdrawn w.e.f. 18-7-2022. Thus, not normal GST rate of 18% will apply w.e.f. 18-7-2022.

34.5-2 Works contract services relating to construction, erection, commissioning of specified services provided to Government, local authority or Union Territory

There was concessional rate of GST on these services upto 18-7-2022. This concessional rate has been withdrawn w.e.f. 18-7-2022. Thus, now normal GST rate of 18% will apply w.e.f. 18-7-2022.

34.5-3 GST rate of 18% in respect of works contract predominantly relating to earth work provided to Central/State Government, local authority or Union Territory

Composite supply of works contract as defined in clause section 2(119) of CGST Act ,involving predominantly earth work (that is, constituting more than 75% of the value of the works contract) provided to the Central Government, State Government, Union territory or a local authority is subject to GST @ 18% w.e.f. 22-9-2025 [Rate was 12% during 18-7-2022 to 22-9-2025 and was 5% prior to 18-7-2022 - Sr No. 3(vii) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate) and No. 8/2017-IT (Rate) both dated 28-6-2017 as amended on 22-9-2025.

Sub-contractor was also eligible for concessional rate of 12% w.e.f. 18-7-2022 upto 22-9-2025 - Sub-contractor providing service to main contractor who is providing the aforesaid service was also eligible for concessional rate of 12% [IGST - 6%, CGST and SGST/UTGST - 6% each] - - Sr No. 3(x) of Notification No. 11/2017-CT (Rate) and No. 8/2017-IT (Rate) both dated 28-6-2017 as amended on 18-7-2022 and as existing upto 22-9-2025 [now GST rate is 18% w.e.f. 22-9-2025].

However, in case of service supplied by main contractor to a Government entity, the concessional rate was available only if the service has been procured by Government Entity in relation to work entrusted to it by the Central Government, State Government, Union Territory or Local Authority as the case may be. This condition deleted w.e.f. 1-1-2022 as concessional rate of GST for these services supplied to Government Entity has been withdrawn w.e.f. 1-1-2022.

Concession only to sub-contractor and not to sub-sub contractor - The concession was only to sub-contractor and not to sub-sub-contractor.

34.5-4 Main contractor is entitled to partial or full exemption does not mean sub-contractor is also exempt or entitled to concessional rate

Main contractor is entitled to partial or full exemption does not mean sub-contractor is also exempt or entitled to concessional rate -Giriraj Renewables P Ltd. In re [2018] 69 GST 64 = 94 taxmann.com 286 (AAR - Karnataka).

However, in NHPC Ltd., In re [2018] 100 taxmann.com 16 (AAR - Uttarakhand), NHPC Ltd. (Government Entity) was entrusted with work of construction of road by Ministry of External Affairs, Govt. of India wherein funds were to be provided by MEA to NHPC in form of grants. NHPC had sub-contracted the work to PWD. It was held that activity of NHPC Ltd. is exempted under Notification No. 12/2017-CT (Rate) [Sr. No. 9C] - Central Tax (Rate) dated 28-6-2017. It was also held that when original supply of service, i.e., work contract is exempted, sub-letting of same to PWD is also exempt.

34.6 Reverse charge in respect of services provided by Central/State Government, local authority or Union Territory, except railways and post

In case of services supplied by Central/State Government, Union Territory or local authority to a business entity, the business entity is liable to pay GST under reverse charge.

The IGST rate of 18% will apply to banking and insurance services, courier and postal services, gas and water distribution services, legal and accounting services, telecommunication services, R&D services, software.

A contract is entered into by the applicant to do end to end setting up of a solar power plant which includes supply of various goods (such as modules, structures, inverter transformer etc.) as well as complete design, engineering and transportation, unloading, storage and site handling, installation and, commissioning of all equipments and material, complete project management as well as civil works/construction related services for setting up of a functional Solar Power Plant. Accordingly, the contract entered into by the applicant includes end to end activities i.e., supply of various goods and services.

It filed an application for Advance Ruling seeking clarification as to whether contract for Erection, Procurement and Commissioning of Solar Power Plant shall be classifiable as supply of goods or supply of services under the provisions of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 and Rajasthan State Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.

The AAR ruled that EPC Contract for Solar Power Plant comes under the purview of Works Contract as per section 2(119) of GST Act and attracts 18 per cent rate of tax under IGST Act, or 9 per cent each under the CGST and SGST aggregating to 18 per cent.

The appellant as Joint venture associate, has entered into contract with Power grid corporation of India Ltd. The contract entered by appellant with PGCIL is for on-shore and offshore supply of goods and services for complete execution of +320KV, 2 X 1000MW VSC based HVDC Terminals and DC XLPE Cable system between Pugalur and North Trichur. The said contract of supply of goods and services is divided into 6 contracts by Joint Venture.

The six contracts cover specific and detailed nature of supply of various goods and services to be executed by members of JV. Out of these 6 contracts two contracts i.e. third and fifth contracts are required to be executed by the appellant as a JV's associate. The Third Contract ('on-shore Supply Contract/Third Contract') provides for supply of equipment and materials including mandatory spares except +320KV HVDC Cable (including some of its associated items) from within India and Type Testing (as applicable), required for the complete execution of +320KV, 2 X 1000MW VSC based HVDC Terminals and DC XLPE Cable system between Pugalur and North Trichur. The Fifth Contract termed as 'onshore Service Contract (VSC part) (NOA-V)' ('on shore Service Contract/Fifth Contract') provides for the subject package, for performance of all other activities inter alia including port handling of the plant and Equipment including mandatory Spares (except +320KV HVDC Cable and some of its associated items) to be supplied from abroad, loading, inland transportation and insurance for delivery at site, insurance, unloading, storage and handling at site, installation including civil works, testing and commissioning including Performance Testing in respect of all Plant and Equipment supplied under both 'First Contract' and 'Third Contract' and any other services specified in the Bidding Documents referred to hereinabove. The appellant is entrusted with the responsibility of delivery of the goods at PGCIL's site. For this, the appellant engages local transporters who issue consignment notes to the appellant for such transportation of goods and issue their freight invoices on the appellant. The appellant discharges the GST liability under reverse charge mechanism on such freight amount being paid by it to these transporters as provided under Notification No. 13/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017. The appellant charges local transportation from the PGCIL as per the terms of the Service Contract. However, since the consignment note is already issued by the transporters engaged by the appellant, no subsequent additional consignment note is issued by the appellant. With respect to the local transportation charges recovered by the appellant under the aforesaid contract from the PGCIL without issuance of a consignment note, the appellant sought Advance Ruling on the applicability of tax exemption as provided under Serial No. 18 of the Notification No. 12/2017-Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017.

The Advance Ruling Authority observed that the First Contract including onshore Ex-works supply of all equipment and materials cannot be executed independent of the Second Contract which is for the onshore supply of services. The two contracts are linked by a cross fall breach clause deeming that any breach in either of the contracts is to be considered to be a breach of the other contract as well. Thus, it provides the recipient with an absolute right to either terminate both the contract or claim damages accordingly. That the 'cross fall breach clause', settles unambiguously that supply of goods, their transportation to the contractee's site delivery and related services are not separate contracts, but only form parts of an indivisible composite works contract supply, as defined under section 2(119), with single source responsibility. Thus, contracts are in nature of 'Composite Supply of Works Contract', therefore should be taxable at the rate of 18 per cent.

The appellant entered into a contract with Delhi Metro Railway Corporation (DMRC) for supply, installation, testing and commissioning of UPS systems.

Appellant is required to supply the UPS systems to DMRC and to undertake the erection, installation and commissioning of the UPS system at the sites designated by DMRC and separate consideration for supply of goods and services have been provided. The appellant has been raising separate invoices on DMRC for supply of goods and supply of services in the pre-GST as well as post-GST regime, the applicant has been treating the supplies made to DMRC as separate supply of goods and services.

In the pre-GST regime, the applicants were discharging Central Excise Duty and VAT/Sales tax on the clearance and sale of UPS system. Further, the service of erection, installation and commissioning of UPS system was treated by the appellant as 'works contract' service and thus the applicants were paying service tax accordingly.

It seeks to know whether the contract entered into with DMRC for supply, erection, installation, commissioning and testing of UPS system qualifies as supply of works contract under section 2(119).

AAR held that the supply of UPS system made by appellant to DMRC does not qualify as works contract service and, therefore, the benefit of concessional rate of 12 per cent in terms of Sr. No. 3(v) of the Notification No. 11/2017 - Central Tax (Rate), dated 28-6-2017 (as amended w.e.f. 25-1-2018) would not be available to the appellant and, it has been held that even though the supply of goods is made from Maharashtra of the appellant and supply of installation services is made from their Delhi Branch and, accordingly, both the respective registered units have raised separate invoices on DMRC, it would be treated as one single contract between DMRC and appellant. The goods and services are supplied by appellant in conjunction with each other, wherein the supply of goods (UPS) is the principal supply. Therefore, as per the AAR, the supply made by the appellant under the said contract qualifies as a composite supply in terms of sub-section (30) of section 2 and, hence, appellant would be liable to pay GST at the rate of 18 per cent on entire contract, i.e., the rate applicable to supply of UPS.

The appellant accepts the ruling given by the AAR with regard to the first question. However, it filed present appeal against the finding given by the AAR.

Facts in the case of Harekrishna Developers, In re [2008] 14 STT 175 (AAR - New Delhi) 3.2 The applicant-firm intends to develop on its own plot of land a residential complex having more than twelve residential units with a club house and other common facilities. It will sell plots of land inside the complex to prospective buyers who will enter into a works contract with the applicant for the construction of residential units. The applicant itself will execute a part of the works contract [‘activity No. 3’] and for remaining part, the applicant will further enter into a works contract with other contractors [‘activity No. 4’]. However, goods for construction will be purchased/acquired by the applicant and the property in those goods will be transferred to buyers of the housing units and such transfer would be exigible to tax as sale of goods. The applicant sought advance ruling of the Authority on questions of its liability in these two types of activities, and also on question of rate of tax in case of activity No. 3.

The applicant contends that since the works contract in activities 3 and 4 involves construction of a new building-such an activity can only be covered under(ii)( b) in the Explanation to section 65(105)(zzzza). Since the new building proposed to be constructed in the course of the execution of the works contract is a residential one, and is not for the purpose of commerce or industry, such a works contract will not fall under (b) and therefore, will not attract service tax. The applicant further states that a works contract for construction of a new building for residential purposes is also not covered under any of the remaining classifications in (ii) of the Explanation to clause (zzzza). The classification (c) which covers ‘construction of a new residential complex or a part thereof’ is not applicable in applicant’s case as the works contract is for construction of an individual residential unit and not for construction of a residential complex.

Decision in the case of Harekrishna Developers (supra )

3.3 Authority for Advance Ruling held:

1. To attract service tax under sub-clause (zzzza) of section 65(105), a works contract has to meet the two conditions: (i) and (ii) in the Explanation to sub-clause (zzzza). The facts narrated by the applicant indicated that condition (i) is met in the instant case as the transfer of property in goods involved in the execution of the works contract is exigible to tax as sale of goods under the local Sales Tax Act. To meet condition (ii), the activity involved in the works contract in activity Nos. 3 and 4 has to be covered by at least one of the classifications (a ) to (e) in the Explanation to sub-clause (zzzza). Proceeding serially, one finds that building of a residential house on a sub-plot in a residential complex is clearly not covered in (a). As pointed out by the applicant itself, it is also not covered by (b) which covers construction of a new building intended primarily for commerce and industry and does not cover construction of a new building. Item (c) of sub-clause (zzzza) of clause (105) covers ‘construction of a new residential complex or a part thereof’.

2. As per the draft of the works contract submitted, it is clear that such contracts will be for construction of individual houses on sub-plots located within the plot owned by the applicant on which the applicant proposes to develop a residential housing project. As per the applicant’s own narration, the residential project to be constructed on this plot would have at least 12 residential units, a club house and other common facilities and the layout of the project would be approved by the prescribed authority under the relevant law in force. Such a project constructed as per activity Nos. 3 and 4 squarely conforms to the definition of a ‘residential complex’ given in clause (91a) of section 65, and the individual houses constructed get covered under the definition of a ‘residential unit’ contained therein. Execution of the works contract, thus, involves construction of a part of a new ‘residential complex’ and is covered by (c).

8. Section 7 CGST defines supply in an inclusive manner meaning it is a widened and broadened connotation. Essentially, a flat under construction and intended to be sold to a buyer is sale of immovable property, but when it is undergoing construction there is an element of service and consequently, it was necessary to treat construction of flats as a supply of service vide Section 7(1)(d) read with item no 5(b) of Schedule II. 9. Schedule of Goods and Service Tax rates for services approved by GST Council laying down fitment of rates of services states at entry 19 that "Construction of a complex, civil structure or part thereof intended for sale to a buyer wholly or partly" will bear GST at 12.5% with full input tax credit, but no refund of overflow of input tax credit. The entry also explains that the value of land is included in the amount charged from the service recipient. Simultaneously, rate of GST for composite works contract as defined in Section 2(119) vide entry 27 is 18% with full input tax credit. In substance and effect, though construction of flat is treated as a service yet it is akin to a works contract. Drawing such a cue implies that concession of 6% is given to factor in value of land thereby leading to a calculation of 33% of abatement on the total consideration. However, prescription of such a standard rate of abatement [assumed] does not take into realities of cheap, medium, semi-luxury, luxurious and elite segments where composition of land value would considerably vary. Moreover, in semi-rural developing towns, presumed rate of 33% in respect of land value may be on higher side leading to excess input credit over 12% output tax inasmuch as input supplies for builders mostly carry a rate of 18% to 28% which as per schedule of rates as seen above is not refundable. In cases, where input tax credit falls short of GST rate of 12% profits of builders will truncate or lead passing of burden on to consumers. In my opinion, this matters ought to have been formulated by the legislature in a flexible manner through a methodology by way of rules to reckon local factors.

10. Another daunting controversy that may arise is whether the overflow of input tax credit is to be worked per project or on a net basis for all projects put together. Section 16 of CGST provides that every person shall subject to such terms and conditions as may be prescribed and in the manner specified in Section 49 be entitled to the credit of any input tax in respect of any supply of goods and services or both to him which are used or intended to be used in the course or furtherance of his business and the amount shall be credited to the electronic ledger of such person. In my opinion, looking at the wording of Section 16 aforesaid read with Section 17 better view appears to be that an overall picture of all projects will have to be undertaken and not project wise. No guidance is found either in the Act or the relevant rules as what are the implications of GST in a case when a project undertaken by the builder where he has to give flats to the owner of land in discharge of consideration for obtaining development rights. Assuming in a particular case, the developers have to provide 100 flats to owners and there other 200 flats for free sale; in former case he will be a contractor levying GST at 18% with input tax credit, whereas in the latter case, the rate would be 12% with full input tax credit but no refund of overflow credit in a situation where flats are sold before they are fully developed. In the aforementioned example, there can controversy as to how the overflow of input tax credit to be computed being the difference between the rate of GST on input supplies and 18% GST rate more particularly, after considering common input supplies and capital goods employed for both types of flats. Moreover, disputes will arise as to what is time of supply of the 100 units to be allotted to owners more specifically, if land is not parted physically at one go, but in stages. Can we say the supply of flats is complete when possession of land is given despite the fact that flats are yet to be constructed? If the free sale flats are sold in stages question will emanate as to whether input tax credit is to be accumulated or can be claimed while construction is progressing without any sale? It would be best to issue clarifications on these and other potential roadblocks that may lead to avoidable litigation.

1. Our company has executed works contract for Central Rail Side Warehousing Corporation Ltd. (CRWC) at Ranchi (Jharkhand). The nature of works is construction, erection and installation of PEB structures of steel and incidental works for warehouse complex. The period of contract executed is 1st April, 2007 to 31st March, 2012. The service tax department is asking for payment of service tax for the contract value of this work of say Rs. 1 crore.

We understand that Railways is exempted from service tax. The definition of railways as given in the Railways Act includes its warehouses. So, our company should not be liable to service tax on such works contract of construction, erection and installation of warehouses. Use of the warehouses is not exempted but construction of railway warehouses is exempted.

Constitution of CRWC is as follows: Indian Railways have entered into a MOU with the Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC) as its strategic partner for development of integrated railside warehouse complexes. CWC has created a SPV as its subsidiary, named as CRWC with the sole purpose of developing railside warehousing complexes (not other complexes). The Indian Railways has provided land near various railway terminals and the CRWC has constructed and erected railway warehousing complexes on the land by contracting with our company. Indian Railway will get its share of profit by way of profit sharing from CRWC.

Kindly enlighten us whether the stand of the company is correct that construction of railside warehousing by Indian Railways in partnership with CRWC should not be taxable.

Railway is defined in section 2(31) of the Railways Act, 1989; the same is reproduced below -

"railway" means a railway, or any portion of a railway, for the public carriage of passengers or goods, and includes-

"(a)

all lands within the fences or other boundary marks indicating the limits of the land appurtenant to a railway;

(b)

all lines of rails, sidings, or yards, or branches used for the purposes of, or in connection with, a railway;

(c)

all electric traction equipments, power supply and distribution installations used for the purposes of, or in connection with, a railway;

(d)

all rolling stock, stations, officers warehouses, wharves, workshops, factories, fixed plant and machinery, roads and streets, running rooms, rest houses, institutes, hospitals, water works and water supply installations, staff dwellings and any other works constructed for the purpose of, or in connection with, railway;

(e)

all vehicles which are used on any road for the purposes of traffic of a railway and owned, hired or worked by a railway; and

(f)

all ferries, ships, boats and rafts which are used on any canal, river, lake or other navigable inland waters for the purposes of the traffic of a railway and owned, hired or worked by a railway administration,

but does not include-

(i)

a tramway wholly within a municipal area; and

(ii)

lines of rails built in any exhibition ground, fair, park or any other place solely for the purpose of recreation.

The relevant taxable services, viz., Commercial construction services and works contract services exclude services/works contracts in respect of roads, airports, railways, transport terminals, bridges, tunnels and dams.

The query can be answer solely on basis of clause (d) of the definition, as it lists various places to be considered as 'railways'.

Services provided by railway include transport of passengers and goods and, constructions necessary therefor are covered by the term 'railways'. The words "officers warehouses"... "rest houses"... "any other works" … "for the purpose of railways" or "in connection with railways" are wide enough to cover warehouses meant for storage of goods transported by the railways.

If that is the case, the services will be considered as having been provided in respect of construction of warehouse for use of the railways.

However, construction of warehouses meant for commercial use by railways and not for use of railways will not be covered under 'railways' and services provided would be not considered as 'in respect of' railways.

Please note that the services must be provided "in respect of" railways and not merely "to" railways.

Hence, it appears that the services provided by your client would be liable to service tax.

Empowered Committee of State Finance Ministers had released Draft of model GST Act and IGST Act on 14-6-2016. Later draft rules relating to registration, invoice, payments, returns and refunds were released in September, 2016 by CBE&C. FAQs were also released by CBE&C in September, 2016.

On basis of various suggestions received, fresh model laws have been released by GST Council Secretariat on 26-11-2016. Following three drafts have been released—

1.

Model GST Law

2.

Model IGST Law

3.

Draft Goods and Service Tax (Compensation to the States for Loss of Revenue) Bill, 2016

Many changes have been made compared to earlier draft. It is heartening to note that many suggestions from trade and industry have been considered and suitable changes have been made.

These drafts have already been discussed at officers' level. Now, these will be placed before GST Council which is scheduled to meet on 2-12-2016. Finishing touches may be given in the meeting.

After approval of GST Council, the Bill will be presented before Parliament in week commencing on 5-12-2016.

If all goes well, the Bills may be passed in winter 2016 session of Parliament and the GST will see light of day on 1-4-2017. Of course there are many slips between cup and the lip.

Detailed write up is attached. The highlights of major changes vis-à-vis Model Laws released in June, 2016 are given below.

Ceiling on GST Rates

The new Model Law specifies ceiling on GST rates as follows - SGST - 14%, CGST - 14% and IGST - 28%.

Of course, this ceiling is illusory as section 8 of GST (Compensation to the States for Loss of Revenue) Bill, 2016 makes provision for levy and collection of GST Compensation Cess on supplies of goods and services. This cess will be non-vatable.

Thus, all what is achieved by GST can be lost through such cess. Only solace is that this cess can be levied by Central Government and not individual State Governments.

Definition of 'supply without consideration' pruned and made more practical

The earlier definition of 'supply without consideration' as contained in Schedule I was very broad. It covered transactions which were for private use. This would have created huge amount of litigation, particularly because as per provisions of input tax credit, input credit of expenses not related to business was anyway not available. Thus, this would have created double whammy.

The revised definition of 'supply without consideration' in Schedule I is as follows—

1.

Permanent transfer/disposal of business assets where input tax credit has been availed on such assets.

2.

Supply of goods or services between related persons, or between distinct persons as specified in section 10, when made in the course or furtherance of business.

3.

Supply of goods—

(a)

by a principal to his agent where the agent undertakes to supply such goods on behalf of the principal, or

(b)

by an agent to his principal where the agent undertakes to receive such goods on behalf of the principal.

4.

Importation of services by a taxable person from a related person or from any of his other establishments outside India, in the course or furtherance of business.

The transactions between agent and principal will be subject to GST on goods only when Agent receives the goods (like C&F Agency or Consignment Agent). If the Agent is commission agent and does not receive goods, he will be liable only to GST on his commission.

Definition of 'works contract' restricted to services relating to immovable property

The earlier model law was covering works contracts of 'movable property' also. Now, only works contracts relating to immovable property will alone be covered (though first part of definition of 'works contract' still contains the words 'transfer of property in goods is involved in the execution of such contract', which are likely to cause confusion and litigation).

The revised definition as per section 2(110) of new Model Law is as follows—

"works contract" means a contract wherein transfer of property in goods is involved in the execution of such contract and includes contract for building, construction, fabrication, completion, erection, installation, fitting out, improvement, modification, repair, maintenance, renovation, alteration or commissioning of any immovable property.

DELHI METRO RAIL CORPORATION IS NOT 'RAILWAYS' 2. Our company has executed works contract for the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) by way of supply and erection of PEB structures for six elevated stations of DMRC in New Delhi during 1st April, 2008 to 31st March, 2010. The value of the contract is say of Rs. 1 crore. The service tax department is asking for payment of service tax on works executed for DMRC. The company is of the view that DMRC is railways, and the works executed for railway is exempted in service tax. But the service tax department says that DMRC is not included in railways, as it is a separate corporation from the Indian Railways. We understand that the definition of 'railways' as per the Railways Act is not restricted to the Indian railways. It says "Railways means a railway or any portion of a railway, for the public carriage of passengers or goods." Thus, whether it is DMRC or Indian Railways, both are railways and works contract executed to any of them is exempted.

You may kindly enlighten us whether the stand of the company is right that the works contract of supply and erection of PEB structures for six elevated stations of DMRC is exempted.

As per section 2(31) of the Railways Act, 1989, "railway" means a railway, or any portion of a railway, for the public carriage of passengers or goods. It doesn't include a tramway wholly within a Municipal area.

The relevant taxable services, viz., commercial construction services and works contract services exclude services/works contract in respect of roads, airports, railways, transport terminals, bridges, tunnels and dams.

As per clause (20) of section 2 the aforesaid Act :

(20) "Government railway" means a railway owned by the Central Government;

As per clause (g) ibid :

(g) "railway administration", in relation to-

(a)

a Government railway, means the General Manager of a Zonal Railway; and

(b)

a non-Government railway person means the person who is the owner or lessee of the railway or the person working for the railway under an agreement;

As per the meaning given to it "railway" means a railway, or any portion of a railway, for the public carriage of passengers or goods. Thus, railways may be Government owned or private owned. Even private-owned railways is railways within the meaning of the Act. However, a 'tramway' is excluded.

Further, present section 66D(o) provides that service of transportation of passengers, with or without accompanied belongings, by-

(i)

a stage carriage;

(ii)

railways in a class other than-

(A)

first class; or

(B)

an air-conditioned coach;

(iii)

metro, monorail or tramway;...

shall be in the negative list.

Thus, the present law conceives of 'railways' differently from 'metro or monorail or tramway'.

As per Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, a tram-train is a light-rail public transport system where trams run through from an urban tramway network to main-line railway lines which are shared with conventional trains. This combines the tram's flexibility and accessibility with a train's greater speed, and bridges the distance between a main railway station and a city centre. There is also a train-tram, which is a train modified to run also on tramlines. Generally, the tram-train and train-tram are interchangeable, although a train-tram is based on a train design modified to also run as a tram and a tram-train is based on a tram design modified also to run on a train line.

Hence, it appears that Delhi Metro is a 'tramway' and not a 'railway'. The services may not be eligible for exemption.

[A useful reference may also be made to : http://www.hindustantimes.com/India-news/Mumbai/Mumbai-Metro-Is-it-a-tramway-or-a-railway/Article1-763834.aspx]

However, in Bangalore Metro Rail Corpn. Ltd. v. Ministry of Finance [2013] 39 STT 107/31 taxmann.com 381 (Kar.), the Court has ruled that services provided in relation to execution of works contract for Metro Rail Corporation would not be liable to service tax, in view of provisions of section 65(105)(zzzza), excluding services provided in relation to railways.

Illustration 2 - M/s. XYZ Ltd. are engaged in carrying out works contract liable to VAT under the State-VAT laws. They had started a works contract on 1-6-2012 and had opted for composition scheme for payment of VAT and service tax both. On 1-7-2012, since the composition scheme stands withdrawn, their works contract (not being original works) falls under rule 2A(ii)(C) of the Service Tax (Determination of Value) Rules, 2006 (value cannot be determined on actual basis under Rule 2A(i) ibid). How should they determine their liability to pay service tax in respect of the said works contract in the following situations -

(i) service provided, bills raised and amounts received prior to 1-7-2012 ;

(ii) service provided and bill raised prior to 1-7-2012, but, amounts received on or after 1-7-2012 ;

(iii) service provided prior to 1-7-2012, but bill raised and amount received on or after 1-7-2012 ;

(iv) service provided, bill raised and amounts received on or after 1-7-2012.

Solution - Works Contract Service is notified as continuous supply of service for which Point of Taxation is determinable under rule 3 of the Point of Taxation Rules, 2011. However, in case of change in effective rate of tax, rule 4 ibid shall apply, as rule 4 ibid has overriding effect.

POT - CONSTRUCTION SERVICES - REVISION IN ABATEMENT - APPLICABILITY OF RULE 4

7. We are builders and are engaged in providing construction services falling under Section 66E(b) of the Finance Act, 1994. We were constructing a new commercial complex with 20 identical units priced at Rs. 90 lakh each since 1-3-2013. A payment of Rs. 50 lakhs on each unit had already been received up to 7-5-2013 and corresponding bills had also been raised and construction was done accordingly. A part of the construction would be carried out on or after 8-5-2013 and bills would be raised accordingly. We have opted for abatement under Notification No. 26/2012-ST. What will be the service tax implication in this case ?

Construction services provided in respect of non-residential construction priced below Rs. 100 lakhs was eligible for abatement at 75% up to 7-5-2013.

However, w.e.f. 8-5-2013, the rate of abatement has been reduced to 70%. This would amount to change in the rate of service tax and Rule 4 of the Point of Taxation Rules, 2011 would apply accordingly (Rule 4 has an overriding effect over Rule 3 of the Point of Taxation Rules, 2011, i.e., Rule 4 applies even if the service amounts to a continuous supply of services.)

Under Rule 4, to the extent invoice has been issued and payment received prior to change in rate of tax, the rate of service tax would continue to be old one, i.e., 75% abatement would be available. However, in respect of bills raised and collections made, taking place on or after 8-5-2013, the rate of abatement would be at 70%.

In certain cases, where the service has been provided prior to 8-5-2013 and bills have been raised before 8-5-2013, but payment only has been received on or after 8-5-2013, the rate of abatement would continue to be 75%.

In one case, said Services forming part of negative list were provided on 1-5-2013 (Value Rs. 25,000) Invoice therefor was issued on 9-5-2013 and payment thereof was received by way of account-payee draft on 9-5-2013 itself. The said draft was presented to the bank on 14-5-2013 and credited to bank account on 16-5-2013. Would the services be liable to service tax ?

In this case, since payment is received by a banking instrument, Rule 2A would be applicable. Since payment is credited in the bank on 16-5-2013 (after 4 working days from 10-5-2013, being date of charge of service tax on such services for the first time), hence, date of payment = date on which payment was credited to bank = 16-5-2013.

Rule 5(a) and 5(b) of the Point of Taxation Rules, 2011 requires that payment must have been received prior to charge of service tax for the first time, which is not the case herein.

23.1-1 Statutory provisions in respect of construction of complex

Following is 'supply of service' as per para 5(b) of Schedule II of CGST Act.

Construction of a complex, building, civil structure or a part thereof, including a complex or building intended for sale to a buyer, wholly or partly, except where the entire consideration has been received after issuance of completion certificate, where required, by the competent authority or after its first occupation, whichever is earlier.

Explanation.- For the purposes of this clause- (1) the expression "competent authority" means the Government or any authority authorized to issue completion certificate under any law for the time being in force and in case of non-requirement of such certificate from such authority, from any of the following, namely - (i) an architect registered with the Council of Architecture constituted under the Architects Act, 1972; or (ii) a chartered engineer registered with the Institution of Engineers (India); or (iii) a licensed surveyor of the respective local body of the city or town or village or development or planning authority.

(2) the expression "construction" includes additions, alterations, replacements or remodeling of any existing civil structure.

Residential Complex - "Residential complex" means any complex comprising of a building or buildings, having more than one single residential unit - para 2 of Notification No. 12/2017-CT (Rate) and No. 9/2017-IT (Rate) both dated 28-6-2017, effective from 1-7-2017.

Single Residential Unit - "Single residential unit" means a self-contained residential unit which is designed for use, wholly or principally, for residential purposes for one family - para 2 of Notification No. 12/2017-CT (Rate) and No. 9/2017-IT (Rate) both dated 28-6-2017, effective from 1-7-2017.

Occupancy certificate granted in is equal to completion certificate - In Mumbai i.e. Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), occupancy certificate is granted. Sale after such occupancy certificate (even before completion certificate) will be sale of immovable property and outside service tax net - PIB (Press Information Bureau), Ministry of Finance dated 26-10-2015.

Same view has been held in Bindu Ventures, In re [2018] 100 taxmann.com 207 (AAR - Karnataka) in respect of occupancy certificate issued by Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike.

23.1-2 Meaning of 'first occupation'

As per para 5 of Schedule III read with para 5(b) of Schedule II of CGST Act, If entire consideration is received 'after issuance of completion certificate/occupancy certificate by the competent authority or its first occupation whichever is earlier', the promoter (builder or developer) is not liable to pay GST, even if completion certificate or occupancy certificate is not obtained from authorities.

Further, relevant rule 3(1) of such composition scheme rules provides for such incidence of tax at 2 per cent on the basis of service provided or to be provided, meaning thereby that any such service provided prior to June 1, 2007 shall not qualify under the scheme. Rule 3(1) reads as follows :

Service tax on works contract

SUDHIR HALAKHANDI*

The Finance Minister with a sole motto, ‘when transfer of property involved in works contract is taxable, then why the transfer of services involved in works contract is not taxable’ proposed one more complicated levy of service tax on works contract vide the Finance Bill, 2007. Now the contractors involved in works contract will have to pay service tax on transfer of services. This write-up highlights the types of contract where the levy is attracted, where the levy is not attracted and the composition scheme while making reference to departmental clarification in this regard. The rules of valuation and the composition scheme will be declared later though anticipating the requirement of opting for composition scheme, the law-makers have already disclosed the rate of composition as 2 per cent on the whole amount of contract.

Introduction

1. Transfer of property in goods involved in works contract is taxable under the State tax i.e. VAT or sales tax. This levy under the State sales tax laws was a very complicated levy and the complications further increased on the introduction of VAT. Most of the contractors have opted for composition schemes introduced by the State Governments. The service tax was introduced in 1994 with a sole motto ‘When goods are taxable why not services’. On the same ground the Finance Minister seems to have a thought that ‘When transfer of property involved in works contract is taxable, then why the transfer of services involved in works contract is not taxable’ and, hence, he proposed one more complicated levy of service tax on works contract. Now the contractors involved in execution of works contract will have to pay service tax on transfer of services also. The rules of valuation and the composition scheme in this regard will be declared later though, anticipating the requirement of opting for composition scheme, the law makers have already disclosed the rate of composition as 2 per cent on the whole amount of contract.

Finance Minister’s speech

2. The relevant portion of the Finance Minister’s Speech is as under :

"154. State Governments levy a tax on the transfer of property in goods involved in the execution of a works contract. The value of services in a works contract should attract service tax. Hence, I propose to levy of service tax on services involved in the execution of a works contract. However, I also propose an optional composition scheme under which service tax will be levied at only 2 per cent of the total value of the works contract."

Service tax on works contract

3. The levy of service tax and its taxability is defined and explained in section 65(105)(zzzza ), which is proposed to be added to the Finance Act, 1994 by the Finance Bill, 2007.

This section reads as under :

"Taxable service means a service provided or to be provided :

to any person, by any other person in relation to the execution of a works contract, excluding works contract in respect of roads, airports, railways, transport terminals, bridges, tunnels and dams.

Explanation.—For the purposes of this sub-clause, ‘works contract’ means a contract wherein,—

(i )Transfer of property in goods involved in the execution of such contract is leviable to tax as sale of goods, and

(ii )Such contract is for the purposes of carrying out,—

( a)Erection, commissioning or installation of plant, machinery, equipment or structures, whether pre-fabricated or otherwise, installation of electrical and electronic devices, plumbing, drain laying or other installations for transport of fluids, heating, ventilation or air-conditioning including related pipe work, duct work and sheet metal work, thermal insulation, sound insulation, fire proofing or water proofing, lift and escalator, fire escape staircases or elevators; or

( b)Construction of a new building or a civil structure or a part thereof, or of a pipeline or conduit, primarily for the purposes of commerce or industry; or

( c)Construction of a new residential complex or a part thereof; or

( d)Completion and finishing services, repair, alteration, renovation or restoration of, or similar services, in relation to (b) and (c); or

( e)Turnkey projects including Engineering Procurement and Construction or Commissioning (EPC) projects;,

Exclusions

4. The levy of this tax is not applicable to the following infrastructure related works contract :

uRoads.

uAirports.

uRailways.

uTransport terminals.

uBridges.

uTunnels.

uDams.

Levy is only on certain type of contracts

5. The tax is proposed only with respect to the following contracts :

(i)Works contract for carrying out erection, commissioning or installation.

(ii)Works contract for commercial or industrial construction.

(iii)Works contract for construction of complex.
